Proposed Revisions to the DesertLink, LLC Transmission Owner Tariff to Provide for Large Load Interconnection and Cost Recovery

Dear Secretary Reese:
Pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Part 35 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC” or “Commission”) regulations,2 and in response to the Commission’s order instituting the show cause proceeding in California Independent System Operator Corp.,3 DesertLink, LLC (“DesertLink”) submits revisions to its Transmission Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”) to establish a framework for the interconnection of Large Loads4 and for the recovery of the costs of transmission upgrades driven by Large Loads. The revisions include (1) adding a new Section 10A and a new Appendix VI (Large Load Interconnection Procedures (“LLIP”)) to establish an interconnection process for Eligible Customers for Large Load (“ECLLs”);

(2) corresponding revisions to the TO Tariff; and (3) adding a new Appendix V, the pro forma Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement (“CRA”). DesertLink respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed tariff revisions to become effective January 16, 2027, sixty-one

(61) days after filing, consistent with the Commission’s prior notice requirement,5 and grant any necessary waivers.

I. INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY OF FILING
The proposed revisions establish a transparent framework for DesertLink, a transmission-only, non-load-serving Participating Transmission Owner (“PTO”) in the California Independent System Operator Corporation (“CAISO”), to interconnect Large Loads and to recover the costs of transmission upgrades that are driven, in whole or in part, by a Large Load (“Large Load-Driven Upgrades”). New Section 10A and the LLIP in Appendix VI govern ECLL applications, studies, interim service, and interconnection agreements. The pro forma CRA in Appendix V establishes the Eligible Customer’s twenty-year Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“MTRC”) and related payment and security obligations for each Covered Upgrade. Amounts received under a CRA are credited to transmission customers through DesertLink’s existing Transmission Revenue Balancing Account Adjustment (“TRBAA”), and the Formula Rate Template is revised to identify Covered Upgrade plant and to ensure that those credits are not counted twice. The filing responds to the Show Cause Order’s direction that respondents (1) ensure transparency concerning the network upgrade costs to provide transmission service to Eligible Customers on behalf of large loads, (2) establish a pro forma cost recovery agreement to mitigate the risk of cost shifting among transmission customers, and (3) ensure that such payments are appropriately credited toward transmission owners’ transmission revenue requirements.6 The CRA assigns the wholesale revenue-support obligation to the Eligible Customer that takes transmission service on behalf of the Large Load Facility and backs that obligation with Construction Security, Operational Security, and a Termination Fee. The framework is designed to mitigate the risk that other customers bear the costs of a Covered Upgrade if the associated Large Load is delayed, reduced, or does not materialize, while preserving DesertLink’s recovery of its revenue requirement through its Formula Rate and the CAISO Transmission Access Charge (“TAC”), and without changing CAISO cost allocation.

The proposed revisions do not change the cost-of-service inputs, return, depreciation, taxes, or allocators used to calculate DesertLink’s revenue requirement. Absent any Covered Upgrade or CRA, the revised Formula Rate Template produces the same revenue requirement as the currently effective Formula Rate Template, and no changes are proposed to DesertLink’s Formula Rate Implementation Protocols (Appendix IV) or to Appendix I of the TO Tariff. Once these revisions are accepted, a conforming, executed CRA with populated Schedules generally will not require an individual FPA section 205 filing, while unexecuted agreements, agreements containing a material deviation, and other agreements required by Commission rule or order will be filed with the Commission.7

II. BACKGROUND
A. DesertLink and Its Formula Rate
DesertLink is a transmission-only PTO in the CAISO that owns the Harry Allen to Eldorado 500 kV Transmission Line Project (“Harry Allen to Eldorado Project”), which CAISO selected DesertLink to develop in 2016 through its Order No. 1000-compliant competitive solicitation process and which DesertLink placed in service in August 2020. DesertLink is a non-load-serving PTO; it neither serves retail load nor has a retail relationship with any customer seeking a Large Load interconnection. DesertLink’s formula rate consists of its Formula Rate Template (Appendix III of the TO Tariff) and its Formula Rate Implementation Protocols (“Protocols”) (Appendix IV of the TO Tariff) (together, the “Formula Rate”), which were originally accepted in Docket No. ER17- 135-000 and most recently revised in Docket No. ER26-3479-000. DesertLink’s Transmission Revenue Requirement (“TRR”) is the sum of its Base Transmission Revenue Requirement (“Base TRR”), determined under the Formula Rate, and its TRBAA, and is recovered through the CAISO TAC. DesertLink already uses the TRBAA to credit customers with revenue it receives outside the TAC.

B. Show Cause Order and Stakeholder Process
On June 18, 2026, the Commission issued the Show Cause Order, instituting an FPA section 206 proceeding in Docket No. EL26-71-000 directed to CAISO and its PTOs. The Commission preliminarily found that existing tariffs appear to be unjust, unreasonable, or unduly discriminatory or preferential because they lack sufficiently clear and consistent provisions to address the challenges posed by the rapid growth of large loads and co-location arrangements between loads and generating facilities.8 The Commission directed each respondent either to show cause why its tariff remains just and reasonable or to explain what tariff changes would remedy the identified concerns.9

Following the Show Cause Order, CAISO convened joint coordination meetings with the PTOs to address the Show Cause Order and CAISO’s proposed implementation framework, and DesertLink participated in those meetings from July through October 2026. DesertLink also participated in CAISO’s public stakeholder meetings and submitted written comments on CAISO’s Straw Proposal, Draft Final Proposal, and Draft Tariff Language asking CAISO to recognize non- load-serving and affected PTOs expressly and to preserve a meaningful role for those PTOs in the interconnection and study process. DesertLink further participated in discussions with other non- load-serving PTOs, the broader PTO group, and load-serving PTOs addressing the application and study process, information sharing, technical coordination, and the allocation and recovery of costs.10 Those discussions highlighted the need to ensure that an affected PTO has a meaningful

III. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED REVISIONS
A. Large Load Interconnection Framework (Section 10A and Appendix VI)
A new Section 10A of the TO Tariﬀ establishes an interconnection process for ECLL Interconnections. An ECLL is a Utility Distribution Company or Metered Subsystem that provides retail transmission and interconnection service to Large Load End-Users in the CAISO Balancing Authority Area, and a Large Load is an End-User located at a single site behind one or more Points of Withdrawal from the CAISO Controlled Grid with a peak load of 50 MW or greater. Section 10A.2 speciﬁes the contents of an ECLL Interconnection Application, including the load ramp schedule, site plan, Site Control, permits and approvals, electrical conﬁguration, related requests, technical data, and Co-Located Large Load information. Section 10A.3 directs that ECLL Interconnection Applications be processed, and ECLL Interconnection Agreements be tendered, executed, and ﬁled, under the LLIP in Appendix VI. Section 10A.4 provides for Interim Firm Interconnection Service and Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (“FILI”) Service before the required facilities are completed. FILI Service is subject to curtailment, including during normal operating conditions, and is curtailed before Firm Interconnection Service. If FILI Service is elected, the Large Load Interconnection Customer must ensure that, before the Service Commencement Date, the Large Load Customer executes, or requests the ﬁling of an unexecuted, FILI Service Agreement with DesertLink and, as applicable, CAISO. That agreement identiﬁes the curtailment conditions and the mechanism for implementing curtailment. Section 10A.5 addresses Co-Located Large Loads.12

The LLIP applies to new Large Loads, capacity increases to Large Loads previously processed under the LLIP, and increases of 50 MW or greater to existing loads not previously processed under the LLIP, for completed Interconnection Requests submitted after Appendix VI becomes effective. It provides for a scoping meeting, a Large Load Study Process Agreement, and a Large Load Interconnection Study subject to CAISO review and concurrence, with a ninety-Calendar- Day reasonable-efforts study period. The study must consider alternative transmission technologies, including dynamic line ratings, advanced power flow control devices, advanced conductors, and transmission switching, and, if traditional network upgrades are selected, the PTO must demonstrate why alternative transmission technologies are not feasible or would not result in lower costs or a faster timeline.13 The LLIP also establishes financial readiness

Section 10.1 directs ECLL requests to Section 10A, and revised Section 10.9 provides that, where a TSWL Interconnection will serve one or more Large Loads, the Eligible Customer taking or requesting transmission service on behalf of the Large Load must execute and maintain a CRA, or request that it be ﬁled unexecuted, as a condition to DesertLink’s design, procurement, construction, or operation of any associated Large Load-Driven Upgrades. Section 3 adds deﬁnitions for, among other terms, Co-Located Large Load, Cost Recovery Agreement, ECLL, ECLL Interconnection, Firm Interconnection Service, FILI Service, Interim Firm Interconnection Service, Large Load, Point of Withdrawal, Site Control, and TSWL Interconnection, and renumbers the existing deﬁnitions.

B. Pro Forma CRA (Appendix V)
The pro forma CRA is a contract between DesertLink, as Transmission Owner, and the Eligible Customer taking wholesale transmission service under the CAISO Tariﬀ on behalf of a Large Load Customer. Assigning the payment obligation to that Eligible Customer preserves the wholesale obligor structure and does not establish a FERC-jurisdictional retail rate or payment obligation for the Large Load Customer. The Large Load Customer executes a Limited Acknowledgment for information, authorization, notice, and cooperation purposes, but is not a party to the wholesale payment obligations. CAISO is not a party to the CRA, and the CRA creates no obligation of CAISO. Covered Upgrades include Large Load-Driven Upgrades and any DesertLink-owned share of a CAISO-Assigned Regional Project identiﬁed in the applicable Schedules for which an Annual MTRC is established; Aﬀected System Upgrades and regional project shares owned by another entity are addressed through separate arrangements. Where DesertLink requires a CRA, Section 10.9 (for a TSWL Interconnection) and LLIP Section 5.3, incorporated through Section 10A.6 (for an ECLL Interconnection), require the applicable Eligible Customer to execute it, or to request that it be ﬁled unexecuted, within the applicable interconnection-agreement execution period.15 For each Covered Upgrade, the CRA establishes an Annual MTRC calculated solely under the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5, separately from the Formula Rate. The Estimated Annual MTRC uses then-current estimated capital cost. Within one year after the Covered Upgrade enters service, when actual capital cost is known, DesertLink establishes the Final Annual MTRC as the final incurred capital cost multiplied by the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate calculated under Schedule 5 using the applicable capital structure, cost of debt, return on equity, income-tax inputs, a fixed five percent (5%) annual levelized-depreciation

The MTRC Term begins on the applicable in-service date and ends on the day immediately preceding its twentieth anniversary, with partial Rate Years prorated. The Final Annual MTRC is not recalculated through the Formula Rate and may change only as permitted by Section 6.3.1, including to correct errors or fraud, to implement an effective prospective reassignment or a final Commission order, or to reflect prospectively a Commission-approved change in DesertLink’s return on equity or subsequently enacted tax rates or tax law.16

The twenty-year MTRC Term is a deﬁned contractual revenue-support period, not the depreciable life of a Covered Upgrade. Each Covered Upgrade placed under CAISO’s Operational Control remains in DesertLink’s rate base and Base TRR and is subject to ordinary Formula Rate treatment. Where an upgrade is driven by more than one Large Load, Schedule 1 identiﬁes an Initial Allocation Percentage for each Large Load Customer using the applicable ﬁnal study and allocation methodology, accounting for loads studied individually, jointly, or in a cluster and for any portion of the facility that serves other transmission system needs or customers. The aggregate Annual MTRC allocated to all Large Load Customers may not exceed one hundred percent (100%) of the Annual MTRC for that Covered Upgrade; any unallocated portion remains subject to otherwise applicable CAISO cost-allocation and rate-recovery requirements. Each allocation percentage is applied only once in calculating the Annual MTRC.17 The Eligible Customer pays a Supplemental MTRC equal to the greater of zero and the applicable Annual MTRC less Qualifying Transmission Revenues (“QTR”). QTR consists of wholesale transmission revenues attributable to service to the Large Load Facility that reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. As applicable, QTR includes the portion of TAC revenues attributable to the Large Load Facility and allocable to DesertLink under the reproducible methodology in Schedule 2, qualifying Wheeling Access Charges, and other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission-service charges, including charges paid through a non-PTO serving entity, without duplicate recognition. The Annual MTRC therefore operates as a revenue ﬂoor, not an additive charge or separate capacity-reservation commitment. DesertLink invoices the forecast Supplemental MTRC, including any prior-period true-up adjustment, in monthly installments following each Annual Projection, and serves a Reconciliation Statement with each Annual Update using actual QTR. Under-billed or over-billed amounts are carried into billing following the next Annual Projection, without interest between DesertLink and the Eligible Customer.18 Section 6.7 of the CRA establishes for each Covered Upgrade a Total Required Revenue Commitment equal to the Final Annual MTRC multiplied by twenty, which is reduced by QTR, Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds, and other permitted amounts, without

Cancellation, downsizing, curtailment, or cessation after an applicable in-service date does not itself eliminate the Eligible Customer’s obligations. Upon effective termination of the CRA or permanent cessation of service after that date, the Eligible Customer owes a lump-sum Termination Fee equal to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, less any Supplemental MTRC billed and unpaid as of the effective termination or cessation date, which remains separately payable and secured. The Termination Fee is an accelerated contractual termination charge, not a penalty. DesertLink holds each Termination Fee in a separately identified, interest-bearing Termination Fee Account and credits it to transmission customers through the TRBAA as Annual Termination Fee Credits equal to the Annual MTRC for each remaining Rate Year of the MTRC Term. The uncredited balance is accounted for as a deferred liability and is not included in rate base.19

Article 7 of the CRA requires Construction Security for incurred and irrevocably committed costs and Pre-In-Service Termination Costs, including applicable cancellation, demobilization, and restoration costs and properly accrued allowance for funds used during construction. Operational Security must be delivered no later than thirty Calendar Days before the earliest expected in- service date and equals one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. Consistent with the Commission’s decision to reduce unnecessary redundancy by allowing an Eligible Customer to rely on credit support posted by a large load under a retail agreement, direct Operational Security is reduced dollar-for-dollar by Qualifying Retail Security Support identiﬁed in a currently eﬀective Retail Security Certiﬁcation. That reduction does not reduce the underlying wholesale obligation and does not apply to Construction Security or Pre-In-Service Termination Costs. Security does not cap the Eligible Customer’s liability. Construction Security provided under an interconnection or engineering and procurement agreement for the same costs counts toward, and is not duplicated by, the CRA requirement. A Commercial Readiness Deposit may be credited dollar-for-dollar toward required CRA Construction Security only if it is in a form permitted under Schedule 3 and DesertLink elects that treatment in writing; no amount may be applied or credited more than once.20 This ﬁling adopts the conservative requirement that direct Operational Security equal one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, subject only to Qualifying Retail Security Support. DesertLink expects to work with CAISO and interested stakeholders to evaluate whether, and under what objectively deﬁned circumstances, a lower requirement or another credit-support structure could provide comparable protection against cost shifting. Any future change would be submitted to the Commission for review under FPA section 205.

C. Crediting CRA Amounts Through the TRBAA (Sections 3 and 5.5)
CRA amounts are credited to transmission customers through DesertLink’s existing TRBAA, not as Formula Rate revenue credits. Because the TO Tariﬀ deﬁnes Transmission Revenue Credits as amounts received from, or charges imposed by, CAISO, DesertLink proposes to revise the deﬁnition of the TRBAA (Section 3.103) and Section 5.5 so that the TRBAA also ﬂows through to transmission customers all amounts that a CRA requires to be credited through it. The revisions clarify that Section 5.5 does not require the payment of interest between DesertLink and a party to a CRA, which is governed solely by the CRA, and the deﬁnition of Interest (Section 3.60) is revised to the same eﬀect. The deﬁnition of Transmission Revenue Credits is unchanged.21 Each October, DesertLink will include a Forecast TRBAA Credit equal to the projected Supplemental MTRC for the following year, increased or reduced by any prior-period true-up adjustment, plus any Annual Termination Fee Credit scheduled for that year. The Forecast TRBAA Credit lowers the TRR eﬀective January 1 and, through the TAC, the transmission charges paid by all customers, while the Eligible Customer pays the Supplemental MTRC directly to DesertLink. Supplemental MTRC cash receipts, Applied Security Proceeds applied to Supplemental MTRC obligations, Annual Termination Fee Credits, and any duplicate-recovery credits are recorded in the TRBA. A billed but unpaid Supplemental MTRC is not a TRBAA Credit. If DesertLink later receives payment or applies Security proceeds to that obligation, the amount is recorded only in the Rate Year in which it is received or applied. Any diﬀerence between the Forecast TRBAA Credit and the actual amounts recorded in the TRBA is reﬂected in the TRBA principal balance and ﬂowed through in a subsequent TRBAA. QTR is not credited again, and posting, drawing, or holding Security does not itself produce a credit. The Eligible Customer remains liable for unpaid Large Load Charges, and the CRA’s Security and collection provisions mitigate, but do not eliminate, nonpayment risk. Because the TRBA ensures that DesertLink collects no more and no less than its Base TRR, DesertLink retains none of the TRBAA Credits.22

DesertLink’s annual TRBAA ﬁling is made under FPA section 205 and is noticed by the Commission, open to intervention, comment, and protest, and subject to Commission review and acceptance. DesertLink will include in each ﬁling the calculations, workpapers, and testimony supporting the TRBAA Credits, substantially in the form of Exhibit No. DLK-205, with customer-speciﬁc information presented on an aggregated basis or submitted with a request for privileged treatment under 18 C.F.R. § 388.112. No change to Appendix I is required because TRBAA Credits are included in the TRBAA amount stated in Appendix I each year.23

Balances in the TRBA attributable to CRA amounts accrue interest in the same manner as other TRBA balances, because a balance created by a late payment, a non-payment before Security is applied, or the timing of monthly installments reﬂects an actual over- or under-recovery by

D. Formula Rate Template Revisions and Rate Treatment of Covered Upgrades
DesertLink’s current Formula Rate Template reports plant values only in total and has no means of identifying facilities built to serve Large Loads. The revised Template adds Attachment 1a – Project Plant Detail, which reports gross plant, accumulated depreciation, Construction Work in Progress, unamortized abandoned plant, and net plant separately for the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project and each Covered Upgrade, with totals that tie to Attachment 4 and Appendix III so that total plant and the total revenue requirement are unchanged. Attachment 1 – Project Revenue Requirement Worksheet draws each project’s plant and depreciation from Attachment 1a, with allocation factors unchanged. New Line 17a on Attachment 12 – Revenue Credit Detail removes any TRBAA Credits recorded in revenue accounts, so those amounts are credited to customers once, through the TRBAA, and not also through the Formula Rate. Attachment 1a is also added to the Table of Contents; there are no other changes to the Template. No changes to the Protocols are required because the existing posting, review, challenge, and true-up procedures apply to the new detail.25

Covered Upgrades placed under CAISO’s Operational Control are included in DesertLink’s rate base and Base TRR in the same manner as other DesertLink transmission plant and are subject to the return components reﬂected in DesertLink’s eﬀective Formula Rate, including any generally applicable Commission-approved return incentive. Covered Upgrades do not receive return-on- equity incentives speciﬁc to the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project and are not subject to that project’s Competitive Bid Concession, Binding Cost Cap, or other project-speciﬁc cost- containment commitments. Covered Upgrade costs will be separately identiﬁed on Attachment 1a and reported as “other costs” in the commitment work paper provided under Attachment A to the Protocols. DesertLink is not requesting a diﬀerent return on equity or any new incentive in this proceeding.26

IV. THE PROPOSED REVISIONS ARE JUST AND REASONABLE
DesertLink’s approach materially mitigates the cost-shifting concern identified in the Show Cause Order. Before in-service, LLIP deposits, Construction Security, and the Pre-In-Service Termination Cost provisions protect against cancellation and related exposure. After an upgrade enters service, the Annual MTRC, Supplemental MTRC, Total Required Revenue Commitment, Required Operational Security, and Termination Fee establish and secure a defined twenty-year revenue responsibility tied to the allocated capital cost of the identified Covered Upgrades. That design responds to the concern that bilateral revenue contributions “untethered from any assessment of the actual cost of providing transmission service induced by individual large loads” may be insufficient to protect other customers against unjustified cost shifts.27

The proposal also supplies the transparency and crediting mechanisms the Commission identiﬁed. The CRA Schedules, Annual Projection workpapers, Reconciliation Statements, and Cumulative Revenue Ledger make the upgrade-speciﬁc calculations available to the Eligible Customer, which has information rights under CRA Section 6.12 and dispute rights under Article

11. Attachment 1a separately identiﬁes Covered Upgrade plant, and each annual TRBAA ﬁling is an FPA section 205 proceeding in which interested parties may review and challenge the TRBAA Credits. The LLIP further provides for study reports, a Report Meeting addressing study results and assigned cost responsibility, and CAISO posting of FILI Service Agreements. Customer-speciﬁc information is protected under Section 16.3 of the TO Tariﬀ, the CAISO Tariﬀ, and, in TRBAA ﬁlings, 18 C.F.R. § 388.112.

Crediting CRA amounts through the TRBAA ensures that Large Load payments are credited toward DesertLink’s TRR. The full cost of each Covered Upgrade remains in the Base TRR,

The TRBA ensures that DesertLink collects no more and no less than its Base TRR, and Attachment 12, Line 17a ensures that each dollar is credited only once. The CRA does not alter CAISO cost allocation or the retail arrangements between an Eligible Customer and a Large Load Customer.

Finally, the proposal is appropriately tailored to DesertLink as a non-load-serving PTO. It gives DesertLink a meaningful interconnection and cost-recovery role when a Large Load affects its facilities, even though DesertLink has no retail relationship with the load, and requires evaluation of alternative transmission technologies before traditional network upgrades are selected, consistent with the Commission’s focus on keeping costs at a responsible and accountable level. It does not disturb the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project, DesertLink’s existing revenue requirement, CAISO cost allocation, or CAISO’s study and planning authority.

V. REQUESTED EFFECTIVE DATE AND WAIVERS
DesertLink requests an effective date of January 16, 2027, sixty-one (61) days after the date of this filing, satisfying the Commission’s sixty-day notice requirement.28 DesertLink requests waiver of the cost-of-service-statement requirements of 18 C.F.R. § 35.13, and any other Part 35 requirements that otherwise may apply, to the extent necessary. The requested waivers are appropriate because the filing establishes a prospective interconnection and contractual framework, does not change the cost-of-service inputs or methods of DesertLink’s Formula Rate, and, absent any Covered Upgrade or CRA, produces the same revenue requirement as the currently effective Formula Rate Template.

3. TO Definitions. Certain capitalized terms used in this TO Tariff shall have the meanings set out below unless otherwise stated or the context otherwise requires. Capitalized terms used in this TO Tariff and not defined below shall have the meanings set out in the ISO Tariff as it may be amended from time to time.

3.1.
Access Charge. A charge paid by all UDCs, MSSs, and, in certain cases, Scheduling Coordinators delivering Energy to Gross Load, as set forth in Section 26.1 of the ISO Tariff. The Access Charge includes the High Voltage Access Charge and the Low Voltage Access Charge, as applicable.

3.2.
AGC. Generation equipment that automatically responds to signals from the ISO’s EMS control in real time to control the power output of electric generators within a prescribed area in response to a change in system frequency, tie-line loading, or the relation of these to each other, so as to maintain the target system frequency and/or the established interchange with other areas within the predetermined limits.

3.3.
Ancillary Services. Regulation, Spinning Reserve, Non-Spinning Reserve, Voltage Support and Black Start together with such other interconnected operation services as the ISO may develop in cooperation with Market Participants to support the transmission of Energy from generation resources to Loads while maintaining reliable operation of the ISO Controlled Grid in accordance with Good Utility Practice.

3.4.
Applicable Reliability Criteria. The Reliability Standards and reliability criteria established by NERC and WECC, and Local Reliability Criteria, as amended from time to time, including any requirement of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

3.5.
Available Transfer Capacity. The available capacity of a given transmission path, in MW after allocation of rights associated with Existing Contracts and Transmission Ownership Rights, to that path’s Operating Transfer Capability established consistent with ISO and WECC transmission capacity rating guidelines, as further described in Appendix L to the ISO Tariff.

3.6.
Base Transmission Revenue Requirement. The Transmission Revenue Requirement which does not reflect amounts for the TRBAA.

3.7.
Black Start. The procedure by which a Generating Unit self-starts without an external source of electricity, thereby restoring power to the ISO Controlled Grid following system or local area blackouts.

3.8.
Business Day. Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays and the day after Thanksgiving Day.

3.9.
Co-Located Large Load. A Large Load that is physically connected to the facilities of an existing or planned Generating Facility on the Interconnection Customer’s side of the Point of Interconnection to the ISO Controlled Grid (each as defined in the ISO Tariff).

PDF page 20

3.10. Completed Application Date. The date on which a party submits an Interconnection Application that satisfies the requirements of a Completed TSWL or ECLL Interconnection Application.

3.11. Completed ECLL Interconnection Application. An ECLL Interconnection Application that has been deemed valid under Section 4.3 of Appendix VI.

3.12. Completed TSWL Interconnection Application. A TSWL Interconnection Application that satisfies all of the information and other requirements of this TO Tariff and, if applicable, the information requirements as specified by the ISO and posted on the ISO Home Page.

3.13. Congestion. A characteristic of the transmission system produced by a binding Constraint to the optimum economic dispatch to meet Demand such that the LMP, exclusive of Marginal Cost of Losses, at different Locations of the transmission system is not equal.

3.14. Congestion Management. The alleviation of Congestion in accordance with applicable ISO Protocols and Good Utility Practice.

3.15. Converted Rights. Those transmission service rights determined in accordance with Section 4.3.1.6 of the ISO Tariff.

3.16. Cost Recovery Agreement. An agreement between the Participating TO and an Eligible Customer, including an ECLL, substantially in the form of the pro forma Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement set forth in Appendix V, entered into pursuant to Section 10.9 or Section 10A.6 of this TO Tariff.

3.17. CPUC. The California Public Utilities Commission or its successor.

3.18. Demand. The rates at which Energy is delivered to Load and Scheduling Points by Generation, transmission or distribution facilities. It is the product of voltage and the in- phase component of alternating current measured in units of watts or standard multiples therefore, e.g. 1000 W = 1 kW, 1000 kW= 1 MW, etc.

3.19. DesertLink, LLC (“DesertLink”). The Delaware limited liability company that is the Participating TO under this TO Tariff.

3.20. Direct Assignment Facilities. Facilities or portions of facilities that are owned by the Participating TO necessary to physically and electrically interconnect a particular party requesting a TSWL Interconnection under this TO Tariff to the ISO Controlled Grid at the point of interconnection. Direct Assignment Facilities shall be specified in the Interconnection Agreement that governs TSWL Interconnection service to such party and shall be subject to FERC approval.

PDF page 21

3.21. Dispatch. The operating control of an integrated electric system to: i) assign specific Generation Units and other sources of supply to effect the supply to meet the relevant area Demand taken as Load rises or falls; ii) control operations and maintenance of high voltage lines, substations, and equipment, including administration of safety procedures;

iii) operate Interconnections; iv) manage Energy transactions with other interconnected Control Areas; and v) curtail Demand.

3.22. Distribution System. The distribution assets of a TO, UDC, or MSS.

3.23. Eligible Customer. (i) Any utility (including any Participating TO, Market Participant or power marketer), Federal power marketing agency, or any person generating Energy for sale or resale; Energy sold or produced by such entity may be Energy produced in the United States, Canada or Mexico; however, such entity is not eligible for transmission service that would be prohibited by FPA Section 212(h)(2); and (ii) any retail customer taking unbundled transmission service pursuant to a state retail access program or pursuant to a voluntary offer of unbundled retail transmissions service by the Participating TO.

3.24. Eligible Customer for Large Load (“ECLL”). A UDC or MSS that provides retail transmission and interconnection service to Large Load End-Users in the ISO’s Balancing Authority Area.

3.25. ECLL Interconnection Agreement. The agreement between an ECLL and the Participating TO governing an ECLL Interconnection.

3.26. ECLL Interconnection. The interconnection of the facilities of an ECLL to the facilities of the Participating TO that are for the purpose of an ECLL interconnecting and providing transmission service to a Large Load Customer.

3.27. ECLL Interconnection Application. An application that requests an ECLL Interconnection to the ISO Controlled Grid.

3.28. ECLL Interconnection Facilities. The facilities, additions, and upgrades of the Participating TO necessary to accomplish an ECLL Interconnection, as identified in the applicable ECLL Interconnection Agreement.

3.29. Encumbrance. A legal restriction or covenant binding on the Participating TO that affects the operation of any transmission lines or associated facilities and which the ISO needs to take into account in exercising Operational Control over such transmission lines or associated facilities if the Participating TO is not to risk incurring significant liability. Encumbrances shall include Existing Contracts and may include: (1) other local restrictions or covenants meeting the definition of Encumbrance and arising under other arrangements entered into before the ISO Operations Date, if any; and (2) legal restrictions or covenants meeting the definition of Encumbrance and arising under a contract or other arrangement entered into after the ISO Operations Date.

PDF page 22

3.30. End-Use Customer or End-User. A purchaser of electric power that purchases such power to satisfy a Load directly connected to the ISO Controlled Grid or to a Distribution System and who does not resell the power.

3.31. Energy. The electrical energy produced, flowing, or supplied by Generation, transmission, or distribution facilities, being the integral with respect to time of the instantaneous power, measured in units of watt-hours or standard multiples thereof. 3.31.1.1.

E.g. 1000 Wh = 1 kW, 1000 kWh = 1 MWh, etc.

3.32. Entitlement. The right of a Participating TO obtained through contract or other means to use another entity’s transmission facilities for the transmission of Energy.

3.33. Existing Contracts. Those transmission service agreements or other contracts which grant transmission service rights in existence on the ISO Operations Date (including any contracts entered into pursuant to such contracts) as may be amended in accordance with their terms or by agreement between the parties thereto from time to time.

3.34. Existing Rights. Those transmission service rights defined in Section 16.1 of the ISO Tariff.

3.35. Expedited Interconnection Agreement. A contract between a party which has submitted a Request for Expedited Interconnection Procedures and the Participating TO under which the Participating TO agrees to process, on an expedited basis, the Completed Interconnection Application of such party and which sets forth the terms, conditions, and cost responsibilities for such Interconnection.

3.36. Facilities Study Agreement. An agreement between a Participating TO and either a party requesting Interconnection to the ISO Controlled Grid, Market Participants, Project Sponsor, ECLL, or identified principal beneficiaries pursuant to which the party requesting such Interconnection agrees to reimburse the Participating TO for the cost of performing or reviewing a Facilities Study.

3.37. Facility or Facilities Study. An engineering study conducted to determine required modifications to the Participating TO’s transmission system, including the estimated cost and scheduled completion date for such modifications, that will be required to provide needed services.

3.38. FERC. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, or its successor.

3.39. Firm Interconnection Service. The highest quality (priority) load Interconnection service that provides the on-going safe and reliable operation and maintenance of, and the Parties’ rights and responsibilities associated with their facilities.

3.40. Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (“FILI”) Service. A transmission interconnection service offered by the Participating TO and accepted by an Eligible Customer on behalf of a Large Load retail customer to manage operational constraints on

PDF page 23

withdrawals from the transmission system while the interconnection and system upgrades necessary to provide Firm Interconnection Service are being developed.

3.41. FILI Service Agreement. The agreement developed by the Participating TO pursuant to Section 10A.4 that sets forth the terms, conditions, and operating requirements for FILI Service.

3.42. FPA. The Federal Power Act, 16 U.S.C.§ 791a et seq., as it may be amended from time to time.

3.43. Generating Facility. An Interconnection Customer’s Generating Unit(s) used for the production and/or storage for later injection of electricity identified in the Interconnection Request, but shall not include the Interconnection Customer’s Interconnection Facilities.

3.44. Generating Unit. An individual electric generator and its associated plant and apparatus whose electrical output is capable of being separately identified and metered or a Physical Scheduling Plant, that, in either case, is: (a) located within the ISO Control Area; (b) connected to the ISO Controlled Grid, either directly or via interconnected transmission or distribution facilities; and (c) that is capable of producing and delivering net Energy (Energy in excess of a generation stations’ internal power requirements).

3.45. Generation. Energy delivered from a Generating Unit.

3.46. Generator Interconnection. The interconnection of one or more Generating Units to the ISO Controlled Grid facilities owned by the Participating TO.

3.47. Good Utility Practice. Any of the practices, methods, and acts engaged in or approved by a significant portion of the electric utility industry during the relevant time period, or any of the practices, methods, and acts which, in the exercise of reasonable judgment in light of the facts known at the time the decision was made, could have been expected to accomplish the desired result at a reasonable cost consistent with good business practices, reliability, safety, and expedition.

3.48. Gross Load. For purposes of calculating the transmission Access Charge, Gross Load is all Energy (adjusted for distribution losses) delivered for the supply of End-Use Customer Loads directly connected to the transmission facilities or directly connected to the Distribution System of a Utility Distribution Company or MSS Operator located in a PTO Service Territory. Gross Load shall exclude (1) Load with respect to which the Wheeling Access Charge is payable, (2) Load that is exempt from the Access Charge pursuant to Section 4.1, Appendix I of the ISO Tariff, and the portion of the load of an individual retail customer of a Utility Distribution Company, Small Utility Distribution Company or MSS Operator that is served by a Generating Unit that: (a) is located on the customer’s site or provides service to the customer’s site through over-the-fence arrangements as authorized by Section 218 of the California Public Utilities Code; (b) is a qualifying small power production facility or qualifying cogeneration facility, as those

PDF page 24

terms are defined in the FERC’s regulations implementing Section 201 of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978; and (c) secures Standby Service from the Participating TO under terms approved by a Local Regulatory Authority or FERC, as applicable, or can be curtailed concurrently with an Outage of the Generating Unit serving the Load. Gross Load forecasts consistent with filed Transmission Revenue Requirements will be provided by each Participating TO to the ISO.

3.49. High Voltage Access Charge. A component of the Access Charge determined by the ISO under Section 26.1 of the ISO Tariff.

3.50. High Voltage Transmission Facility. A transmission facility under the Operational Control of the ISO that is owned by the Participating TO or to which the Participating TO has an Entitlement that may be associated with a Converted Right, which operates at a voltage at or above 200 kilovolts, and supporting facilities, and the costs of which are not directly assigned to one or more specific customers.

3.51. High Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement. The portion of the Participating TO’s TRR associated with and allocable to the Participating TO’s High Voltage Transmission Facilities and Rights associated with High Voltage Transmission Facilities 3.52. High Voltage Utility-Specific Rate. The Participating TO’s High Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement divided by the Participating TO’s forecast of its Gross Load.

3.53. High Voltage Wheeling Access Charge. The Wheeling Access Charge assessed by the ISO associated with the recovery of the Participating TO’s High Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement in accordance with Section 26.1 of the ISO Tariff.

3.54. Independent System Operator (“ISO”). The California Independent System Operator Corporation, a state chartered, nonprofit corporation that controls the transmission facilities of all Participating TOs and dispatches certain Generating Units and Loads. 3.55. ISO ADR Procedures. The procedures for resolution of disputes or differences set out in Section 13 of the ISO Tariff, as amended from time to time.

3.56. ISO Controlled Grid. The system of transmission lines and associated facilities of the Participating TOs that have been placed under the ISO’s Operational Control.

3.57. ISO Protocols. The rules, protocols, procedures and standards promulgated by the ISO (as amended from time to time) to be complied with by the ISO Scheduling Coordinators, Participating TOs and all other Market Participants in relation to the operation of the ISO Controlled Grid and the participation in the markets for Energy and Ancillary Services in accordance with the ISO Tariff.

3.58. ISO Tariff. The California Independent System Operator Agreement and Tariff, dated November 1, 2013, as it may be modified from time to time.

3.59. Interconnection Agreement. A contract between a party requesting a TSWL

PDF page 25

Interconnection and  a Participating TO, as it may be amended from time to time, and, for an ECLL Interconnection, the ECLL Interconnection Agreement.

3.60. Interest. Interest shall be calculated in accordance with the methodology specified for interest on refunds in the regulations of FERC at 18 C.F.R. § 35.19a. Interest on delinquent amounts shall be calculated from the due date of the bill to the date of payment. When payments are made by mail, bills shall be considered as having been paid on the date of receipt. Notwithstanding the foregoing, interest, if any, on amounts payable or refundable between the Participating TO and a party to a Cost Recovery Agreement shall be governed solely by that Cost Recovery Agreement.

3.61. Interim Firm Interconnection Service. Interconnection service that can be provided, if any, on a firm basis prior to the completion of the ECLL Interconnection Facilities and an authorization for the Large Load to withdraw Energy.

3.62. Large Load. An End-User located at a single site behind one or more Point(s) of Withdrawal from the ISO Controlled Grid and that has a peak load of 50 MW or greater.

3.63. Load. An end-use device of an End-Use Customer that consumes power. Load should not be confused with Demand, which is the measure of power that a Load receives or requires.

3.64. Local Publicly Owned Electric Utility. A municipality or municipal corporation operating as a public utility furnishing electric service, a municipal district furnishing electric services, or a joint powers authority that includes one or more of these agencies and that owns Generation or transmission facilities, or furnishes electric services over its own or its members’ electric Distribution System.

3.65. Local Regulatory Authority. The state or local governmental authority responsible for the regulation or oversight of a utility.

3.66. Local Reliability Criteria. Reliability criteria established by the ISO, unique to the transmission systems of each of the Participating TOs, as they may be updated from time to time.

3.67. Low Voltage Access Charge. The Access Charge applicable under Section 26.1 of the ISO Tariff to recover the Low Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement of the Participating TO.

3.68. Low Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement. The portion of the Participating TO’s TRR associated with and allocable to the Participating TO’s Low Voltage Transmission Facilities and Converted Rights associated with Low Voltage Transmission Facilities.

3.69. Low Voltage Wheeling Access Charge. The Wheeling Access Charge associated with the recovery of the Participating TO’s Low Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement

PDF page 26

in accordance with Section 26.1 of the 1SO Tariff.

3.70. Market Participant. An entity, including a Scheduling Coordinator, who participates in the Energy marketplace through the buying, selling, transmission, or distribution of Energy or Ancillary Services into, out of, or through the ISO Controlled Grid.

3.71. Metered Subsystem (“MSS”). A geographically contiguous system, located within a single zone which has been operating as an electric utility for a number of years prior to the ISO Operations Date as a municipal utility, water district, irrigation district, state agency or federal power marketing authority subsumed within the ISO Balancing Authority Area and encompassed by ISO certified revenue quality meters at each interface point with the ISO Controlled Grid and ISO-certified revenue quality meters on all Generating Units or, if aggregated, each individual resource and Participating Load, Reliability Demand Response Resource, and Proxy Demand Resource internal to the system, which is operated in accordance with a MSS agreement described in Section 4.9.1 of the ISO Tariff.

3.72. NERC. The North American Electric Reliability Corporation or its successor.

3.73. New Participating TO. A Participating TO that is not an Original Participating TO.

3.74. Non-Load-Serving Participating TO. A Participating TO that does not serve Load.

3.75. Non-Participating TO. A TO that is not a party to the TCA or, for the purpose of Section 16.1 of the ISO Tariff, the holder of transmission service rights under an Existing Contract that is not a Participating TO.

3.76. Non-Spinning Reserve. The portion of off-line generating capacity that is capable of being synchronized and ramping to a specified load in ten minutes (or load that is capable of being interrupted in ten minutes) and that is capable of running (or being interrupted) for at least two hours.

3.77. Operational Control. The rights of the ISO under the Transmission Control Agreement and the ISO Tariff to direct Participating TOs how to operate their transmission lines and facilities and other electric plant affecting the reliability of those lines and facilities for the purpose of affording comparable nondiscriminatory transmission access and meeting Applicable Reliability Criteria.

3.78. Original Participating TO. A Participating TO that was a Participating TO as of January 1, 2000. The Original Participating TOs are Pacific Gas and Electric Company, Southern California Edison Company, and San Diego Gas & Electric Company. 3.79. Participating TO (“PTO”). A party to the TCA whose application under Section 2.2 of the TCA has been accepted and who has placed, or expects to place, its transmission assets and/or Entitlements under the ISO’s Operational Control in accordance with the TCA. A PTO may be an Original Participating TO or a New Participating TO. For the purposes of this Tariff, the Participating TO is DesertLink.

PDF page 27

3.80. Participation Agreement. An agreement between a Participating TO and a Project Sponsor that specifies the terms and conditions under which the Participating TO will construct a transmission addition or upgrade on behalf of the Project Sponsor. 3.81. Physical Scheduling Plant. A group of two or more related Generating Units each of which is individually capable of producing Energy, but which either by physical necessity or operational design must be operated as if they were a single Generating Unit and any Generating Unit or Units containing related multiple generating components which meet one or more of the following criteria: (i) multiple generating components are related by a common flow of fuel which cannot be interrupted without substantial loss of efficiency of the combined output of all components; (ii) the Energy production from one component necessarily causes Energy production from other components; (iii) the operational arrangement of related multiple generating components determines the overall physical efficiency of the combined output of all components; (iv) the level of coordination required to schedule individual generating components would cause the ISO to incur scheduling costs far in excess of the benefits of having scheduled such individual components separately; or (v) metered output is available only for the combined output of related multiple generation components and separate generating component metering is either impractical or economically inefficient.

3.82. Point of Withdrawal. Point(s) within the ISO Balancing Authority Area, or for purposes of scheduling and operating the Day Ahead Market only, the EDAM Area where Energy and Ancillary Services are made available to a receiving party under the ISO Tariff, for purposes of scheduling and operating the Real-Time Market only, the EIM Area where Energy and Ancillary Services are made available to a receiving party under the ISO Tariff, or for purposes of the definition of Large Load only, the point(s) where a non- transmission facility that is used to withdraw Energy from the ISO Controlled Grid to serve an End-User connects to the ISO Controlled Grid.

3.83. Project. DesertLink’s interest in the single-circuit 500 kV (AC) overhead transmission line connecting the existing Harry Allen Substation in Nevada to the existing Eldorado Substation in Nevada, including series compensation. For the avoidance of doubt, the Project does not include any required work within the fence line of each substation.

3.84. Project Proponent. A Market Participant or group of Market Participants that (i) advocates a transmission addition or upgrade; (ii) is unwilling to pay the full cost of the proposed transmission addition or upgrade, and thus is not a Project Sponsor; and (iii) initiates proceedings under the ISO ADR Procedures to determine the need for the proposed transmission addition or upgrade.

3.85. Project Sponsor. A Market Participant or group of Market Participants or a Participating TO that proposes the construction of a transmission addition or upgrade in accordance with Section 24 of the ISO Tariff.

3.86. Regional Transmission Group (“RTG”). A voluntary organization approved by FERC

PDF page 28

and composed of transmission owners, transmission users, and other entities, organized to efficiently coordinate the planning, expansion, and use of transmission on a regional and inter-regional basis.

3.87. Regulation. The service provided either by Generating Units certified by the ISO as equipped and capable of responding to the ISO’s direct digital control (AGC) signals, or by System Resources that have been certified by the ISO as capable of delivering such service to the ISO Balancing Authority Area, in an upward and downward direction to match, on a Real Time basis, Demand and resources, consistent with established NERC and WECC reliability standards, including any requirements of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Regulation is used to control the Power output of electric generators within a prescribed area in response to a change in system frequency, tie-line loading, or the relation of these to each other so as to maintain the target system frequency and/or the established interchange with other Balancing Authority Areas within the predetermined Regulation Limits. Regulation includes both the increase of output by a Generating unit or System Resource (Regulation Up) and the decrease in output by a Generating unit or System Resource (Regulation Down). Regulation Up and Regulation Down are distinct capacity products, with separately stated requirements and ASMPs in each Settlement Period.

3.88. Regulatory Authority. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

3.89. Reliability Criteria. Pre-established criteria that are to be followed in order to maintain desired performance of the ISO Controlled Grid under contingency or steady state conditions.

3.90. Reliability Upgrade. The transmission facilities, other than Direct Assignment Facilities, beyond the first point of Interconnection necessary to accomplish a TSWL Interconnection safely and reliably to the ISO Controlled Grid, which would not have been necessary but for the TSWL Interconnection, including network upgrades necessary to remedy short circuit or stability problems resulting from the TSWL Interconnection. Reliability Upgrades also include, consistent with WECC practice, the facilities necessary to mitigate any adverse impact a TSWL Interconnection may have on a path’s WECC path rating. Reliability Upgrades shall be specified in the Interconnection Agreement that governs a TSWL Interconnection and shall be subject to FERC approval.

3.91. Requests for Expedited Interconnection Procedures. A written request by which an applicant for Interconnection can request expedited processing of its TSWL Interconnection Application.

3.92. Scheduling Coordinator. An entity certified by the ISO for the purpose of undertaking the functions specified in Section 4.5 of the ISO Tariff.

3.93. Scheduling Point. A location at which the ISO Controlled Grid or a transmission facility owned by a Transmission Ownership Right holder is connected, by a group of transmission paths for which a physical, non-simultaneous transmission capacity rating

PDF page 29

has been established for Congestion Management, to transmission facilities that are outside the ISO’s Operational Control.

3.94. Site Control. An ECLL may demonstrate that its Large Load Customer has Site Control by:

an option for a lease or an executed lease for real property of sufficient size to house the Large Load; or

an option to purchase or title to real property of sufficient size to house the Large Load.

3.95. Spinning Reserve. The portion of unloaded synchronized generating capacity that is immediately responsive to system frequency and that is capable of being loaded in ten minutes, and that is capable of running for at least two hours.

3.96. System Impact Study. An engineering study conducted to determine whether a request for Interconnection to the ISO Controlled Grid would require new transmission additions, upgrades, or other mitigation measures.

3.97. System Impact Study Agreement. An agreement between a Participating TO and an entity that has requested Interconnection to the Participating TO’s transmission system pursuant to which the entity requesting Interconnection agrees to reimburse the Participating TO for the cost of performing or reviewing a System Impact Study.

3.98. TO Tariff. This Transmission Owner Tariff, as it may be amended or superseded.

3.99. [Reserved].
3.100. [Reserved].
3.101. Transmission Control Agreement (“TCA”). The agreement between the ISO and Participating TOs establishing the terms and conditions under which TOs will become Participating TOs and how the ISO and each Participating TO will discharge its respective duties and responsibilities, as may be modified from time to time.

3.102. Transmission Owner (“TO”). An entity owning transmission facilities or having firm contractual rights to use transmission facilities.

3.103. Transmission Revenue Balancing Account Adjustment (“TRBAA”). A mechanism established by the Participating TO which will ensure that all Transmission Revenue Credits and other credits specified in Section 6 and 8 of Appendix F, Schedule 3 of the ISO Tariff, and all amounts that a Cost Recovery Agreement requires to be credited through the TRBAA, flow through to ISO Tariff and TO Tariff transmission customers.

3.104. Transmission Revenue Credit. The proceeds received from the ISO (other than for the recovery of the Participating TO’s High Voltage and Low Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement through the High Voltage and Low Voltage Transmission Access Charges) and charges imposed by the ISO that are received and paid by the Participating TO in its

PDF page 30

role as Participating TO, as defined in the ISO Tariff.
3.105. Transmission Revenue Requirement (“TRR’). The total annual authorized revenue requirement associated with transmission facilities and Entitlements turned over to the Operational Control of the ISO by the Participating TO. The costs of any transmission facility turned over to the Operational Control of the ISO shall be fully included in the Participating TO’s TRR. The TRR includes the costs of transmission facilities and Entitlements and deducts Transmission Revenue Credits and is shown in Appendix I.

3.106. Transmission System Rights (“TSRs”). TSRs represent DesertLink’s exclusive transmission entitlement on its share of the Project. DesertLink, as the holder of the TSRs, is entitled to all associated rights as are available under the ISO Tariff and Protocols. The use of this definition does not limit DesertLink from seeking any additional revenues or rights that are authorized by FERC due to a beneficial increase in the ISO controlled grid capacity resulting from the Project.

3.107. Transmission System Wholesale Load (“TSWL”) Interconnection. The
interconnection of the transmission facilities of the Participating TO to the transmission facilities of a Transmission Owner, electric utility, or other entity eligible to request interconnection. A TSWL Interconnection does not include a Generator Interconnection or an ECLL Interconnection.

3.108. TSWL Interconnection Application. An application that requests a TSWL Interconnection to the ISO Controlled Grid, including any modifications to existing points of interconnection.

3.109. Uncontrollable Force. Any act of God, labor disturbance, act of the public enemy, war, insurrection, riot, fire, storm, flood, earthquake, explosion, any curtailment, order, regulation or restriction imposed by governmental, military or lawfully established civilian authorities or any other cause beyond the reasonable control of the ISO or Market Participant, as the case may be, which could not be avoided through the exercise of Good Utility Practice.

3.110. Utility Distribution Company (“UDC”). An entity that owns a Distribution System for the delivery of Energy to and from the ISO Controlled Grid, and/or that provides regulated retail electric service to End-Users.

3.111. Voltage Support. Services provided by Generating Units or other equipment such- as shunt capacitors, static vat compensators, or synchronous condensers that are required to maintain established grid voltage criteria. This service is required under normal or system emergency conditions.

3.112. Western Electricity Coordinating Council (“WECC”). The Western Electricity Coordinating Counsel or its successor.

3.113. Wheeling Access Charge. The charge assessed by the ISO that is paid by a Scheduling Coordinator for Wheeling in accordance with Section 26.1.4.1 of the ISO Tariff.

PDF page 31

Wheeling Access Charges shall not apply for Wheeling under a bundled non-economy Energy coordination agreement of a Participating TO executed prior to July 9, 1996. The Wheeling Access Charge consists of a High Voltage Wheeling Access Charge and, if applicable, a Low Voltage Wheeling Access Charge.

3.114. Wheeling Out. Except for Existing Rights exercised under an Existing Contract in accordance with Section 16.1 of the ISO Tariff, the use of the ISO Controlled Grid for the transmission of Energy from a Generating Unit located within the ISO Controlled Grid to serve a Load located outside the transmission and Distribution System of a Participating TO.

3.115. Wheeling Through. Except for Existing Rights exercised under an Existing Contract in accordance with Section 16.1 of the ISO Tariff, the use of the ISO Controlled Grid for the transmission of Energy from a resource located outside the ISO Controlled Grid to serve a Load located outside the transmission and Distribution System of a Participating TO. 3.116. Wheeling. Wheeling Out or Wheeling Through.

3.117. Wholesale Customer. A person wishing to purchase Energy and Ancillary Services at a Bulk Supply Point or a Scheduling Point for resale.

4. Eligibility for Service. Transmission service over a Participating TO’s system shall be provided only to Eligible Customers for transmission service under the ISO Tariff. Any dispute as to whether an entity that resells power is eligible for an interconnection under this TO Tariff shall be resolved by the FERC. Any dispute as to whether an End-User is eligible for an interconnection under this TO Tariff will be resolved by the Local Regulatory Authority.

5. Access Charges and Transmission Rates. The applicable Access Charges are provided in the ISO Tariff.

5.1
Low Voltage Access Charge. The Low Voltage Access Charge shall be determined in accordance with the ISO Tariff. As DesertLink is a Non-Load- Serving Participant TO, the ISO shall charge for and collect the Low Voltage Access Charge on DesertLink’s behalf pursuant to Section 26.1 and Appendix F, Schedule 3, Section 13 of the ISO Tariff from the Participating TO to whose facilities DesertLink’s Low Voltage Transmission Facilities are directly connected. The rate for DesertLink’s Low Voltage Access Charge Shall be DesertLink’s Low Voltage Transmission Revenue Requirement divided by the forecasted Gross Load of the Participating TO that is the Low Voltage Access Charge customer. The Low Voltage Access Charge customer shall pay the ISO a Low Voltage Access Charge equal to the product of DesertLink’s Low Voltage Access Charge rate and the actual Gross Load of the Participating TO that is the Low Voltage Access Charge Customer.

5.2
Wheeling Access Charge. The Wheeling Access Charge shall be determined in accordance with the ISO Tariff. The Wheeling Access Charge assessed by the ISO consists of a High Voltage Wheeling Access Charge and, if applicable, a Low Voltage Wheeling Access Charge. The High Voltage Wheeling Access Charge is set forth in the ISO Tariff.

5.3
Transmission Revenue Requirement. As set forth in the ISO Tariff, the Transmission Revenue Requirement for each Participating TO is used to develop the Access Charges set forth in the ISO Tariff and is used by the ISO to calculate the disbursement of Wheeling revenues among Participating TOs. Wheeling revenues are disbursed by the ISO to Participating TOs pursuant to Section 26.1.4.3 of the ISO Tariff. DesertLink’s TRR is set forth in Appendix I.

5.4
Transmission System Rights. DesertLink owns the TSRs with respect to the Project consistent with its ownership percentage of the Project and owns the TSRs with respect to any subsequent project it develops.

5.5
Transmission Revenue Balancing Account Adjustment (“TRBAA”). The
Participating TO shall maintain a Transmission Revenue Balancing Account with an annual TRBAA that will ensure that all Transmission Revenue Credits and adjustments for any over-or under-recovery of its annual Transmission Revenue Requirement, if any, specified in Sections 6, 8 and 13 of Appendix F, Schedule 3 of the ISO Tariff, flow through to transmission customers. The TRBAA used to calculate the High Voltage Revenue Requirement shall include other adjustments specified in Appendix F, Schedule 3, Sections 6, 8 and 13 of the ISO Tariff. The TRBAA shall also ensure that all amounts that a Cost Recovery Agreement requires to be credited to transmission customers through the TRBAA flow through to transmission customers.

PDF page 34

The TRBAA shall be equal to:
TRBAA = Cr + Cf + I
Where:

Cr =
The principal balance in the Transmission Revenue Balancing Account (“TRBA”) recorded in FERC Account No. 254 as of September 30 of the year prior to commencement of the January billing cycle. This balance represents the unamortized balance in the TRBA from the previous period and the difference in the amount of revenues or expenditures from Transmission Revenue Credits, amounts recorded in the TRBA under any Cost Recovery Agreement, and any over- or under-recovery of its annual Transmission Revenue Requirement and the amount of such revenues or expenditures that has been refunded to or collected from customers through operation of the TRBAA;

Cf =
The forecast of Transmission Revenue Credits, if any, for the following calendar year, plus any forecast credit that a Cost Recovery Agreement requires to be included in the TRBAA for the following calendar year;

I =
The interest balance for the TRBA, which shall be calculated using the interest rate pursuant to Section 35.19a of FERC’s regulations under the Federal Power Act (18 CFR Section 35.19a). Interest shall be calculated based on the average TRBA principal balance each month, compounded quarterly. Amounts recorded in the TRBA under any Cost Recovery

Agreement shall be included in the TRBA principal balance for purposes of this calculation. Nothing in this Section 5.5 requires the payment of interest between the Participating TO and a party to a Cost Recovery Agreement on amounts payable or refundable under that agreement, which shall be governed solely by the terms of the Cost Recovery

Agreement; and

The DesertLink TRBAA, calculated in accordance with the ISO Tariff and approved by the FERC, is stated in Appendix I.

8. Obligation to Interconnect or Construct Transmission Expansions and Facility Upgrades. Unless DesertLink is the lead Participating TO with respect to an Interconnection, the provisions of Section 8 of this TO Tariff, and its subparts, shall have no application to the Project or any other High Voltage Transmission Facilities, Low Voltage Transmission Facilities, or Entitlements turned over to the ISO’s operational control by DesertLink, and the corresponding provisions of the lead Participating TO’s TO Tariff shall govern.

8.1
Participating TO Obligation to Interconnect. The Participating TO shall, at the request of a third party, interconnect its system to the wholesale generation or Load of such third party, or modify an existing wholesale Interconnection. Interconnections under this TO Tariff shall be available to entities eligible to request Interconnection consistent with the provisions of Section 210(a) of the FPA. The procedures for the Interconnections of Load to the ISO Controlled Grid shall be governed by this TO Tariff and the ISO Tariff. The procedures for Interconnection of wholesale generation to the ISO Controlled Grid shall be governed by the ISO Tariff.

8.1.1 Interconnection to Transmission System. Any interconnection must be consistent with Good Utility Practice, in conformance with all Applicable Reliability Criteria, all applicable statutes, regulations, and ISO reliability criteria for the ISO Controlled Grid. The Participating TO will not accommodate the interconnection if doing so would impair systems reliability, or would otherwise impair the ability of the Participating TO to honor its Encumbrances existing as of the time an entity submits its interconnection application. The Participating TO shall identify any such adverse effect on its Encumbrances in the interconnection studies. To the extent the Participating TO determines that the interconnection will have an adverse effect on Encumbrances, the party requesting interconnection shall mitigate such adverse effect.

8.1.1.1 Letter Agreement for Generator Interconnections. Pursuant to Section 12 of Appendix DD or KK of the ISO Tariff, prior to executing a Generator Interconnection Agreement, a party seeking a Generator Interconnection may, in order to advance the implementation of its Interconnection, request, and the Participating TO shall offer the party, a Letter Agreement that authorizes the Participating TO to begin engineering, design, and procurement of long lead-time items, or construction necessary for the establishment of the Generator Interconnection. However, the Participating TO shall not be obligated to offer a Letter Agreement if the party seeking Generator

Interconnection is in Dispute Resolution as a result of an allegation that the party seeking Interconnection has failed to meet any milestones or comply with any prerequisites specified in the ISO Tariff. The Letter Agreement is an optional procedure. The Letter

PDF page 36

Agreement shall provide for the party seeking Generator
Interconnection to pay the cost of all activities authorized by the party and to make advance payments or provide other satisfactory security for such costs.

Following a party seeking Interconnection’s request for a Letter Agreement, the Participating TO shall prepare and tender to the party seeking Interconnection a draft Letter Agreement, including draft exhibits that include the proposed scope of work, estimated costs, payments, financial security and milestones, as applicable. The party seeking Generator Interconnection shall provide written comments, or notification of no comments, to the draft exhibits within thirty (30) Calendar Days. The Participating TO and the party seeking Interconnection shall negotiate concerning any disputed provisions of the exhibits to the draft Letter Agreement for not more than ninety (90) Calendar Days after the Participating TO tenders the draft Letter Agreement to the party seeking Generator Interconnection. If the party seeking Interconnection determines that negotiations are at an impasse, it may request termination of the negotiations at any time after tender of the draft Letter Agreement and request submission of the unexecuted Letter Agreement with FERC or initiate dispute resolution procedures pursuant to Section 14 of this TO Tariff. If the party seeking Generator Interconnection requests termination of the negotiations, but within ninety (90) Calendar Days after the Participating TO tenders the draft Letter Agreement to the party seeking Interconnection, fails to request either the filing of the unexecuted Letter Agreement or initiate dispute resolution procedures, it shall be deemed to have withdrawn its request for a Letter Agreement and the Participating TO shall have no further obligation to enter into a Letter Agreement, unless an extension is mutually agreed to by the parties. The Participating TO shall provide to the party seeking Interconnection a final Letter Agreement within fifteen (15) Business Days after the completion of the negotiation process.

Following submission of the final Letter Agreement to the party seeking Generator Interconnection, the party shall either: (i) execute two originals of the tendered Letter Agreement and return them to the Participating TO; or (ii) request in writing that the Participating TO file with FERC a Letter Agreement in unexecuted form. As soon as practicable, but not later than ten (10) Business Days after receiving either the two executed originals of the tendered Letter Agreement or the request to file an unexecuted Letter Agreement, the Participating TO shall file the Letter Agreement with FERC, together with its explanation of any matters as to which the party seeking Interconnection and the Participating TO disagree and support for the costs that the Participating TO proposes to charge to the party seeking

PDF page 37

Generator Interconnection under the Letter Agreement. An unexecuted Letter Agreement should contain terms and conditions deemed appropriate by the Participating TO for the Generator Interconnection request.

If the party seeking Interconnection executes the final Letter Agreement, the Participating TO and the party seeking Generator Interconnection shall perform their respective obligations in accordance with the terms of the Letter Agreement, subject to modification by FERC. Upon submission of an unexecuted Letter Agreement, the party seeking Generator Interconnection and the Participating TO shall promptly comply with the unexecuted Letter Agreement, subject to modification by FERC.

8.1.2 Costs Associated with Interconnection. Each party requesting Interconnection shall pay the costs of planning, installing, owning, operating, and maintaining any Direct Assignment Facilities and, if applicable, any Reliability Upgrades required to provide the requested Interconnection. In addition, such party shall implement all existing operating procedures necessary to safely and reliability interconnect such party’s generation or wholesale load to the facilities of the Participating TO and to ensure the ISO Controlled Grid’s conformance with the ISO Grid Planning Criteria, and shall bear all costs of implementing such operating procedures. Any additional costs associated with accommodating the Interconnection shall be allocated in accordance with the cost responsibility methodology set forth in the ISO Tariff for transmission expansions or upgrades.

8.1.3 Interconnection Agreement. Interconnection Agreements shall be tendered, executed, and filed as provided in Sections 10.9 and 10A.3.

8.1.4 Due Diligence to Construct. The Participating TO shall use due diligence to construct, within a reasonable time, any Direct Assignment Facilities and any Reliability Upgrades that it is obligated to construct pursuant to this TO Tariff and Section 24 of the ISO Tariff. The Participating TO’s obligation to build will be subject to: (1) its ability, after making a good faith effort, to obtain any necessary approvals and property rights under applicable federal, state, and local laws; (2) the presence of a cost recovery mechanism with cost responsibility assigned to accordance with the ISO Tariff or applicable FERC precedent; and

(3) a signed Interconnection Agreement or a signed Expedited Interconnection Agreement, or, by mutual agreement of the parties, FERC acceptance for filing of an unexecuted Interconnection Agreement.

8.1.5 Energization. The Participating TO shall not be obligated to energize,

PDF page 38

nor shall the applicant or wholesale load be entitled to have its interconnection to the ISO Controlled Grid energized, unless and until an Interconnection Agreement has been executed, or filed at FERC pursuant to Section 8.1.3, and become effective and such applicant or wholesale load has demonstrated to the ISO’s reasonable satisfaction that it has complied with all of the requirements of the ISO Tariff and the requirements of this TO Tariff.

8.1.6 Coordination with ISO on Interconnection Requests. The Participating TO shall coordinate with the ISO, pursuant to the provisions of the TCA, in developing interconnection standards and guidelines for processing interconnection request under this TO Tariff.

8.2
Participating TO Obligation to Construct Transmission Expansions or Facility Upgrades. The Participating TO shall be obligated to: (1) perform System Impact or Facility Studies where the Project Sponsor or the ISO agrees to pay the study cost and specifies the project objectives to be achieved, and (2) build transmission additions and facility upgrades where the Participating TO is obligated to construct or expand facilities in accordance with and subject to the limitations under Section 24 of the ISO Tariff’ and this TO Tariff.

8.2.1 Obligation to Construct. A Participating TO shall not be obligated to construct or expand transmission facilities or system upgrades unless and until the conditions stated in Section 9.2.1 hereof have been satisfied.

8.3
Request for FERC Deference Regarding Need Determination. It is intended that FERC grant substantial deference to the factual determinations of the ISO, (including the ISO’s ADR Procedures), the CPUC, WECC, or RTG coordinated planning processes as to the need for or construction of a facility, the need for full cost recovery, end the allocation of costs.
