DA = Direct Assignment; GP = Gross Plant Allocator (page 2, line 5); N/A = Not Applicable; NP = Net Plant Allocator (page 2, line 17); TP = Transmission Plant Allocator (page 4, line 5); WS = Wage and Salary Allocator (page 4, line 11). X

The revenues credited on page 1, lines 2-6, shall include only the amounts received by DesertLink for service rendered using facilities for which recovery is provided under this tariff. They do not include revenues associated with FERC annual charges, gross receipts taxes, or facilities not included in this template (e.g., direct assignment facilities and GSUs) which are not recovered under this Rate Formula Template.

Accumulated deferred income tax amounts associated with asset or liability accounts excluded from rate base (such as ADIT related to asset retirement obligations and certain tax-related regulatory assets or liabilities) do not affect rate base.  Balance of Account 255 will be reduced by prior flow throughs and excluded if the utility chooses to utilize amortization of tax credits against taxable income. Account 281 is not allocated to Transmission.

Recovery of Regulatory Asset permitted only for pre-commercial and formation expenses as authorized by the Commission. Recovery of any other regulatory assets requires authorization from the Commission. A carrying charge equal to the AFUDC rate will be applied to the Regulatory Asset prior to the rate year when costs are first recovered.

Cash Working Capital assigned to transmission is one-eighth of O&M allocated to transmission at page 3, line 17, column 5 minus amortization of Regulatory Asset at page 3, line 14, column 5.  Prepayments are the electric related prepayments booked to Account No. 165 and reported on page 111, line 57 in the Form 1.

The FERC's annual charges for the year assessed the Transmission Owner for service under this tariff.  To the extent the charges are separately identified on the FERC Form 1, page 350, column 1, the line number will be added to the source in Column 2 for reference.  Line item references can change from year to year.  Items not specifically identified in the FERC Form 1, page 350 will be obtained from Company books and records.

Includes only FICA, unemployment, highway, property, gross receipts, and other assessments charged in the current year.  Taxes related to income are excluded.  Enter the line number on page 262-63 upon which each item is identified.  To the extent individual types of taxes are separately identified on the FERC Form 1, page 262, column a, the line number will be added to the source in Column 2 for reference.  Line item references can change from year to year.  Items not specifically identified in the FERC Form 1, page 262-63 will be obtained from Company books and records.

FIT is the weighted average Federal income tax rate and SIT is the weighted average State income tax rate, both from Attachment 7, and p is the "the percentage of federal income tax deductible for state income taxes". A utility that elected to utilize amortization of tax credits against taxable income, rather than book tax credits to Account No. 255 and reduce rate base, must reduce its income tax expense by the amount of the Amortized Investment Tax Credit (Form 1, 266.8.f) multiplied by (1/1-T) (page 3, line 26). Excess Deferred Income Taxes reduce income tax expense by the amount of the expense multiplied by (1/(1-T)).

The Tax Effect of Permanent Differences captures the differences in the income taxes due under the Federal and State calculations and the income taxes calculated in Appendix III that are not the result of a timing difference. Tax Effect equals Permanent Differences multiplied by T.

The cost of debt will be determined based on the financing in place during each stage of project development. Before debt is obtained, a proxy interest rate which will be supported in the original Section 205 filing will be used. This rate is provided on Attachment 8 line 36. If construction debt (wherein principal is drawn down over time) is issued, the rate plus an amortization of fees projected to be incurred on the construction debt during the rate year will be the cost of debt. This construction debt rate (inclusive of fees) will be reset and trued-up every year using the method on Attachment 9 for multi-year construction projects. Once non-construction debt is obtained, the actual interest rate and fees on the debt in place at the end of the year such non- construction debt is obtained will become the cost of debt. In the first full year after non-construction debt is obtained, the cost of debt will be the actual cost of debt determined using the method on Attachment 5. A h

Calculate rate base using 13 month average balance, except ADIT.  The calculation of ADIT in the annual true-up calculation will use the beginning-of-year and end-of-year balances, and will be performed in accordance with IRS regulation Section 1.167(l)- 1(h)(6).  The calculation of ADIT in the annual projection will be performed in accordance with IRS Regulation Section 1.167(l)-1(h)(6).

Removes dollar amount of transmission plant to be included in the development of OATT ancillary services rates and generation step-up facilities, which are deemed to be included in OATT ancillary services. For these purposes, generation step-up facilities are those facilities at a generator substation on which there is no through-flow when the generator is shut down.

Upon enactment of changes in tax law, ADIT balances are re-measured and adjusted in the Company’s books of account, resulting in excess or deficient accumulated deferred income tax assets and liabilities.  Excess or deficient ADIT attributable to timing differences between the amounts of expenses or revenues recognized for income tax purposes and amounts of expenses or revenues recognized for ratemaking purposes as well as subsequent recoverable or refundable amortization of such amounts will be based upon Company records and be calculated and recorded in accordance with ASC 740 and any applicable normalization requirements of the taxing jurisdiction.  The Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Tax Adjustment (page 3, line 44) is computed by multiplying each component of Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Taxes (page 3, line 40) by the applicable tax gross-up factor.  For each re-measurement of ADIT, the amounts entered as the Deficient or (Excess) Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes component of ADJUSTMENTS TO RATE BASE (page 2, line 22a) or as the Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Tax Adjustment component of INCOME TAXES (page 3, line 44) will be supported by Attachment 13 (Deficient or Excess Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) providing the balance for each taxing jurisdiction at the beginning and end of the year, amortization for the year, calculation of the gross-up to the revenue requirement level and any other information required to support compliance with any applicable normalization requirements.

General and Intangible Depreciation and Amortization Expense includes all expenses (except depreciation and armortization of G&I Asset Retirement Obligations) not directly associated with a project, which is entered on page 3 , column 9.

Project Gross Plant is the total capital investment including CWIP for the project calculated from Company books and records in the same method as the gross plant value in line 1.  This value includes subsequent capital investments required to maintain the facilities to their original capabilities.  Refer to Attachment 1a for detail.

Project Net Plant is the Project Gross Plant Identified in Column 3 less the associated Accumulated Depreciation plus CWIP in rate base if applicable and Unamortized Abandoned Plant.  Refer to Attachment 1a for detail. Project Depreciation Expense is the actual value booked for the project (excluding General and Intangible depreciation) at Appendix III, page 3, line 19, plus amortization of Abandoned Plant at Appendix III, page 3, line 21.  For each project on Attachment 1a, Depreciation Expense is Attachment 1a, Line 2, Column (15) minus Column (3), and Amortization of Abandoned Plant is the difference between Columns (3) and (15) on Attachment 1a, Line 4. The Competitive Concession is the reduction in revenue, if any, that the company agreed to, for instance, to be selected to build facilities as the result of a competitive process and equals the amount by which the  annual revenue requirement is reduced from the ceiling rate.

Recovery of CWIP in rate base must be approved by FERC.  Lines 29-41 of page 2 provide a reconciliation of the Company's total CWIP to the CWIP allowed in rate base. The annual report filed pursuant to the Protocols will include for each project under construction (i) the CWIP balance eligible for inclusion in rate base; (ii) the CWIP balance ineligible for inclusion in rate base; and (iii) a demonstration that AFUDC is only applied to the CWIP balance that is not included in rate base The annual report will also describe the reconciliation prepared on this Attachment

Recovery of a Regulatory Asset is permitted only for pre-commercial and formation expenses, and is subject to FERC approval before the amortization of the Regulatory Asset can be included in rates. Recovery of any other regulatory assets requires authorization from the Commission.

The Formula Rate shall include a credit to rate base for all unfunded reserves (funds collected from customers that (1) have not been set aside in a trust, escrow or restricted account; (2) whose balance are collected from customers through cost accruals to accounts that are recovered under the Formula Rate; and (3) exclude the portion of any balance offset by a balance sheet ac count (see Note H)).  Each unfunded reserve will be included on lines 42 above. The allocator in Col. (g) will be the same allocator used in the formula for the cost accruals to the account that is recovered under the Formula Rate.  Since reserves can be created by creating an offsetting balance sheet account, rather than through cost accruals, the amount to be deducted from rate base should exclude the portion offset by another balance sheet account. Not all unfunded reserves are created only from contributions from customers. Many are created by creating an offsetting liability in whole or in part.  Column (f) ensures only the portion of the unfunded reserve contributed by the customer (and not created by an offsetting liability) is a reduction to rate base.

The inputs in Column (f) are the percentage of the unfunded reserve that was created by an offsetting liability. The percentage shown in Column (f) is then equal to the percentage that customers have contributed to the unfunded reserve.

In the case of tax law changes with an effective date(s) after the beginning of the test period, the impact of a timing difference on current tax expense or benefit differs from the impact on ADIT.  For example, in the case of a deductible timing difference originating in a tax year with a higher enacted tax rate than will apply when the difference will reverse, the current tax benefit will exceed the deferred tax expense.  In this situation, the adjustment computed below to recoverable income tax expense is made in order to avoid over-recovering income tax expense in the current test period due to the excess of current tax benefit over deferred tax expense (computed based on the estimated amount of the future tax liability) with respect to a given timing difference.  The adjustment to recoverable tax expense during the test period in which a timing difference originates mitigates the need for refund of a regulatory liability for excess deferred taxes in a future period (or, as applicable, the need for recovery of a regulatory asset for deficient deferred taxes in a future period).  Amounts in column (i) are reported in the Income Tax Allowance Adjustment Mechanism - Summary on this worksheet.

Note 2 - Explanation of how ADIT accounts are re-measured upon a change in income tax law
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted (re-measured) for the effect of the changes in tax law (including tax rates) in the period that the change is enacted.  Adjustments are recorded in the appropriate deferred tax balance sheet accounts (Accounts 190, 281, 282 and 283) based on the nature of the temporary difference and the related classification requirements of the accounts.   If as a result of action or expected action by a regulator, it is probable that the future increase or decrease in taxes payable due to the change in tax law or rates will be recovered from or returned to customers through future rates, a regulatory asset or liability is recognized in Account 182.3 (Other Regulatory Assets), or Account 254 (Other Regulatory Liabilities), as appropriate, for that probable future revenue or reduction in future revenue.  Re-measurements of deferred tax balance sheet accounts may also result in re-measurements of tax-related regulatory assets or liabilities that had been recorded prior to the change in tax law.  If it is not probable that the future increase or decrease in taxes payable due to the change in tax law or rates will be recovered from or returned to customers through future rates, tax expense is recognized in Account 410.2 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes, Other Income or Deductions) or tax benefit is recognized in Account 411.2 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes-Credit, Other Income or Deductions), as appropriate.

Note 3 - [Complete to support information above.]
Note 4 - The amortization of the deficient or excess ADIT reducing Account 254 (Other Regulatory Liabilities) is recorded with credits to Account 411.1 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes – Credit, Utility Operating Income) and to Account 190 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) or Account 283 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes—Other), as appropriate, in accordance with the Commission’s Accounting for Income Taxes Guidance.  The amortization of the deficient or excess ADIT reducing Account 182.3 (Other Regulatory Assets) is recorded with debits to Account 410.1 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes, Utility Operating Income) and to Account 190 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) or Account 283 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes—Other), as appropriate, in accordance with the Commission’s Accounting for Income Taxes Guidance. This activity is summarized in the table "Income Tax Allowance Mechanism - Projected" or the table "Income Tax Allowance Mechanism - Actual," as appropriate.  The annual amortization in the tables above reflects tax gross-up and is stated at the revenue requirement level.

Note 5 - [Complete to support information above.]
Note 6 -  The worksheet indicates whether each excess or deficient ADIT amounts are protected (i.e., subject to normalization rules of a taxing jurisdiction) or unprotected (i.e., not subject to normalization rules of a taxing jurisdiction).  To the extent that normalization requirements apply to ADIT remeasurements, additional computations (e.g., proration of excess deferred tax activity related to future test periods) may be necessary.

Note 3 -
Note 4  -  Column J is the difference between actual monthly and projected monthly activity (Column I minus Column C).  Specifically, if projected and actual activity are both positive, a negative in Column J represents over-projection (i.e., the amount of projected activity that did not occur) and a positive in Column J represents under-projection (i.e., the excess of actual activity over projected activity). If projected and actual activity are both negative, a negative in Column J represents under-projection (i.e., the excess of actual activity over projected activity) and a positive in Column J represents over-projection (i.e., the amount of projected activity that did not occur).

Note 5  -  Column K preserves the effects of excess ADIT proration from the projected revenue requirement when actual monthly excess ADIT activity and projected monthly excess ADIT activity are either both increases or decreases.  Specifically, if Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was over-projected, enter Column G x [Column I / Column C].  If Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was under-projected, enter the amount from Column G and complete Column L).  In other situations, enter zero.

Note 6  -  Column L applies when (1) Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was under-projected AND (2) actual monthly and projected monthly activity are either both increases or both decreases.  Enter 50 percent of the amount from Column J.  In other situations, enter zero.  The excess ADIT activity in column L is multiplied by 50 percent to reflect averaging of rate base to the extent that the proration requirement has not been applied to a portion of the monthly excess ADIT activity.

Note 7  -  Column M applies when (1) projected monthly activity was an increase while actual monthly activity was a decrease OR (2) projected monthly activity was a decrease while actual monthly activity was an increase.  Enter 50 percent of the amount of actual monthly activity (Column I).  In other situations, enter zero.  The excess ADIT activity in column M is multiplied by 50 percent to reflect averaging of rate base to the extent that the proration requirement has not been applied to a portion of the monthly excess ADIT activity.

Note 8  -  Column N is computed by adding the balance at the end of the prior month to EITHER (1) the sum of prorated monthly excess ADIT activity, if any, from Column K and the portion of monthly excess ADIT activity, if any, from Column L OR (2) the portion of monthly excess ADIT activity in Column M.

DESERTLINK, LLC
[PRO FORMA] LARGE LOAD COST RECOVERY AGREEMENT

This Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of this __ day of _______ 20  , by and between [________], a [●] and an Eligible Customer under the CAISO Tariff (“Eligible Customer”), and DesertLink, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“DesertLink” or “Transmission Owner”). DesertLink and Eligible Customer are referred to collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

[_______], a [●] (“Large Load Customer”), executes the Limited Acknowledgment set forth below solely for the purposes stated therein and is not a Party to the wholesale payment obligations established by this Agreement.

RECITALS

WHEREAS, DesertLink is a transmission-only company established to develop, own, and operate transmission facilities (“Transmission Facilities”) pursuant to the provisions of its Transmission Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”) and the California Independent System Operator Corporation (“CAISO”) Open Access Transmission Tariff (“CAISO Tariff”);

WHEREAS, Eligible Customer is eligible to take transmission service under the CAISO Tariff and does or will take such service on behalf of the Large Load Customer, whether or not Eligible Customer owns or operates an electric distribution system;

WHEREAS, Eligible Customer and Transmission Owner are parties to, or are entering into, an Eligible Customer for Large Load (“ECLL”) Interconnection Agreement or Transmission System Wholesale Load (“TSWL”) Interconnection Agreement (each, an “Interconnection Agreement”) concerning the Large Load Facility;

WHEREAS, Large Load Customer owns, operates, or proposes to develop the Large Load Facility identified in Schedule 1;

WHEREAS, the Eligible Customer has submitted an ECLL Interconnection Application or TSWL Interconnection Application for the interconnection of the Large Load Facility as a new or incremental load;

WHEREAS, Eligible Customer intends to procure transmission service pursuant to the CAISO Tariff and its associated schedules on behalf of Large Load Customer; WHEREAS, in connection with the Large Load Facility, Transmission Owner must make additions and/or modifications to its transmission system, including the Large Load-Driven Upgrades identified in Schedule 1;

WHEREAS, CAISO may, under the CAISO Tariff or a Commission-accepted
methodology, formally assign to the Large Load Facility a specific share of the costs or revenue requirement of a regional transmission project, and the Parties intend this Agreement to address

PDF page 288

2

that assigned share without changing any allocation otherwise established under the CAISO Tariff;

WHEREAS, the applicable studies may identify impacts on transmission systems other than DesertLink’s transmission system and may identify Affected System Upgrades necessary to accommodate or mitigate such impacts;

WHEREAS, Eligible Customer is responsible for entering into and maintaining the arrangements, payment obligations, and financial security or credit support required by each applicable Affected System Owner to ensure that costs and financial risks associated with Affected System Upgrades are not shifted to customers that did not cause those costs; WHEREAS, Transmission Owner, Eligible Customer, and Distribution Utility have executed or expect to execute an engineering and procurement agreement and/or an Interconnection Agreement governing the design, construction, and interconnection of the Transmission Owner’s facilities to the Distribution Utility’s facilities, including the Network Upgrades, required to support service of the Large Load Facility;

WHEREAS, the Parties enter into this Agreement to establish the Eligible Customer’s wholesale revenue-support and security obligations associated with the Large Load Facility and the Large Load-Driven Upgrades, without establishing or prescribing the retail rates, charges, or recovery arrangements between Eligible Customer and Large Load Customer;

WHEREAS, the Commission has recognized that the framework under which CAISO provides transmission service is unique and that certain responsibilities fall to the Participating Transmission Owners, Cal. Indep. Sys. Operator Corp., 195 FERC ¶ 61,214, at P 37 (2026), and this Agreement is the form of agreement established under Sections 10.9 and 10A.6 of the TO Tariff to secure Eligible Customer’s minimum contribution toward Transmission Owner’s transmission revenue requirement;

WHEREAS, CAISO is not a party to this Agreement; this Agreement does not create any obligation of CAISO, including any obligation to provide settlement, metering, billing, resettlement, or allocation data, which arises, if at all, under the CAISO Requirements; and DesertLink shall recover the costs of the Covered Upgrades through its Formula Rate and shall flow TRBAA Credits, including any adjustment resulting from the resolution of a dispute under this Agreement, through to transmission customers through its TRBAA;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises and covenants set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties intending to be legally bound, agree as follows:

1. Recitals. The statements set forth in the recitals above are hereby incorporated herein into the terms and conditions of this Agreement as if fully set forth herein.

PDF page 289

3

2. Definitions
Capitalized terms not defined herein have the meanings given in the CAISO Tariff, the DesertLink TO Tariff Formula Rate Implementation Protocols in Appendix IV of the TO Tariff (“Protocols”), or the relevant Interconnection Agreement.

2.1.
“Affected System” means an electric transmission system, other than DesertLink’s transmission system, that an applicable study determines may be materially affected by the interconnection or service of the Large Load Facility, including the transmission system of another Participating TO or a transmission system outside the CAISO Controlled Grid.

2.2.
“Affected System Arrangement” means an executed agreement or other binding arrangement entered into by Eligible Customer with an Affected System Owner that establishes the applicable study, engineering, design, procurement, construction, ownership, cost responsibility, cancellation-cost, revenue-support, payment, financial security or credit support, true-up, and other obligations associated with an Affected System Upgrade.

2.3.
“Affected System Owner” means the owner or operator responsible for an Affected System.

2.4.
“Affected System Upgrade” means an addition, modification, or upgrade to an Affected System that an applicable study determines is necessary to accommodate or mitigate an impact caused, in whole or in part, by the interconnection or service of the Large Load Facility.

2.5.
“Annual MTRC” means the annual Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution for a Covered Upgrade, calculated solely under the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5. Before the Final MTRC Determination Date for a Covered Upgrade, the Annual MTRC is the Estimated Annual MTRC. On and after that date, it is the Final Annual MTRC fixed under Section 6.3. Each Annual MTRC is levelized over a twenty (20)-year MTRC Term beginning on the applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In-Service Date, as applicable. The Annual MTRC is not an input to, or calculation made under, DesertLink’s annual Formula Rate update. 2.6.

“Annual Termination Fee Credit” means the annual amount of a Termination Fee Balance included in the TRBAA under Section 3.3.4.

2.7.
“Applicable Allocation Percentage” has the meaning set forth in Section 6.3.3. 2.8.

“Applicable Laws and Regulations” means all duly promulgated applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, rules, ordinances, codes, decrees, judgments, directives, judicial or administrative orders, permits, and other duly authorized actions of any Governmental Authority.

2.9.
“Applied Security Proceeds” means proceeds of Operational Security that Transmission Owner has applied under Section 7.6 to an identified Supplemental

PDF page 290

4

MTRC, prior-period true-up adjustment, Termination Fee, or other payment obligation arising under Article 6 or Section 3.3.4. Proceeds of Construction Security applied to Pre-In-Service Termination Costs or other construction-related obligations are not Applied Security Proceeds and shall be treated as provided in Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3. 2.10. “ARR” means annual revenue requirement.

2.11. “Break-Even” has the meaning set forth in Section 6.7.
2.12. “Business Day” means a Business Day as defined in Appendix A to the CAISO Tariff, as amended from time to time.

2.13. “CAISO-Assigned Regional Project” means a regional transmission project approved or designated through a CAISO Tariff process for which CAISO, under the CAISO Tariff or a Commission-accepted methodology, formally assigns a specific percentage or amount of project costs or revenue requirement to the Large Load Facility. The project and assignment must be identified in Schedule 4. A project’s regional designation, general system benefit, or inclusion in a CAISO transmission plan, without a specific assignment to the Large Load Facility, does not by itself make the project a CAISO-Assigned Regional Project.

2.14. “CAISO Requirements” means the CAISO Tariff, the Transmission Control Agreement, any other agreement to which CAISO is a party that is on file with or accepted by the Commission, and any Commission order, regulation, or Commission- accepted methodology applicable to CAISO, each as amended from time to time, together with any CAISO business practice manual or procedure to the extent it implements any of the foregoing.

2.15. “Calendar Day” means every day, including Saturdays, Sundays, federal holidays, and other holidays.

2.16. “Construction Security” has the meaning set forth in Section 7.1. 2.17. “Covered Upgrade” means each Large Load-Driven Upgrade and each DesertLink- owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project share that is included in Schedule 1 or Schedule 4, as applicable, and for which an Annual MTRC is established under this Agreement.

2.18. “Credit Review Event” means a payment default, credit rating downgrade of the Eligible Customer or an issuing bank that has not yet triggered a Material Adverse Credit Event, a notice of nonrenewal of a Letter of Credit, or another event that, in DesertLink’s reasonable judgment, warrants updated credit information. A Credit Review Event does not, by itself, require delivery of additional Security absent a resulting shortfall.

2.19. “Cumulative Revenue Ledger” means the customer-, Large Load Facility-, project-, and Covered Upgrade-specific record maintained by DesertLink under Section 6.7. The Cumulative Revenue Ledger shall identify the applicable Total Required Revenue

PDF page 291

5

Commitment, Annual MTRC, Qualifying Transmission Revenues, Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds, effective prospective reassignments, other permitted adjustments, and the resulting Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and Required Operational Security.

2.20. “Cumulative Revenue Responsibility” or “Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility” means the Total Required Revenue Commitment less amounts that have satisfied that commitment under Section 6.7.

2.21. “Dispute Determination” has the meaning set forth in Section 11.5. 2.22. “Distribution Utility” means the public utility, municipal utility, cooperative, or other entity that owns, operates, or is responsible for the distribution facilities to which the Large Load Facility is interconnected or proposed to be interconnected, including its successors and permitted assigns.

2.23. “Effective Date” has the meaning set forth in Section 3.1.
2.24. “Estimated Annual MTRC” means the annual MTRC for a Covered Upgrade calculated from the then-current estimated capital cost using the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5. DesertLink may update the Estimated Annual MTRC as costs change during construction, including when DesertLink requires additional Construction Security.

2.25. “Event of Default” has the meaning set forth in Section 7.11.
2.26. “Final Annual MTRC” means the fixed Annual MTRC for a Covered Upgrade established on the Final MTRC Determination Date using final incurred capital cost and the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate calculated under the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5, including the agreed five percent (5%) annual levelized-depreciation schedule over the twenty (20)-year MTRC Term. The Final Annual MTRC is not recalculated through DesertLink’s Formula Rate or Protocols and may be recalculated only as provided in Section 6.3.1.

2.27. “Final MTRC Determination Date” means the date on which DesertLink establishes the Final Annual MTRC for a Covered Upgrade, which shall occur within one (1) year after the applicable Covered Upgrade enters service, when the actual capital cost of that Covered Upgrade is known and all costs associated with its estimated capital cost have been accounted for.

2.28. “Force Majeure” means any cause beyond the reasonable control of the Party claiming, and without the fault or negligence of such Party, which materially prevents or impairs the performance of such Party’s obligations hereunder, including but not limited to landslides, storms, ice storms, flood, drought, tornado, hurricane, lightning, earthquake, fire, explosion, failure or imminent threat of failure of facilities, supply chain issues, civil disturbance, strike, or other labor disturbance, sabotage, vandalism,

PDF page 292

6

riot, terrorism, blockade, insurrection, war, national emergency, or restraint by any Governmental Authority.

2.29. “Forecast TRBAA Credit” has the meaning set forth in Section 6.8. 2.30. “Formula Rate” means DesertLink’s transmission formula rate template and associated provisions in the TO Tariff, as accepted by the Commission and amended from time to time.

2.31. “Governmental Authority” means any federal, state, local, or other governmental, regulatory, or administrative agency, court, commission, department, board, legislature, rulemaking body, tribunal, or other governmental authority having jurisdiction over a Party, the Large Load Facility, any Large Load-Driven Upgrade, or the services or obligations addressed by this Agreement.

2.32. “Initial Allocation Percentage” has the meaning set forth in Section 6.3.2. 2.33. “Large Load-Driven Upgrades” means the transmission facilities owned or to be constructed by DesertLink and identified in Schedule 1 that the applicable study determines are driven in whole or in part by the Large Load Facility, alone or together with one or more other large loads. Large Load-Driven Upgrades do not include Affected System Upgrades or any facilities whose costs are directly assigned to and paid by Eligible Customer under an Interconnection Agreement and are not included in DesertLink’s rate base. Where a Large Load-Driven Upgrade is an addition to or modification of a facility jointly owned by DesertLink and another entity, the Large Load-Driven Upgrade includes only DesertLink’s ownership share identified in Schedule 1.

2.34. “Large Load Facility” means the new or incremental load facility owned, operated, or proposed to be developed by Large Load Customer and identified in Schedule 1. 2.35. “Large Load Service Commencement Date” means the date on which the Large Load Facility first takes electric service through the CAISO Controlled Grid or otherwise begins receiving service under the applicable CAISO Tariff arrangement, as specified in Schedule 1. If the Large Load Facility is not reflected in a CAISO billing determinant used to assess TAC, Schedule 2 shall identify the applicable wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or other CAISO Tariff billing arrangement. 2.36. “Letter of Credit” means an irrevocable, transferable standby letter of credit issued for the benefit of DesertLink, meeting the requirements of Schedule 3. 2.37. “Material Adverse Credit Event” means any of the following: (a) a bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, or similar event described in Section 7.6(e); (b) a reduction in the long-term senior unsecured debt rating of the Eligible Customer or an issuing bank below the standards set out in Section 4 of Schedule 3; (c) loss, cancellation, material impairment, or expiration of Qualifying Retail Security Support without timely replacement; (d) an incorrect, expired, withdrawn, unavailable, or materially

PDF page 293

7

misleading Retail Security Certification, as described in Section 7.7 of this Agreement; or (e) another event that, in DesertLink’s reasonable judgment, materially impairs Eligible Customer's ability to perform its payment or Security obligations under this Agreement.

2.38. “MTRC Term” means, with respect to each Covered Upgrade, the period beginning on and including the applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In- Service Date, as applicable, and ending on the day immediately preceding the twentieth (20th) anniversary of that in-service date (the “MTRC Term End Date”). The first and final Rate Years of the MTRC Term shall be prorated for partial-year service. 2.39. “MTRC Term End Date” has the meaning set forth in the definition of “MTRC Term.”

3. Effective Date, Term and Termination
3.1.
Effective Date. This Agreement shall become effective upon execution by the Parties, subject to acceptance by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”) (if applicable), or, if filed unexecuted, upon the date specified by FERC (the “Effective Date”).

3.2.
Term. This Agreement shall remain in effect from the Effective Date until DesertLink issues a final Reconciliation Statement determining that the Total Required Revenue Commitment for every Covered Upgrade has been satisfied, transferred to a successor, prospectively reassigned, or otherwise discharged. The MTRC Term for each Covered Upgrade begins on its applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In- Service Date and ends on its applicable MTRC Term End Date. Earlier Break-Even remains available if the Total Required Revenue Commitment is satisfied before the applicable MTRC Term End Date. If DesertLink holds a Termination Fee Balance when the Total Required Revenue Commitment is otherwise discharged, this Agreement shall remain in effect for purposes of the Termination Fee Account

PDF page 296

10

provisions in Section 3.3.4 until the Termination Fee Balance has been fully credited or released.

3.3.
Termination. This Agreement may be terminated as follows:
3.3.1.
Termination Before the First Applicable In-Service Date. Before any Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date and before any DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project reaches its Regional Project In-Service Date, this Agreement may be terminated upon thirty (30) Calendar Days’ written notice if: (a) the Large Load Service Commencement Date has not occurred by the Outside Date; (b) Eligible Customer or Large Load Customer cancels or abandons the Large Load Facility or associated request for service; (c) the applicable interconnection, access to the CAISO Controlled Grid, or other arrangement necessary for the Large Load Facility is terminated; (d) an Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, or DesertLink exercises a termination right arising from default under this Agreement or an applicable interconnection or transmission service agreement; or (e) Eligible Customer fails to timely execute, maintain, or provide the documentation, financial security, or credit support required under Sections 4.2, 6.3.6, or 7.1, and such failure continues for ten (10) Business Days after written notice from DesertLink or cannot reasonably be cured by the date on which DesertLink must commence or continue physical construction or incur a material noncancelable procurement or construction commitment. Any such termination shall be subject to Applicable Laws and Regulations and any required Commission authorization or acceptance and shall not release or limit the obligations described in Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3.

If any Large Load-Driven Upgrade has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date or any DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project has reached its Regional Project In-Service Date identified in Schedule 4, cancellation, abandonment, termination, or failure of the Large Load Facility to commence or continue service shall not terminate this Agreement. Section 3.3.4 and Articles 6 and 7 shall apply to each Large Load-Driven Upgrade and DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project for which the applicable in-service date has occurred. Section 6.3.6 shall govern any assigned share of a project owned by another entity.

3.3.2.
Pre-In-Service Termination Costs and Construction Security. If the Large Load Facility, its associated request for service, or any associated Large Load- Driven Upgrade is cancelled, abandoned, or otherwise terminated before an applicable Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date, Eligible Customer shall be responsible for all actual and reasonable costs prudently incurred or irrevocably committed by DesertLink with respect to that Large Load-Driven Upgrade that have not otherwise been recovered by DesertLink (“Pre-In-Service Termination Costs”). Pre-In-Service Termination Costs include costs incurred before or after the applicable cancellation,

PDF page 297

11

abandonment, or termination to wind down, secure, remove, or otherwise address the unfinished Large Load-Driven Upgrade.

Pre-In-Service Termination Costs include, as applicable:
(a) engineering, design, study, permitting, environmental, siting, land and land- right, procurement, construction, testing, project management, legal, regulatory, and administrative costs;

(b) vendor and contractor cancellation charges, termination charges, change- order costs, restocking charges, demobilization costs, contract closeout costs, and third-party claims;

(c) the costs of securing, preserving, mothballing, relocating, redeploying, dismantling, removing, transporting, storing, selling, or disposing of equipment, materials, and partially completed facilities;

(d) site restoration, environmental remediation, and the restoration or modification of DesertLink’s existing facilities made necessary by the cancellation or abandonment;

(e) Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (“AFUDC”) properly accrued in accordance with the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts through the date on which the applicable construction activities cease or the applicable project is determined to have been abandoned, excluding AFUDC associated with amounts of Construction Work in Progress included in rate base or otherwise recovered through rates; and

(f) any other costs reasonably incurred by DesertLink as a direct result of the cancellation, abandonment, suspension, or termination.

DesertLink may draw upon and apply Construction Security to Pre-In-Service Termination Costs as such costs are incurred or the associated obligations become fixed and payable. DesertLink may retain Construction Security until all Pre-In-Service Termination Costs are reasonably determinable and DesertLink has served on Eligible Customer a final statement reconciling Pre-In-Service Termination Costs, Construction Security applied, and the recoveries described in this Section, together with supporting information (the “Termination Cost Reconciliation”). Construction Security does not limit Eligible Customer’s underlying liability. Eligible Customer shall pay any deficiency within ten (10) Business Days after receipt of the Termination Cost Reconciliation. The Termination Cost Reconciliation shall become final in the same manner and within the same period as a Reconciliation Statement under Section 6.6, and DesertLink shall release any excess Construction Security after the Termination Cost Reconciliation becomes final, including through resolution of any dispute under Article 11. Construction Security applied under this Section does not constitute Applied Security Proceeds and does not produce a TRBAA Credit except to the extent provided in Section 3.3.3(d). Nothing in this Agreement limits DesertLink’s right to seek recovery of unpaid Pre-In-Service Termination Costs through its Formula Rate or otherwise as the Commission may authorize.

PDF page 298

12

DesertLink shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate Pre-In-Service Termination Costs, provided that DesertLink shall not be required to take any action inconsistent with prudent utility practice, safety requirements, Applicable Laws and Regulations, existing contractual obligations, or the reliable operation of its transmission facilities. The Termination Cost Reconciliation shall reflect, when realized, applicable vendor refunds, insurance recoveries, net salvage proceeds, reuse or redeployment credits, and other recoveries attributable to the cancelled or abandoned scope, but shall not credit amounts representing DesertLink’s lawfully earned return or carrying costs except to the extent necessary to prevent duplicate recovery.

This Section applies separately to each Large Load-Driven Upgrade. If one or more Large Load-Driven Upgrades have reached their Upgrade In-Service Dates when the Large Load Facility or associated request for service is cancelled, this Section shall apply only to the Large Load-Driven Upgrades and portions of the project that have not reached their Upgrade In-Service Dates. The treatment of each Large Load-Driven Upgrade that has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date shall be governed by Section 3.3.4 and Articles 6 and 7.

3.3.3.
Rate Base and Formula Rate Treatment Before an Upgrade In-Service Date. To the extent costs associated with a cancelled or abandoned Large Load- Driven Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date have been included in Construction Work in Progress or any other component of DesertLink’s rate base, DesertLink shall, consistent with the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts, its Formula Rate and Protocols, and other Applicable Laws and Regulations:

(a) remove, reclassify, or otherwise exclude such costs from rate base to the extent required by applicable Commission accounting and ratemaking requirements;

(b) reflect that treatment in the next practicable Annual Update and corresponding true-up;

(c) cease accruing AFUDC to the extent and at the time required by the Commission’s accounting requirements; and

(d) make any adjustment or credit necessary to prevent DesertLink from recovering the same cost both through Construction Security or another payment by Eligible Customer and through its Formula Rate; provided that any such credit to transmission customers shall be recorded in the TRBA and flowed through to transmission customers through the TRBAA as provided in Section 6.8, and not through a revenue credit or other input to the Formula Rate.

Any depreciation, amortization, or other amount recovered through DesertLink’s Formula Rate that represents recovery of the same underlying capital or expense included in Pre-In-Service Termination Costs shall be reflected, without duplication, in the Termination Cost Reconciliation under Section 3.3.2. Application of Construction Security shall not require DesertLink to refund or

13

surrender any return, carrying cost, tax allowance, or other amount lawfully recovered for a period during which DesertLink’s investment was properly included in rate base, except to the extent necessary to prevent duplicate recovery.

This Section 3.3.3 applies only to a Large Load-Driven Upgrade, or portion thereof, that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date.

3.3.4.
Effect of Cancellation After an Upgrade or Regional Project In-Service Date. After any Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date or any DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project reaches its Regional Project In-Service Date specified in Schedule 4, Eligible Customer shall promptly notify DesertLink if Eligible Customer or Large Load Customer anticipates or becomes aware of the cancellation, abandonment, downsizing, curtailment, permanent cessation, or material reduction of service at the Large Load Facility.

Cancellation, abandonment, suspension, downsizing, termination, or failure of the Large Load Facility to commence or continue service shall not, by itself:

(a) terminate this Agreement;
(b) require the removal from rate base of a Large Load-Driven Upgrade or a DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project that has reached its in- service date;

(c) reduce or cap any Annual MTRC, Regional Project Allocated ARR, Total Required Revenue Commitment, or remaining Cumulative Revenue

Responsibility; or
(d) terminate, reduce, or excuse Eligible Customer’s obligation to pay the Supplemental MTRC and prior-period true-up adjustments under Section 6.6, maintain and replenish Operational Security, or satisfy the remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility.

Upon any effective termination of this Agreement, or upon the permanent cessation of service by the Large Load Facility following an applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In-Service Date, Eligible Customer shall pay DesertLink a one-time lump-sum termination fee equal to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, less any Supplemental MTRC that has been billed and remains unpaid as of the effective termination or cessation date (the “Termination Fee”). DesertLink shall calculate the Termination Fee separately for each Covered Upgrade that has reached its applicable in-service date from the most recently served Cumulative Revenue Ledger, updated through the effective termination or cessation date for then-known Qualifying Transmission Revenues, Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds, billed and unpaid Supplemental MTRC, and any effective prospective reassignment. Billed and unpaid Supplemental MTRC excluded from the Termination Fee remains separately payable and secured; its later payment, satisfaction through Applied Security Proceeds, or direct recovery shall reduce the Cumulative Revenue

14

Responsibility. The Termination Fee is due thirty (30) Calendar Days after DesertLink’s invoice. It is an accelerated contractual termination charge, not a penalty or consideration for future transmission service. Its receipt in full discharges only the remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility included in the fee. The Termination Fee is not a Supplemental MTRC Receipt, Applied Security Proceeds, prepayment for future transmission service, customer advance for construction, contribution in aid of construction, or reduction to rate base. DesertLink shall administer the Termination Fee only as provided in Section 3.3.4 and Article 6.

Each Large Load-Driven Upgrade that has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date and each DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project for which an Annual MTRC has been established shall remain subject to the applicable Formula Rate and Protocols for so long as it is properly includable in rate base under applicable Commission requirements. The associated payment, Security, reconciliation, and TRBAA Credit obligations shall continue in accordance with Articles 6 and 7, subject to any prospective reassignment or adjustment authorized under the CAISO Tariff or a Commission-accepted methodology, or transfer to a Successor Eligible Customer under Section 6.10.

DesertLink shall hold each Termination Fee, and any proceeds of Operational Security applied to its payment, in a separately identified, interest bearing Termination Fee Account for the applicable Covered Upgrade. The amounts in that account, together with actual earnings and less amounts credited or released, constitute the “Termination Fee Balance.” For each Covered Upgrade, the Annual Termination Fee Credit for each Rate Year remaining in the MTRC Term shall equal the applicable Annual MTRC, prorated for any partial Rate Year, but shall not exceed the then-available Termination Fee Balance. In the final Rate Year of the MTRC Term, the Annual Termination Fee Credit shall include the entire remaining Termination Fee Balance, including actual earnings, so that the Termination Fee Account is reduced to zero, subject to any amount required to be released under this Section 3.3.4. DesertLink shall include each Annual Termination Fee Credit in the TRBAA only for the Rate Year for which it is scheduled. The Termination Fee Balance shall be separately accounted for as a deferred liability pending its scheduled annual TRBAA treatment, shall not be included in rate base, and shall not itself be a TRBAA Credit or Formula Rate input. If a prospective reassignment becomes effective after receipt of a Termination Fee, DesertLink shall release the portion of the Termination Fee Balance attributable to the reassigned responsibility, together with actual earnings, and prospectively adjust the remaining Annual Termination Fee Credits.

If the Commission subsequently requires DesertLink to retire, remove, reclassify, or exclude all or a portion of an in-service Large Load-Driven Upgrade or DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project from rate base, DesertLink shall make corresponding prospective adjustments to the applicable Annual MTRC, Regional Project Allocated ARR, Total Required Revenue

Commitment, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, Supplemental MTRC, and Operational Security. Such adjustments shall prevent Eligible Customer from remaining responsible under this Agreement for costs that are no longer included in DesertLink’s transmission revenue requirement, without requiring a refund or reopening of amounts properly determined for a prior Rate Year.

If, at the time of cancellation or abandonment, one or more Large Load-Driven Upgrades have reached their Upgrade In-Service Dates or a DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project has reached its project in-service date, and one or more other upgrades or project shares have not, Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3 shall apply to Large Load-Driven Upgrades and project scope that have not reached their applicable in-service dates; this Section 3.3.4 and Articles 6 and 7 shall apply to the upgrades and DesertLink-owned project shares that have reached their applicable in-service dates; and Section 6.3.6 shall continue to govern any assigned share of a project owned by another entity.

3.3.5.
Mutual Termination. The Parties may terminate this Agreement by mutual written consent only after addressing all incurred construction costs, the continuing Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, Supplemental MTRC amounts, prior-period true-up adjustments, and Security. No termination is effective to extinguish such obligations unless expressly accepted or approved by FERC. 3.4.

Regulatory Effect of Termination. No termination shall become effective until the Parties comply with all Applicable Laws and Regulations, including any required notice to or acceptance by FERC. A regulatory rejection, cancellation, downsizing, curtailment, cessation, Force Majeure event, or termination shall not excuse incurred construction costs or the obligations arising on or after an applicable Upgrade In- Service Date or Regional Project In-Service Date unless FERC expressly determines otherwise.

3.5.
Effect of Termination. Termination does not release Eligible Customer from obligations arising under Articles 4, 6, or 7, including future annual Supplemental MTRC payments, prior-period true-up adjustments, and Security maintenance and replenishment, until the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility is finally satisfied or transferred in accordance with this Agreement. Upon DesertLink’s receipt of the Termination Fee in full, no further Supplemental MTRC shall accrue for any period after the effective termination or cessation date, subject to final true-ups and reconciliation for periods before that date. Security does not limit the underlying liability. The Large Load Customer’s information, notice, authorization, and cooperation obligations stated in its Limited Acknowledgment also survive.

4. Transmission Project
4.1.
Design, Procurement, and Construction. Subject to Eligible Customer’s execution of this Agreement and the relevant Interconnection Agreement, delivery of Construction Security under Section 7.1, and satisfaction of Section 4.2, DesertLink shall design, procure, construct, install, and own the Large Load-Driven Upgrades

PDF page 302

16

described in the relevant Interconnection Agreement and Schedule 1, using reasonable efforts to meet the applicable construction schedule and expected Upgrade In-Service Dates.

Eligible Customer shall maintain Construction Security under Section 7.1 sufficient to secure DesertLink’s incurred and committed construction costs and the Pre-In-Service Termination Costs described in Section 3.3.2. Construction Security shall apply separately to each Large Load-Driven Upgrade until that upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date and the conditions for release or conversion under Section 7.2 have been satisfied.

If different Large Load-Driven Upgrades reach their Upgrade In-Service Dates on different dates, Construction Security shall continue to apply to each Large Load- Driven Upgrade and portion of the project that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date, notwithstanding the release or conversion of Construction Security attributable to an upgrade that has entered service.

Upon cancellation, abandonment, or termination, before an applicable Large Load- Driven Upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date, DesertLink may draw, retain, and apply Construction Security in accordance with Sections 3.3.2 and 7.1 and the relevant Interconnection Agreement. DesertLink shall not be required to take action inconsistent with its safety practices, design criteria, construction procedures, Applicable Laws and Regulations, or the reliable operation of its transmission facilities.

4.2.
Affected Systems
4.2.1. Identification and Coordination. Eligible Customer shall cooperate with DesertLink, CAISO, each affected Participating TO, and each other Affected System Owner in identifying and studying potential impacts of the interconnection or service of the Large Load Facility on any Affected System.

4.2.2. Required Affected System Arrangements. For each Affected System Upgrade identified through an applicable study, Eligible Customer shall timely enter into and maintain an Affected System Arrangement with the applicable Affected System Owner. Each Affected System Arrangement shall address, as applicable:

(a) study, engineering, design, procurement, construction, testing, and energization responsibilities;

(b) responsibility for the costs of the Affected System Upgrade;
(c) responsibility for cancellation, abandonment, demobilization, equipment removal, disposition, remediation, restoration, AFUDC, and other costs resulting from cancellation or failure of the Large Load Facility to proceed;

(d) construction-period and post-in-service payment obligations and financial security or credit support sufficient to protect the Affected System Owner and its other customers against cost shifting;

PDF page 303

17

(e) applicable invoicing, reconciliation, true-up, refund, and release procedures; and

(f) any Commission filing, acceptance, or other regulatory authorization required for the Affected System Arrangement.

4.2.3. Evidence Before DesertLink Construction. At least thirty (30) Calendar Days before DesertLink’s scheduled commencement of physical construction, and in all events before any notice to proceed for physical construction may occur or DesertLink incurs a material noncancelable procurement or construction commitment, Eligible Customer shall provide DesertLink:

(a) a complete copy of each executed Affected System Arrangement;
(b) evidence that all financial security or credit support required to be effective before construction under each Affected System Arrangement has been provided;

(c) evidence of any required Commission filing, acceptance, or other regulatory authorization; and

(d) a certification that each Affected System Arrangement remains in full force and effect and that Eligible Customer is not in default thereunder.

DesertLink may permit specifically identified preliminary engineering, procurement, or other limited activities to proceed before satisfaction of this Section by written notice. Such permission shall not waive any requirement of this Section or obligate DesertLink to commence or continue physical construction. 4.2.4. Continuing Obligation. Eligible Customer shall promptly provide DesertLink a copy of any material amendment, replacement, termination notice, default notice, demand upon financial security or credit support, or other material notice concerning an Affected System Arrangement. Eligible Customer shall maintain each required Affected System Arrangement and all financial security or credit support required thereunder until the obligations secured by that arrangement have been finally satisfied, transferred, or released.

4.2.5. Later-Identified Affected Systems. If an Affected System or Affected System Upgrade is identified after DesertLink has commenced work, Eligible Customer shall promptly enter into the required Affected System Arrangement and provide the documentation required by this Section. Subject to the applicable tariffs and agreements, DesertLink may suspend further work, procurement, energization, or service to the extent reasonably necessary to avoid additional exposure until the requirement is satisfied.

4.2.6. Failure to Satisfy Requirements. Eligible Customer’s failure to timely execute, maintain, or provide evidence of an Affected System Arrangement or required financial security or credit support constitutes a material default under this Agreement. Subject to Applicable Laws and Regulations and the applicable tariffs and agreements, DesertLink may: (a) decline to commence or continue construction or material procurement commitments; (b) suspend work, energization, or service;

PDF page 304

18

(c) exercise the termination right in Section 3.3.1; and (d) recover all resulting Pre- In-Service Termination Costs and other amounts payable under this Agreement. 4.2.7. Confidentiality. Documents provided under this Section shall be subject to the confidentiality protections in Section 6.12. Eligible Customer may redact commercially sensitive provisions unrelated to the requirements of this Section, but may not redact information reasonably necessary for DesertLink to verify the scope, effectiveness, cost responsibility, financial security or credit support, termination protection, or continuing enforceability of the Affected System Arrangement. 4.2.8. Separate Administration. Costs, revenues, payments, and financial security or credit support arising under an Affected System Arrangement shall be administered under that arrangement and the applicable Affected System Owner’s tariff. Such amounts shall not be included in any Annual MTRC, Total Required Revenue Commitment, Supplemental MTRC, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, or TRBAA Credit, except to the extent expressly authorized by the Commission and necessary to prevent duplicate recovery.

5. Regulatory Approval(s)
5.1.
FERC Filing. This Agreement is the form of agreement required under Sections 10.9 and 10A.6 of the TO Tariff as a condition of DesertLink’s design, procurement, and construction of Large Load-Driven Upgrades. Consistent with 18 C.F.R. § 35.1(g), a conforming, executed Agreement entered into under the Commission-accepted pro forma with populated Schedules generally shall not require an individual filing under Section 205 of the Federal Power Act. DesertLink shall file an unexecuted Agreement or an Agreement containing a material deviation, and any other agreement required to be filed by Commission order or rule. If FERC does not accept a required filing in its entirety, the Parties shall use reasonable efforts to amend and refile it; regulatory rejection does not excuse incurred construction costs or payment, Security, and true-up obligations for facilities placed in service, except to the extent FERC expressly determines otherwise.

6. Cost Recovery
6.1.
Cost Recovery and Minimum Contribution. DesertLink shall include the Large Load-Driven Upgrades in its Formula Rate to the extent the project costs are properly includable under the Formula Rate, the Protocols, and applicable law. This Agreement does not remove any Covered Upgrade from rate base or require a capital-cost reimbursement. The fixed twenty (20)-year Annual MTRC for each Covered Upgrade is instead calculated under the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5, initially using estimated cost and then using final incurred cost on the applicable Final MTRC Determination Date. DesertLink shall recover its formula-rate revenue requirement through TAC and shall flow TRBAA Credits through to transmission customers through the TRBAA as provided in Section 6.8. Amounts received under this Agreement are not inputs to the Formula Rate, and this Agreement does not require any modification of the Formula Rate. Eligible Customer shall pay a Supplemental

PDF page 305

19

MTRC only to the extent forecast or actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues are less than the applicable Annual MTRC. The Annual MTRC is a revenue floor, not an additive charge, and does not alter CAISO cost allocation or DesertLink plant accounting.

Eligible Customer acknowledges that DesertLink will incur costs and undertake planning, engineering, procurement, and construction in reliance on the Large Load Facility’s development and operation. Eligible Customer therefore accepts the wholesale payment and Security obligations in this Agreement. Any retail recovery from the Large Load Customer remains governed exclusively by applicable state law and Eligible Customer’s retail arrangements.

Affected System Upgrades and the associated costs, revenues, payments, and financial security or credit support are governed by Section 4.2 and the applicable Affected System Arrangement. Unless expressly authorized by the Commission, no Affected System Upgrade or associated revenue requirement shall be included in DesertLink’s Annual MTRC, Total Required Revenue Commitment, Supplemental MTRC, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, or TRBAA Credit.

6.2.
Qualifying Transmission Revenues. For each Rate Year or partial Rate Year, “Qualifying Transmission Revenues” means wholesale transmission revenues paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer under the CAISO Tariff or another Commission- accepted arrangement that are attributable to service to the Large Load Facility and reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. Qualifying Transmission Revenues include: (a) the portion of TAC revenue attributable to the Large Load Facility and allocable to DesertLink under the reproducible methodology in Schedule 2; and (b) Wheeling Access Charges and other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission-service charges paid to CAISO, a Participating TO, or a non-PTO transmission or load-serving entity for deliveries serving the Large Load Facility, but only to the extent they reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected through TAC or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement and are not otherwise reflected as a credit in calculating the Annual MTRC, the Supplemental MTRC, or a TRBAA Credit. Qualifying Transmission Revenues do not include Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds, retail charges, or amounts that do not reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement.

6.3.
Annual MTRC and Allocation.
6.3.1. Upgrade-Specific MTRC Calculation. DesertLink shall calculate a separate Annual MTRC for each Covered Upgrade solely under the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5. Before the Final MTRC Determination Date, DesertLink shall calculate and update the Estimated Annual MTRC from the then-current estimated capital cost. Within one (1) year after the applicable Covered Upgrade enters service, when the actual capital cost of that Covered Upgrade is known and all costs associated with its estimated capital cost have been accounted for,

PDF page 306

20

DesertLink shall establish the Final Annual MTRC using final incurred capital cost and the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate calculated under Schedule 5. Schedule 5 shall calculate the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate by: (i) determining the present-worth revenue requirement using the applicable capital structure, cost of debt, return on equity, federal and state income-tax rates, income- tax conversion factor, and levelized-depreciation schedule; (ii) applying a depreciation rate of five percent (5%) of the applicable capital cost input in each year of the twenty (20)-year MTRC Term to calculate present-worth federal and state income-tax depreciation benefits; (iii) annualizing the resulting present-worth revenue requirement over the MTRC Term using the applicable after-tax discount rate and annualization factor; and (iv) adding the fixed expense allocator specified in Schedule 5. The Final Annual MTRC shall equal the applicable final incurred capital cost multiplied by the resulting Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate. No component reflected in the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate or the fixed expense allocator shall be added again as a separate component of the Annual MTRC. The Final Annual MTRC and the Schedule 5 inputs used to calculate it are fixed as of the Final MTRC Determination Date and shall not be recalculated for later changes in actual cost, Formula Rate inputs, or other cost-of- service components, except to correct an error or fraud, to implement an effective prospective reassignment, to implement a final FERC order applicable to the calculation, or to reflect, prospectively, a change in (i) DesertLink’s return on equity component of its Formula Rate, resulting from a final FERC order accepting or approving such change, or (ii) applicable federal or state income tax rates or income tax law enacted after the Final MTRC Determination Date; provided that, the five percent (5%) annual levelized-depreciation schedule in Schedule 5 shall remain fixed for the MTRC Term unless a final FERC order requires otherwise. If DesertLink adjusts the Final Annual MTRC after the Final MTRC Determination Date pursuant to the foregoing provision, DesertLink shall update the MTRC Calculation Template and serve it upon Eligible Customer in accordance with the notice provisions contained in this Agreement. Upon such service to Eligible Customer, the updated MTRC Calculation Template shall replace the existing MTRC Calculation Template in its entirety and become effective on the date of such service. The foregoing effectiveness of an updated MTRC Calculation Template does not preclude Eligible Customer from disputing any change to the MTRC Calculation Template pursuant to Article 11 of this Agreement. Any resulting adjustment to the Total Required Revenue Commitment shall apply only to the Rate Years remaining in the MTRC Term as provided in Section 6.7.

Each Annual MTRC shall apply for its separate twenty (20)-year MTRC Term, with the initial and final partial Rate Years prorated based on the number of monthly Billing Periods in the applicable Rate Year during which the Covered Upgrade is in service. Schedule 1 shall identify the initial Estimated Annual MTRC and initial projected Total Required Revenue Commitment for each Large Load-Driven Upgrade, and Schedule 5 shall record the Final MTRC Determination Date, Final Annual MTRC, Total Required Revenue Commitment, and the completed

calculation for each Covered Upgrade. Schedule 4 shall provide the corresponding

project-specific information for a DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project, if applicable.

6.3.2. Initial Allocation. Schedule 1 shall identify, separately for each Large Load- Driven Upgrade, the percentage of the upgrade initially allocated to the Large Load Customer under this Agreement (the “Initial Allocation Percentage”). The Initial Allocation Percentage shall be determined using the applicable final study and allocation methodology and shall account for:

(a) Large Load Customers studied individually, jointly, or in a cluster;
(b) the extent to which two or more Large Load Customers caused the need for or share a Large Load-Driven Upgrade;

(c) differing requested service levels, development phases, and facility configurations; and

(d) any portion of the facility determined at the outset to serve other transmission system needs or customers.

The aggregate percentages allocated to all Large Load Customers for a Large Load- Driven Upgrade shall not exceed one hundred percent (100%). Any portion not allocated to a Large Load Customer shall be excluded from the Annual MTRC allocable to any Large Load Customer and remain subject to the otherwise- applicable CAISO cost allocation and rate recovery requirements. 6.3.3. Applicable Allocation Percentage. For each Large Load-Driven Upgrade, the “Applicable Allocation Percentage” shall equal the Initial Allocation Percentage identified in Schedule 1, as adjusted prospectively by any reassignment effective under Section 6.9 or as otherwise required by a final Commission order or applicable tariff provision. A cancellation, abandonment, downsizing, curtailment, permanent cessation, or material reduction of service by the Large Load Customer shall not, by itself, reduce the Applicable Allocation Percentage. 6.3.4. Annual MTRC Allocation. The Annual MTRC applicable to Eligible Customer shall equal the Annual MTRC for the Covered Upgrade as a whole multiplied by the Applicable Allocation Percentage; provided that, where Schedule 5 applies that percentage to capital cost or otherwise calculates the Annual MTRC for an already allocated project share, the resulting Annual MTRC is already allocated and the percentage shall not be applied again. DesertLink shall maintain the calculation separately by Large Load Customer, Large Load Facility, and Covered Upgrade. The aggregate Annual MTRCs allocated to all large load customers shall not exceed the Annual MTRC for the Covered Upgrade as a whole.

6.3.5. CAISO-Assigned Regional Projects Owned by DesertLink. For each CAISO- Assigned Regional Project owned by DesertLink and included in its Formula Rate, DesertLink shall calculate separately the Regional Project Allocated ARR attributable to the specific share formally assigned to the Large Load Facility. The Regional Project Allocated ARR shall be calculated solely under the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5, using DesertLink’s allocated share of the

The resulting Annual MTRC shall be included in the Supplemental MTRC calculation and the Total Required Revenue Commitment beginning on the Regional Project In-Service Date. The allocated share shall be determined under the applicable allocation under the CAISO Tariff or Commission-accepted methodology and the project-specific information in Schedule 4. No portion assigned to other customers, other facilities, or broader regional needs shall be included. Before the Regional Project In-Service Date, any costs of a cancelled or abandoned project shall be treated under the applicable CAISO Tariff, Commission order, and any abandoned-plant incentive specifically authorized for that project. This Agreement does not create a separate pre-service payment or Construction Security obligation solely because CAISO has assigned a regional project share to Large Load Facility. Any pre-service payment, contribution, or security required by the CAISO Tariff, an applicable Interconnection Agreement, or another Commission-accepted arrangement remains due under that authority and shall be identified in Schedule 4. Any abandoned-plant recovery, customer payment, or security proceeds shall receive the accounting and rate treatment required by the Commission, and any credit necessary to prevent duplicate recovery of the same costs shall be recorded in the TRBA and flowed through to transmission customers through the TRBAA as provided in Section 6.8. Any prospective adjustment or reassignment of the share assigned to the Large Load Facility shall occur only as provided by the CAISO Tariff or a Commission- accepted methodology. Supplemental MTRC. Beginning on the in-service date of each Covered Upgrade, Eligible Customer shall pay the positive shortfall, if any, between the applicable Annual MTRC, prorated for a partial Rate Year based on the number of monthly Billing Periods in that Rate Year during which the Covered Upgrade is in service, and Qualifying Transmission Revenues attributable to the Large Load Facility during the corresponding Rate Year or partial Rate Year. Until the Final MTRC Determination Date, billing shall use the Estimated Annual MTRC. Upon initial finalization, the Final Annual MTRC shall apply back to the applicable in-service date, and estimated charges shall be reconciled in the next Reconciliation Statement under Section 6.6. Thereafter, the calculation shall use the Final Annual MTRC, subject to adjustments permitted by Section 6.3.1. Qualifying Transmission Revenues attributable to a specific Covered Upgrade shall be applied to that upgrade. Qualifying Transmission Revenues not attributable to a specific Covered Upgrade shall be allocated among the Covered Upgrades then in their MTRC Terms pro rata based on their respective prorated Annual MTRCs for the applicable period.

The calculation may be expressed as:
Supplemental MTRC = max (applicable Annual MTRC − Qualifying Transmission Revenues, $0).

The Annual MTRC is not an annual true-up of project cost or Formula Rate inputs. Annual reconciliation is limited to Qualifying Transmission Revenues, Supplemental MTRC invoices and receipts, Applied Security Proceeds, TRBAA Credits, partial-year

proration, effective prospective reassignment, and correction of error, fraud, a final FERC order applicable to the calculation, and any prospective recalculation of the Final Annual MTRC permitted by Section 6.3.1.

6.5.
Invoice. With each Annual Projection, DesertLink shall forecast Qualifying Transmission Revenues and calculate the projected Supplemental MTRC using the applicable fixed or estimated Annual MTRC from Schedule 5, increased or reduced by any prior-period true-up adjustment under Section 6.6. DesertLink shall invoice the forecasted Supplemental MTRC for the applicable Rate Year or partial Rate Year in equal monthly installments for each Billing Period in that Rate Year during which the Covered Upgrade is in service; for a full Rate Year, the projected Supplemental MTRC shall be invoiced in twelve (12) equal monthly installments. Each installment is payable within thirty (30) Calendar Days after receipt of the invoice. If a Covered Upgrade reaches its applicable in-service date during a Rate Year for which the Annual Projection did not include a projected Supplemental MTRC for that Covered Upgrade, DesertLink shall promptly forecast Qualifying Transmission Revenues and invoice the prorated Supplemental MTRC for the remaining Billing Periods of that Rate Year. DesertLink shall include the projected Supplemental MTRC, including any prior-period true-up adjustment, as a Forecast TRBAA Credit in the next annual TRBAA under Section 6.8. Only cash actually received by DesertLink, or Applied Security Proceeds actually applied by DesertLink, constitutes an actual receipt for purposes of Sections 6.6 through 6.8. Concurrently with each Annual Projection, DesertLink shall provide Eligible Customer upgrade-specific workpapers showing the applicable Annual MTRC, forecast Qualifying Transmission Revenues, projected Supplemental MTRC, any prior-period true-up adjustment, Forecast TRBAA Credit, Total Required Revenue Commitment, and Required Operational Security. 6.6.

Annual Reconciliation Statement. In connection with each Annual Update, DesertLink shall determine the actual Supplemental MTRC obligation using actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues and the applicable fixed or estimated Annual MTRC from Schedule 5. DesertLink shall identify, by Eligible Customer and Covered Upgrade, the opening unpaid billed Supplemental MTRC balance, Supplemental MTRC invoiced during the Rate Year, cash received by DesertLink, Applied Security Proceeds applied to identified obligations, direct recoveries, closing unpaid billed balance, and each Annual Termination Fee Credit. Concurrently with each Annual Update, DesertLink shall serve on Eligible Customer a Reconciliation Statement containing those determinations, the updated Cumulative Revenue Ledger, Required Operational Security recalculated under Section 7.4, a reconciliation of the Forecast TRBAA Credit to actual amounts recorded in the TRBA, and supporting workpapers. An unpaid Supplemental MTRC remains due from Eligible Customer and, when later received or satisfied through Applied Security Proceeds, is recorded in the TRBA only in the Rate Year of receipt or application. The Reconciliation Statement shall not reopen the Final Annual MTRC or Total Required Revenue Commitment except as expressly allowed by Section 6.3.1.

The difference between the Supplemental MTRC billed for a Rate Year, excluding any prior-period true-up adjustment included in that billing, and the actual Supplemental
