MTRC determined in the Reconciliation Statement for that Rate Year shall constitute a “prior-period true-up adjustment,” which shall increase (if under-billed) or reduce (if over-billed) the projected Supplemental MTRC invoiced under Section 6.5 following the next Annual Projection. If no further Supplemental MTRC will be invoiced under this Agreement, DesertLink shall invoice any under-billed amount, payable within thirty (30) Calendar Days after receipt of the invoice, and shall refund any over-billed amount to Eligible Customer within thirty (30) Calendar Days after service of the Reconciliation Statement. No interest shall accrue on the Supplemental MTRC or on any prior-period true-up adjustment, invoice, refund, or other adjustment of the Supplemental MTRC between DesertLink and Eligible Customer. Any refund to Eligible Customer of an amount previously recorded as a TRBAA Credit shall be reversed in the TRBA when paid, and any under-billed amount later received shall be recorded in the TRBA when received, in each case as provided in Section 6.8. Any amount returned by DesertLink to transmission customers through the TRBAA shall include interest as provided in Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff.

A Reconciliation Statement shall become final on the earlier of (a) Eligible Customer’s written acceptance of the Reconciliation Statement or (b) ninety (90) Calendar Days after service, unless before that date Eligible Customer serves a Notice of Dispute under Section 11.1 identifying with reasonable specificity the items disputed. If a Notice of Dispute is timely served, the undisputed portions of the Reconciliation Statement shall become final on the date that would otherwise apply, and the disputed items shall become final upon the applicable Dispute Determination under Section 11.5. A final Reconciliation Statement may be revised only to implement a Dispute Determination, to reflect CAISO resettlements or other corrected data as provided in Schedule 2, or to correct errors or fraud. Finality of a Reconciliation Statement under this Agreement does not affect the Commission’s review and approval of any TRBAA.

For purposes of this Agreement, Supplemental MTRC Receipts exclude Applied Security Proceeds. Applied Security Proceeds shall be counted only when DesertLink applies such proceeds to satisfy an identified payment obligation and shall reduce that obligation dollar-for-dollar. The posting, maintenance, replenishment, drawing, or holding of Security shall not, by itself, constitute a Supplemental MTRC Receipt, an Applied Security Proceed, satisfaction of the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, or a TRBAA Credit.

No amount shall be counted both as a Supplemental MTRC Receipt and as an Applied Security Proceed. If DesertLink receives payment of an obligation previously satisfied through Applied Security Proceeds, DesertLink shall not count the subsequent payment toward the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility or a TRBAA Credit and shall instead return the duplicative amount, release an equivalent amount of Security, or, with supporting notice to Eligible Customer, apply the amount to another then- outstanding obligation under this Agreement.

6.7.
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and Break-Even. DesertLink shall maintain a Cumulative Revenue Ledger for each Covered Upgrade and shall update it at least

PDF page 312

26

annually in connection with the Annual Update. DesertLink shall include an updated Cumulative Revenue Ledger statement, with supporting workpapers, in each Reconciliation Statement served on Eligible Customer under Section 6.6. For each Covered Upgrade, the Total Required Revenue Commitment equals the Final Annual MTRC multiplied by twenty (20), adjusted only for partial-year proration and any prospective recalculation of the Final Annual MTRC permitted by Section 6.3.1, which shall apply only to the Rate Years remaining in the MTRC Term after the recalculation takes effect. Until the Final MTRC Determination Date, the projected Total Required Revenue Commitment shall equal the Estimated Annual MTRC multiplied by twenty (20).

Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility equals the applicable Total Required Revenue Commitment less:

(a) cumulative Qualifying Transmission Revenues;
(b) cumulative Supplemental MTRC Receipts;
(c) cumulative Applied Security Proceeds;
(d) effective prospective reassignment credits; and
(e) cash amounts received and applied toward the Termination Fee, excluding any portion satisfied through Applied Security Proceeds already counted under clause (c).

Each dollar shall be entered in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger only once. Supplemental MTRC Receipts shall exclude Applied Security Proceeds. Applied Security Proceeds shall be entered only when applied to an identified Supplemental MTRC, prior-period true-up adjustment, Termination Fee, or other payment obligation under Article 6 or Section 3.3.4. Security that is posted, drawn but not applied, held as a deferred liability, replenished, replaced, or returned shall not reduce the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. Annual Termination Fee Credits and the corresponding Termination Fee Balance shall be separately identified in the Reconciliation Statement and in the workpapers required under Section 6.8 and shall not again reduce the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility.

If an amount previously credited in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger is subsequently refunded, reversed, disallowed, or otherwise ceases to satisfy the applicable obligation, DesertLink shall make a corresponding adjustment to the ledger, subject to the finality and no-revival provisions of this Section.

Cancellation, downsizing, curtailment, or departure does not extinguish the remaining responsibility. When a final Reconciliation Statement determines that the responsibility has reached zero (“Break-Even”), DesertLink shall terminate the operational payment and Security obligations and release any excess Security. Once finally satisfied, the responsibility shall not revive because of a later change in ROE, expense, load, forecast, or other Formula Rate input, subject only to final true-ups and correction of errors or fraud for periods before satisfaction.

TRBAA Credit and No Double Recovery. Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds other than Applied Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee, Annual Termination Fee Credits, and any duplicate-recovery credit under Section 3.3.3(d) or Section 6.3.5 shall be credited to transmission customers solely through the TRBAA and shall not be recorded as revenue credits in, or otherwise included as inputs to, the Formula Rate. In each annual TRBAA, DesertLink shall include as the Forecast TRBAA Credit: (a) the projected Supplemental MTRC for the following Rate Year, increased or reduced by any prior-period true-up adjustment invoiced under Section 6.5; and (b) for any Covered Upgrade with a Termination Fee Balance, the Annual Termination Fee Credit scheduled under Section 3.3.4 for the following Rate Year, prorated as applicable and limited to the available Termination Fee Balance. Applied Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee shall be deposited into and held in the Termination Fee Account under Section 3.3.4 and shall be credited to transmission customers solely through the applicable Annual Termination Fee Credits. The difference between the Forecast TRBAA Credit and those actual amounts shall be reflected in the principal balance of the TRBA and flowed through to transmission customers in a subsequent TRBAA. Interest on the TRBA balance shall be calculated as provided in Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff. Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall not be included again as a TRBAA Credit because they are already reflected in calculating the Supplemental MTRC.

Each dollar shall be included in a TRBAA Credit only once. A Forecast TRBAA Credit applies only to the forecast Rate Year and shall be reconciled through the TRBA to actual Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security Proceeds other than those applied to a Termination Fee, and Annual Termination Fee Credits, as applicable. TRBAA filing workpapers sufficient to permit transmission customers to verify the TRBAA Credits reflected in that TRBAA, which may present customer-specific information on an aggregated basis or be submitted subject to a request for privileged treatment under 18 C.F.R. § 388.112 or other appropriate confidentiality protections. 6.9.

Prospective Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility.
6.9.1. Eligibility for Reassignment of Revenue Responsibility. Whether or not the Large Load Customer remains in service, a portion of the prospective revenue responsibility associated with a Large Load-Driven Upgrade may be reassigned to a subsequent load customer if an objective transmission study conducted under the applicable tariff or study process determines that:

(a) the subsequent large load customer relies upon identifiable incremental capability created by the Large Load-Driven Upgrade; and

(b) that reliance avoids or reduces identifiable transmission upgrades that otherwise would have been required to provide the subsequent large load customer’s requested service.

Incidental power flows, generalized system benefits, or use of the transmission system that does not satisfy both requirements shall not support a reassignment. This Section 6.9 applies only to a load customer other than the Large Load Customer, at a facility other than the Large Load Facility. It does not apply to a transfer of ownership or operation of the Large Load Facility, a change in Eligible Customer, or an assignment of this Agreement, which are governed by Sections 6.10 and 10.1 and do not alter the Applicable Allocation Percentage or the Large Load-Driven Upgrades attributable to the Large Load Facility.

6.9.2. Reassignment Calculation. DesertLink shall determine the prospective reassignment separately for each Large Load-Driven Upgrade satisfying Section 6.9.1 (each, a “Shared Upgrade”). For each Shared Upgrade:

(a) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost shall equal the reasonable estimated cost of the transmission upgrades that would have been required for the subsequent large load customer absent the Shared Upgrade, less the reasonable estimated cost of any additional transmission upgrades required when the capability of the Shared Upgrade is considered;

(b) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall equal the portion of the Shared Upgrade’s net plant balance included in rate base immediately before the reassignment that remains assigned to the Large Load Customer under this Agreement;

(c) the Capability-Supported Amount shall equal the portion of the Remaining Allocated Net Plant reasonably attributable to the incremental capability of the Shared Upgrade actually relied upon by the subsequent large load customer; and

(d) the Reassigned Investment Amount shall equal the least of:

PDF page 315

29

(i) the Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost;
(ii) the Capability-Supported Amount; and
(iii) the Remaining Allocated Net Plant.
The Demonstrated Avoided Upgrade Cost, Capability-Supported Amount, and Remaining Allocated Net Plant shall be determined using a consistent cost basis and price year. If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is greater than zero, the Reassignment Percentage shall equal the Reassigned Investment Amount divided by the Remaining Allocated Net Plant, bounded between zero and one hundred percent (100%). If Remaining Allocated Net Plant is zero or negative, no Reassignment Percentage shall be calculated under this methodology; any reassignment shall require an applicable tariff methodology or Commission determination addressing that circumstance.

6.9.3. Prospective Adjustment of Revenue Responsibility. Beginning on the Reassignment Effective Date, the applicable Annual MTRC assigned to the Large Load Customer shall be prospectively reduced by the Reassignment Percentage applied to the Shared Upgrade. DesertLink shall record a separate effective prospective reassignment credit in the Cumulative Revenue Ledger equal to the Reassignment Percentage multiplied by the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility associated with the Shared Upgrade that remains assigned to the Large Load Customer immediately before the Reassignment Effective Date. That credit shall be the sole Cumulative Revenue Ledger adjustment for the reassigned responsibility. It shall not adjust the Total Required Revenue Commitment or result in a second reduction to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility or Required Operational Security for the same reassigned responsibility. DesertLink shall recalculate the Supplemental MTRC and Operational Security under this Agreement to reflect the reassignment. The Reassignment Effective Date shall be the latest of:

(a) the date the subsequent large load customer commences the service for which the Shared Upgrade provides the identified incremental capability;

(b) the effective date of a cost recovery agreement establishing the subsequent large load customer’s corresponding revenue responsibility;

(c) the date on which all Security required from the eligible customer serving the subsequent large load customer becomes effective; and

(d) the date on which the study and any other approvals required under the applicable tariff become final.

No reduction in the Large Load Customer’s Operational Security shall occur until the corresponding responsibility and required Security have become effective for the subsequent large load customer.

6.9.4. Prospective Treatment and Prevention of Duplicate Reassignment. A reassignment under this Section shall:

PDF page 316

30

(a) operate prospectively only and shall not produce a refund, credit, or reopening of amounts properly determined for a prior Rate Year;

(b) transfer prospective revenue responsibility only and shall not constitute a sale or transfer of transmission facilities, a transfer of plant ownership, a change in plant accounting, or a modification of any CAISO cost allocation;

(c) not exceed the prospective responsibility remaining under this Agreement for the Shared Upgrade; and

(d) not assign the same transmission capability, avoided upgrade cost, Annual MTRC, or Cumulative Revenue Responsibility to more than one large load customer.

DesertLink shall maintain an upgrade-specific reassignment ledger identifying the capability and responsibility assigned to each large load customer. Once responsibility has been effectively reassigned, that responsibility shall not revert to the Large Load Customer if the subsequent large load customer later terminates, reduces, or fails to commence service. The reassigned responsibility shall instead remain with the subsequent large load customer and the Eligible Customer responsible for its payment, subject to any further prospective reassignment permitted under the applicable agreement and tariff.

Any prospective reassignment, adjustment, or change in the cost share of a CAISO- Assigned Regional Project shall be recognized under this Agreement only to the extent authorized or required by the CAISO Tariff or a Commission-accepted methodology. DesertLink shall apply an effective change prospectively to the Regional Project Allocated ARR, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, Supplemental MTRC, TRBAA Credit, and Operational Security, and shall update Schedule 4 and the applicable workpapers. The change shall not assign the same project share to more than one customer or alter costs allocated to other customers under the CAISO Tariff.

6.10. Change in Eligible Customer. Cost responsibility is assigned to the Large Load Customer and Large Load Facility, as paid by the Eligible Customer then taking wholesale transmission service on behalf of the Large Load Customer and Large Load Facility. If the Eligible Customer serving a Large Load Customer or Large Load Facility changes, the Successor Eligible Customer must execute an assumption agreement covering the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and any outstanding obligations under Section 6.3.6, provide required Security, and become responsible on a date coordinated with CAISO billing before the prior Eligible Customer is released. Following the complete departure of the Large Load Customer, the last responsible Eligible Customer remains obligated unless responsibility is transferred under an applicable tariff or state-law mechanism, assumed by a successor, or prospectively reassigned as permitted under this Agreement and the CAISO Requirements. If ownership or operation of the Large Load Facility is transferred, Eligible Customer shall notify DesertLink within thirty (30) Calendar Days and shall cause the transferee to execute a Limited Acknowledgment in the form attached to this Agreement. The transfer shall not alter the Applicable Allocation Percentage, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, or Security obligations under this Agreement.

A sale, lease, or other transfer of the Large Load Facility, or of the Large Load Customer’s interest in such Large Load Facility, is not a reassignment under Section 6.9 and does not require a study under Section 6.9.1. Cost responsibility shall continue to follow the Large Load Facility, the transferee shall execute a Limited Acknowledgment substantially in the form included in this Agreement, and Eligible Customer shall remain responsible for its obligations under this Agreement unless they are transferred to a Successor Eligible Customer under this Section 6.10. 6.11. CAISO Data and Settlement Coordination. Eligible Customer shall provide DesertLink, or authorize and direct its Scheduling Coordinator, Utility Distribution Company, Metering Coordinator, and other applicable entities to provide DesertLink, with the metering, settlement, billing, resettlement, allocation, and other data reasonably necessary to calculate and verify Qualifying Transmission Revenues and administer this Agreement. Eligible Customer shall execute any authorization or data- release documentation reasonably necessary for DesertLink to obtain such information.

To the extent authorized or required by the CAISO Tariff, CAISO may provide or make available relevant settlement, metering, billing, resettlement, and allocation data as provided under the CAISO Requirements. Nothing in this Agreement, however, imposes an obligation on CAISO or makes CAISO a party to this Agreement. DesertLink and Eligible Customer shall cooperate with CAISO and other applicable entities to establish and maintain the billing identifiers, metering points, data exchanges, and authorizations identified in Schedule 2.

DesertLink shall calculate Qualifying Transmission Revenues, the Annual MTRC, and the Supplemental MTRC; maintain the Cumulative Revenue Ledger; and serve on Eligible Customer the Reconciliation Statement, including the Cumulative Revenue Ledger statement, required by Sections 6.6 and 6.7.

If final data are not available when a calculation is required, DesertLink may use reasonable estimates based on the best information then available, subject to reconciliation under Section 6.6 when final or corrected data become available. 6.12. Information Rights and Confidentiality. Upon reasonable request, DesertLink shall provide Eligible Customer the workpapers, data, and other information reasonably necessary to verify the identification of Large Load-Driven Upgrades and CAISO- Assigned Regional Projects and all calculations of each Annual MTRC, Regional Project Allocated ARR, Total Required Revenue Commitment, Qualifying Transmission Revenues, Supplemental MTRC, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, TRBAA Credits, reassignment, and Security under this Agreement. Any dispute concerning those matters shall be resolved under Article 11. Large Load Customer and any Successor Eligible Customer may participate in a dispute under Article 11 to the extent the dispute affects its obligations under this Agreement or its Limited Acknowledgment. Customer-specific information shall be protected under Section 16.3 of the TO Tariff, the CAISO Tariff, and any applicable confidentiality agreement.

7. Security and Payment Obligations
7.1.
Construction Security. Before an applicable Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date, Eligible Customer shall maintain Construction Security under the relevant agreement sufficient to secure:

(a) DesertLink’s incurred and irrevocably committed engineering, design, procurement, permitting, construction, testing, and related costs attributable to that upgrade; and

(b) the Pre-In-Service Termination Costs described in Section 3.3.2, including properly accrued AFUDC and applicable cancellation, demobilization,

equipment removal, disposition, remediation, and restoration costs
(“Construction Security”).
Construction Security secures, but does not limit, Eligible Customer’s liability for those amounts. Construction Security provided under the relevant Interconnection Agreement or an engineering and procurement agreement for the same costs shall count toward, and shall not be duplicated by, the Construction Security required under this Agreement. Construction Security shall remain in effect for each Large Load- Driven Upgrade until that upgrade reaches its Upgrade In-Service Date and the applicable release or conversion conditions in Section 7.2 are satisfied. A Large Load-Driven Upgrade reaching its Upgrade In-Service Date shall not result in the release of Construction Security attributable to another Large Load-Driven Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date. Eligible Customer shall replenish Construction Security within ten (10) Business Days after notice of a permitted draw and supporting information if additional secured obligations remain and the remaining Construction Security is less than the amount required under this Section.

For a CAISO-Assigned Regional Project owned by DesertLink, any pre-service payment, contribution, or security required from Eligible Customer for its formally assigned share shall be provided only as required by the CAISO Tariff, an applicable Interconnection Agreement, or another Commission-accepted arrangement, and shall be identified in Schedule 4. This Agreement does not independently require pre- service Construction Security solely because CAISO has assigned a share of a regional project to the Large Load Facility. The treatment of costs for a cancelled or abandoned regional project shall be governed by Section 6.3.5 and the applicable Commission order, CAISO Tariff, and any project-specific abandoned-plant incentive authorized by the Commission. For a project owned by another entity, construction and operational security shall be provided under the CAISO Tariff or the arrangement required by Section 6.3.6 and Schedule 4; it shall not be treated as DesertLink Operational Security unless included in DesertLink’s Formula Rate and expressly identified as DesertLink’s share.

7.2.
Delivery of Operational Security. No later than thirty (30) Calendar Days before the earliest expected Upgrade In-Service Date identified in Schedule 1 or Regional Project

In-Service Date identified in Schedule 4 for a DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project, Eligible Customer shall deliver Operational Security calculated under this Article for the Large Load-Driven Upgrades and DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Project expected to enter service. Operational Security must be fully effective before any applicable Upgrade In-Service Date or Regional Project In-Service Date.

If different Large Load-Driven Upgrades or DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional Projects are expected to reach their applicable in-service dates on different dates, DesertLink shall recalculate the Required Operational Security before each subsequent in-service date to include the additional Cumulative Revenue Responsibility attributable to the upgrade or project share entering service. Eligible Customer shall provide any resulting increase no later than fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. Inclusion of pre-service Construction Work in Progress in rate base shall not constitute an Upgrade In-Service Date or independently trigger the Operational Security requirement. Construction Security shall remain applicable to each Large Load-Driven Upgrade that has not reached its Upgrade In-Service Date.

No Construction Security attributable to a Large Load-Driven Upgrade shall be released or converted unless:

(a) the Required Operational Security attributable to that upgrade is effective;
(b) that upgrade has reached its Upgrade In-Service Date; and
(c) DesertLink has determined that all Pre-In-Service Termination Costs and other construction-related obligations attributable to that upgrade have been paid or adequately reserved for.

Any portion of Construction Security retained for unresolved construction costs shall be released after DesertLink determines that those costs have been paid or adequately reserved for or, if Section 3.3.2 applies, after the Termination Cost Reconciliation becomes final. Failure to timely deliver Required Operational Security is a default permitting DesertLink, to the extent authorized by the applicable tariffs and agreements, to suspend energization or service, terminate applicable interconnection arrangements, and draw Construction Security for secured obligations. 7.3.

Required Operational Security. Required Operational Security shall equal one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue

Responsibility. DesertLink shall reduce that amount only by the portion of Qualifying Retail Security Support identified in a currently effective Retail Security Certification. A Retail Security Certification is accepted in reliance on Eligible Customer’s representations and does not require DesertLink to review the underlying retail- security documents in the ordinary course. If DesertLink has a reasonable basis to question the certification, or after a payment default, Credit Review Event, or Material Adverse Credit Event, DesertLink may request supporting information reasonably necessary to verify continued compliance. Any resulting deficiency shall be delivered

or restored within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier.

7.4.
Annual Resizing and Security Notices. DesertLink shall recalculate Required Operational Security with each Annual Projection, Final MTRC Determination Date, recalculation of a Final Annual MTRC under Section 6.3.1, Reconciliation Statement, effective prospective reassignment, replacement or expiration of Qualifying Retail Security Support, or Credit Review Event. If DesertLink reasonably determines that the Required Security Amount exceeds available Security, it may issue a Security Notice identifying the required increase or restoration and reasonable supporting detail then available. Eligible Customer shall provide the required increase or restoration within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier. A reduction shall be released only after the relevant calculation and reconciliation are final.

7.5.
Form of Operational Security. Except to the extent of currently effective Qualifying Retail Security Support, Eligible Customer shall provide direct Operational Security in the form of cash, an irrevocable standby Letter of Credit meeting Schedule 3, or any combination of cash and Letter of Credit. DesertLink may accept another form of Security that it determines, in its sole discretion, is acceptable.

Each Letter of Credit shall have an initial stated term of at least twelve (12) months and shall remain continuously effective until released under this Agreement; provided, however, that a Letter of Credit may have a stated expiration date before its release date if Eligible Customer timely extends or replaces it so that Security in an amount not less than the Required Security Amount remains continuously available to DesertLink.

If an issuing bank has the right not to renew a Letter of Credit, the Letter of Credit shall require the issuing bank to provide DesertLink and Eligible Customer at least ninety (90) Calendar Days’ prior written notice of nonrenewal. Eligible Customer shall provide a conforming extension or replacement Letter of Credit, or additional cash collateral or other Security accepted by DesertLink, no later than sixty (60) Calendar Days before the applicable expiration date.

If Eligible Customer fails to provide the required extension, replacement, or other Security by that deadline, DesertLink may, before the Letter of Credit expires, draw all or any portion of the then-available amount under the Letter of Credit and retain the proceeds as cash collateral, apply the proceeds to secured obligations, or both. Any proceeds retained but not applied shall continue to constitute Security until released under this Agreement.

7.6.
Draw and Application. DesertLink may draw against all or any portion of a Letter of Credit, apply cash collateral, or apply another form of Security accepted by DesertLink to secured obligations upon: (a) an unpaid Supplemental MTRC, true-up, Termination Fee, or other amount due after the applicable payment period; (b) Eligible Customer’s failure to timely deliver, maintain, replace, restore, or increase Security;

(c) cancellation, termination, withdrawal, abandonment, or permanent cessation of the Large Load Facility or a material breach of this Agreement; (d) a material inaccuracy in a Retail Security Certification or Security instrument; (e) Eligible Customer: (i) files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy or seeks reorganization, arrangement, or similar relief under any bankruptcy, insolvency, or debtor-relief law; (ii) becomes subject to an involuntary bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty

(60) Calendar Days; (iii) has a receiver, trustee, liquidator, or custodian appointed for it or a substantial portion of its assets, which appointment is not vacated within sixty

(60) Calendar Days; (iv) makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or (v) admits in writing its inability to pay debts as they become due; or (f) Eligible Customer fails to extend, replace, or otherwise maintain Security in the amount and within the time required by Section 7.5, including following a notice of nonrenewal, issuer rating reduction, or other event affecting the availability of a Letter of Credit. A draw shall not automatically require replenishment to the amount maintained immediately before the draw. Following any application of drawn proceeds to an amount due, DesertLink shall recalculate the remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and the Operational Security then required under this Article. Eligible Customer shall replenish only the amount, if any, by which the remaining Operational Security is less than the recalculated Required Security Amount, within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of a Security Notice, or by the applicable in-service date if earlier.

Proceeds drawn solely to prevent the expiration or nonrenewal of a Letter of Credit, and cash collateral not yet applied to an identified payment obligation, shall remain refundable Security and shall continue to constitute Operational Security until applied to an amount then due or released under Section 7.9. Such proceeds and cash collateral shall be included in determining the amount of remaining Operational Security and shall not create an additional replenishment obligation merely because they are held by DesertLink.

The posting, drawing, holding, replacement, or replenishment of Operational Security shall not, by itself, satisfy the secured obligation, reduce Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, or produce a TRBAA Credit. Drawn proceeds of Operational Security shall become Applied Security Proceeds only when DesertLink applies them to an identified Supplemental MTRC, prior-period true-up adjustment, Termination Fee, or other secured payment obligation arising under Article 6 or Section 3.3.4. Upon application, the proceeds shall reduce that obligation dollar-for-dollar and shall receive the TRBAA treatment required by Section 6.8; provided, however, that Applied Security Proceeds applied to a Termination Fee shall be administered under Section 3.3.4 and credited to transmission customer only through the Annual Termination Fee Credits provided under Section 6.8. Proceeds of Construction Security applied to Pre- In-Service Termination Costs or other construction-related obligations shall be treated as provided in Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3.

no separate acceleration concept applies. 7.8.
Post-Termination Administration and Cash Collateral. DesertLink shall continue the annual calculations, invoices, and true-ups required under this Agreement following termination of service to, or the departure, permanent cessation, or material reduction of service by, the Large Load Customer until the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and all other obligations under this Agreement have been finally satisfied, transferred, reassigned, refunded, or otherwise resolved. The Parties intend that cash collateral and proceeds of Security be treated as a deposit or deferred liability rather than as a Contribution in Aid of Construction, customer financing of transmission plant, or a reduction to DesertLink’s rate base. To the extent permitted by applicable Commission accounting and ratemaking requirements and tax law, DesertLink shall record and administer such amounts as the corresponding annual costs and payment obligations arise. The treatment described in this Section is subject to the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts, the Formula Rate, the Protocols, applicable Commission orders, and other Applicable Laws and Regulations. If the Commission requires a different accounting or ratemaking treatment, DesertLink shall implement the required treatment and make corresponding adjustments necessary to prevent duplicate recovery and preserve, to the extent permitted, the economic allocation established by this Agreement. The Parties shall cooperate in seeking any necessary Commission authorization or acceptance.

Nothing in this Agreement guarantees a particular accounting, ratemaking, or tax result. Cash collateral and unapplied Security proceeds shall remain subject to release under Section 7.9, including release to reflect an effective prospective reassignment under Section 6.9.

7.9.
Release of Security. DesertLink shall release excess Operational Security only after the applicable Reconciliation Statement becomes final. DesertLink shall release Security attributable to an effective prospective reassignment and shall release all remaining Security within thirty (30) Calendar Days after final satisfaction of the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and all other secured obligations. Termination alone does not require release.

7.10. Security Does Not Limit Liability. The Required Security Amount is based on DesertLink’s then-current estimates and calculations and does not cap, replace, or discharge Eligible Customer’s underlying obligations. A shortfall between Security and the amount due remains immediately payable to DesertLink.

8.1.
If a Party is rendered unable, wholly or in part, by Force Majeure to carry out a nonmonetary obligation, that obligation shall be suspended only to the extent and for the period performance is prevented. 9.1.
Indemnity. Indemnified Person. Indemnifying Party. If an Indemnifying Party is obligated to indemnify and hold any Indemnified Person harmless, the amount owing to the Indemnified Person shall be the amount of such Indemnified Person’s actual loss, net of any insurance or other recovery.

9.2.
Indemnity Procedures. Promptly after receipt by an Indemnified Person of any claim or notice of the commencement of any action or administrative or legal proceeding or investigation as to which the indemnity provided for in Section 9.1 may apply, the Indemnified Person shall notify the Indemnifying Party of such fact. Any failure of or delay in such notification shall not affect a Party’s indemnification obligation unless such failure or delay is materially prejudicial to the Indemnifying Party. The Indemnifying Party shall have the right to assume the defense thereof with counsel designated by such Indemnifying Party and reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Person. If the defendants in any such action include one or more Indemnified Persons and the Indemnifying Party and if the Indemnified Person reasonably concludes that there may be legal defenses available to it and/or other Indemnified Persons which are different from or additional to those available to the Indemnifying Party, the Indemnified Person shall have the right to select separate counsel to assert such legal defenses and to otherwise participate in the defense of such action on its own behalf. In such instances, the Indemnifying Party shall only be required to pay the fees and expenses of one additional attorney to represent an Indemnified Person or Indemnified Persons having such differing or additional legal defenses.

The Indemnified Person shall be entitled, at its expense, to participate in any such action, suit or proceeding, the defense of which has been assumed by the Indemnifying Party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Indemnifying Party (i) shall not be entitled to assume and control the defense of any such action, suit or proceedings if and to the extent that, in the opinion of the Indemnified Person and its counsel, such action, suit or proceeding involves the potential imposition of criminal liability on the Indemnified Person, or there exists a conflict or adversity of interest between the Indemnified Person and the Indemnifying Party, in which event the Indemnifying Party shall pay the reasonable expenses of the Indemnified Person, and (ii) shall not settle or consent to the entry of any judgment in any action, suit or proceeding without the consent of the Indemnified Person, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

10.1. 11. Disputes
All disputes, claims, or controversies arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including any dispute concerning the identification or allocation of Large Load-Driven Upgrades or Covered Upgrades; any calculation, update, or recalculation of an Estimated Annual MTRC, Final Annual MTRC, Regional Project Allocated ARR, or the MTRC Calculation Template; Qualifying Transmission Revenues; Supplemental MTRC; Total Required Revenue Commitment; Cumulative Revenue Responsibility; TRBAA Credits; Pre-In-Service Termination Costs; the Termination Fee; prospective reassignment; or Security, shall be resolved under this Article 11, except that a dispute concerning CAISO’s designation of a regional project or assignment of a project cost share shall be resolved under the applicable CAISO Tariff procedures. Any payment, refund, credit, or other adjustment resulting from the resolution of a dispute under this Article 11 shall be implemented as provided in Section 11.5. 11.1. Submission and Informal Resolution. In the event of a dispute or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the disputing Party shall provide the other Party with a written notice describing the dispute (“Notice of Dispute”). The dispute shall be referred promptly to designated senior representatives for informal resolution. The representatives shall meet or confer within ten (10) Business Days and shall use reasonable efforts to resolve the matter within thirty (30) Calendar Days after receipt of the Notice of Dispute. This informal process is not a condition to seeking emergency relief, filing a FERC complaint, or invoking any ADR processes. 11.2. Alternative Dispute Resolution. If a dispute is not resolved informally, any Party may request Alternative Dispute Resolution (“ADR”). The Parties shall use the ADR procedures, neutral-selection process, confidentiality protections, and timing requirements specified in the applicable FERC rules. ADR shall be conducted by persons knowledgeable in electric utility, transmission, and FERC matters and shall not alter a jurisdictional rate, term, or condition unless accepted or approved by the FERC.

11.3. FERC Complaints and Other Rights. Any Party may instead file a complaint, petition, or other pleading with the FERC under Section 206 or Section 306 of the Federal Power Act, or seek other relief available under the Federal Power Act or Applicable Laws and Regulations, and DesertLink may make any filing under Section

PDF page 326

40

205 of the Federal Power Act permitted by Section 12.12. No Party’s participation in informal negotiations or ADR waives or limits its right to seek FERC action. A final ADR determination affecting jurisdictional rates, terms, conditions, charges, or Network Upgrades shall be filed with the FERC if required.

11.4. Costs and Interim Performance. Unless otherwise determined through ADR, the Parties shall bear their own costs and share neutral costs as specified by the applicable ADR procedure. During a dispute, each Party shall continue performing undisputed payment and operational obligations, and shall pay undisputed amounts when due. 11.5. Implementation of Dispute Determinations; TRBAA. Within thirty (30) Calendar Days after a dispute under this Article 11 is finally resolved, whether by written agreement of the Parties, a final ADR determination (subject to any required Commission filing or acceptance), or a final Commission order (each, a “Dispute Determination”), DesertLink shall: (a) update the affected MTRC Calculation Template, Schedules, Cumulative Revenue Ledger, Reconciliation Statement, and Required Operational Security, as applicable, and serve the updated documents on Eligible Customer; and (b) invoice or refund, as applicable, any amount owed between the Parties as a result of the Dispute Determination, without interest. To the extent a Dispute Determination changes a TRBAA Credit or any other amount previously credited to, or recovered from, transmission customers, including any change in Supplemental MTRC Receipts or Applied Security Proceeds for a prior Rate Year, DesertLink shall record the resulting difference in the TRBA under Section 6.8 and flow it through to transmission customers through the TRBAA, and any amount so returned by DesertLink to transmission customers shall include interest as provided in Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff. If a final Commission order in a proceeding concerning DesertLink’s TRBAA requires a change to any TRBAA Credit attributable to this Agreement, DesertLink shall implement that order in the TRBA and shall make any corresponding updates and adjustments between the Parties under this Section 11.5 as if the order were a Dispute Determination. Nothing in this Section reopens the Final Annual MTRC or Total Required Revenue Commitment except as required to implement a Dispute Determination or as permitted by Section 6.3.1.

7. Schedule Qualifications
7.1 Projected Amounts. The capital costs, Estimated Annual MTRC, projected Total Required Revenue Commitment, Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, and Operational Security amounts stated in this Schedule are initial projections provided for planning and administration purposes. They do not constitute fixed amounts, caps, or guarantees.

7.2 Initial and Applicable Allocation Percentages. The Initial Allocation Percentage identified for each Large Load-Driven Upgrade shall remain the initial allocation of that upgrade to the Large Load Customer. The Applicable Allocation Percentage shall equal the Initial Allocation Percentage, as adjusted prospectively by any reassignment effective under Section 6.9 or as otherwise required by a final Commission order or applicable tariff provision. A change in capital costs, the Upgrade In-Service Date, Formula Rate inputs, or the annual revenue requirement shall not, by itself, change the Initial Allocation Percentage or Applicable Allocation Percentage. Cancellation, abandonment, downsizing, curtailment, permanent cessation, or material reduction of service by the Large Load Customer also shall not, by itself, reduce either percentage.

7.3 Allocation Limitation. The aggregate Annual MTRC assigned to all Large Load Customers for a Covered Upgrade shall not exceed one hundred percent (100%) of the Annual MTRC for that Covered Upgrade. DesertLink shall not allocate the same upgrade cost, transmission capability, or annual revenue requirement to more than one Large Load Customer. 7.4 Upgrade In-Service Dates and MTRC Term End Dates. Each Expected Upgrade In- Service Date stated in this Schedule is a planning estimate. DesertLink shall provide written notice to Eligible Customer of a material change to an Expected Upgrade In-Service Date. Within five (5) Business Days after a Covered Upgrade achieves its Upgrade In-Service Date, DesertLink shall provide written notice to Eligible Customer stating the actual Upgrade In- Service Date and the corresponding MTRC Term End Date. DesertLink shall update this Schedule and the applicable Cumulative Revenue Ledger to reflect those dates. The actual Upgrade In-Service Date shall be determined in accordance with the definition of that term in the Agreement. Inclusion of pre-service Construction Work in Progress in rate base does not constitute an Upgrade In-Service Date.

Schedule 2
Qualifying Transmission Revenues Methodology
1. Purpose and Controlling Principles
This Schedule establishes the reproducible methodology for calculating projected and actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues attributable to the Large Load Facility. It is intended to identify wholesale transmission revenues paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer that are attributable to the Large Load Facility and reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. Such revenues may include applicable TAC revenues and qualifying Wheeling Access Charges or other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission-service charges under the CAISO Tariff or another Commission-accepted arrangement, including charges paid through a non-PTO serving entity. The Supplemental MTRC therefore measures only the remaining shortfall below the applicable Annual MTRC.

Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be counted once in calculating the Supplemental MTRC and the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility against the combined Annual MTRC for all Covered Upgrades. They shall not also be treated as a TRBAA Credit under Section 6.8 because they reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO customers. This Schedule does not modify CAISO settlement rules, establish a retail rate, impose any obligation on CAISO, or alter any cost allocation established under the CAISO Requirements.

2. Project and Settlement Identifiers

3. Data Sources and Responsibilities
(a) DesertLink shall calculate projected and actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues using the best available data from CAISO settlement statements, wheeling, transmission-access, and transmission service invoices, revenue-quality meter data, Eligible Customer and non-PTO serving entity billing records, Scheduling Coordinator records, and other data made available under the CAISO Tariff, another Commission-accepted arrangement, or authorized by Eligible Customer and Large Load Customer.

(b) Eligible Customer shall provide, or cause its Scheduling Coordinator, Utility Distribution Company, Metering Coordinator, or other authorized agent to provide, all information reasonably necessary to identify and verify withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility. Eligible Customer shall maintain all authorizations reasonably necessary for release of that information.

(c) The Large Load Customer shall provide the information and authorizations required by its Limited Acknowledgment, including information needed to distinguish the Large Load Facility from other load behind a common meter or within a common settlement identifier.

(d) DesertLink may use CAISO data made available under the CAISO Requirements or through the authorizations provided under this Agreement. Nothing in this Schedule makes CAISO a party to the Agreement or independently requires CAISO to calculate, invoice, collect, or administer the Supplemental MTRC.

(e) If final data are unavailable when a projection, invoice, Annual Update, or Reconciliation Statement is due, DesertLink may use a reasonable estimate based on the most recent available data, the service forecast, applicable TAC rates, and known settlement adjustments. Estimated amounts shall be replaced with actual data in the next practicable reconciliation.

PDF page 345

Schedule 2 - 3

4. Applicable Withdrawals
For each CAISO settlement interval or other reproducible billing interval, Applicable Withdrawals shall equal the metered energy withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility at the metering point identified in Section 2 of this Schedule, expressed in MWh and adjusted as follows:

(a) Imports, exports, station service, auxiliary load, behind-the-meter generation, storage charging and discharging, and other injections or withdrawals shall be treated consistently with the manner in which they are recognized for the applicable TAC charge under the CAISO Tariff.

(b) Distribution losses and transmission losses shall be included only to the extent they are included in the billing determinant for the applicable TAC component. The loss factor or method shall be identified in the project-specific table in Section 10 of this Schedule.

(c) If the Large Load Facility shares a meter or settlement identifier with other load, the withdrawals attributable to the Large Load Facility shall be determined from revenue- quality submeters or another objective allocation method identified in Section 10 of this Schedule. An allocation based solely on estimates may be used temporarily but shall be reconciled when reliable data become available.

(d) Withdrawals shall not be counted for a period before the corresponding Annual MTRC is included in the Supplemental MTRC calculation under Section 6.4 of the Agreement, except where necessary to correct a prior-period error or resettlement.

5. Applicable TAC Revenue
Applicable TAC Revenue for an interval shall equal Applicable Withdrawals multiplied by the CAISO transmission rate or rates actually applicable to those withdrawals for that interval. The calculation shall include only transmission charge components that contribute to recovery of the revenue requirement in which DesertLink’s costs are included. It shall exclude retail distribution charges, generation charges, non-transmission surcharges, taxes collected for another governmental entity, and any other charge that does not contribute to recovery of DesertLink’s transmission revenue requirement.

If CAISO uses a monthly, annual, or other non-interval billing determinant, DesertLink shall perform the calculation using that same billing period and determinant. If more than one TAC rate or component applies, each component shall be calculated separately before applying the DesertLink Allocation Factor.

6. DesertLink Allocation Factor
The DesertLink Allocation Factor shall identify the portion of Applicable TAC Revenue allocable to DesertLink for the relevant period. Unless a different Commission-accepted method is stated in Section 10 of this Schedule, the factor shall be calculated from the same revenue requirement, billing determinant, allocation percentage, and other inputs used by CAISO to include DesertLink’s net transmission revenue requirement in the applicable TAC rate. For each applicable rate component and period:

PDF page 346

Schedule 2 - 4

DesertLink Allocation Factor = DesertLink Net Revenue Requirement included in the applicable TAC component ÷ Total Net Revenue Requirement recovered through that TAC component.

If DesertLink’s revenue requirement is recovered through a project-specific, zonal, or other direct allocation rather than a systemwide factor, the corresponding Commission-accepted allocation percentage or rate component shall be used. The supporting workpapers shall identify the source and calculation of each factor.

7. Calculation of Qualifying Transmission Revenues
Projected and actual Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall be calculated as follows for each applicable interval, month, or billing period and then aggregated for the Rate Year or partial Rate Year:

Qualifying Transmission Revenues =  Qualifying TAC Revenue + Qualifying Wheeling and Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues ± Applicable Adjustments.

Qualifying TAC Revenue = Σ [(Applicable Withdrawals × Applicable TAC Rate) × DesertLink Allocation Factor]. Qualifying Wheeling and Other Wholesale Transmission Revenues equal Wheeling Access Charges and other wholesale transmission-access, wheeling, or transmission- service charges actually paid by or on behalf of Eligible Customer to CAISO, a Participating TO, or a non-PTO transmission or load-serving entity for deliveries serving the Large Load Facility, but only to the extent those revenues reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected through TAC or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement. Applicable Adjustments shall include only amounts attributable to the Large Load Facility, including CAISO resettlements, billing corrections, refunds, charge reversals, balancing-account adjustments, and other adjustments that change the qualifying transmission revenue. Bad debt or uncollectible amounts shall reduce Qualifying Transmission Revenues only to the extent the corresponding revenue is not recovered from another source and is not otherwise included in DesertLink’s Formula Rate recovery.

8. Projections, Actuals, Resettlements, and Customer Changes
(a) The Annual Projection shall use forecast withdrawals, then-effective or forecast TAC rates, the most recent DesertLink Allocation Factor, and known adjustments. The workpapers shall separately identify each material assumption.

(b) The Reconciliation Statement shall replace projected values with actual withdrawals, rates, factors, and adjustments for the applicable period. CAISO resettlements or other corrections received after a Reconciliation Statement becomes final shall be reflected in the next practicable Reconciliation Statement and Annual Update, subject to Section 6.6 of the Agreement, and any dispute concerning them shall be resolved under Article 11 of the Agreement.

(c) A change in Eligible Customer, Scheduling Coordinator, or retail service provider shall not interrupt the calculation or cause the same withdrawals or revenues to be omitted or counted more than once. Qualifying Transmission Revenues shall remain associated with the Large Load Customer and Large Load Facility, regardless of which Eligible Customer is responsible for payment during the applicable period.

PDF page 347

(d) If two or more Eligible Customers serve the Large Load Facility during a Rate Year, the Qualifying Transmission Revenues and corresponding Supplemental MTRC shall be assigned between them based on the periods during which each provided service, unless the applicable transition agreement provides another Commission-accepted allocation.

9. Workpapers, Verification, and Records
With each Annual Projection and Reconciliation Statement, DesertLink shall provide workpapers sufficient for Eligible Customer to reproduce the calculation, including applicable meter quantities, TAC rates, DesertLink Allocation Factors, adjustments, source references, and a reconciliation to the corresponding Supplemental MTRC and Cumulative Revenue Ledger. Any dispute concerning the calculation shall be resolved under Article 11 of the Agreement.

Schedule 3
Credit and Security Standards
1. Purpose and Application
This Schedule establishes the forms, delivery, maintenance, replacement, draw, application, and release requirements for all Construction Security and Operational Security required under Article 7. Except for the limited reduction of direct Operational Security provided in Section 3, all Security shall be provided directly by Eligible Customer.

2. Permitted Forms of Security
Eligible Customer may provide Security in the form of cash, a Letter of Credit, or any combination thereof. DesertLink may accept another form of Security if it determines, in its sole discretion, that the form is acceptable.

Cash collateral shall be delivered in immediately available funds to an account designated by DesertLink and shall count dollar-for-dollar toward the applicable Required Security Amount while held by DesertLink.

(a) Construction Security
Eligible Customer shall provide and maintain all Construction Security directly in one or more forms permitted under this Section 2. A Retail Security Certification and Qualifying Retail Security Support shall not constitute, reduce, replace, or satisfy Construction Security or any Pre- In-Service Termination Costs.

(b) Operational Security
Except to the extent reduced under Section 3, Eligible Customer shall provide and maintain direct Operational Security in one or more forms permitted under this Section 2 in an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility.

3. Retail Security Certification
A current Retail Security Certification reduces the direct Operational Security requirement dollar-for-dollar by the amount of Qualifying Retail Security Support identified in that certification. It does not reduce Eligible Customer’s underlying obligations, constitute Security posted directly with DesertLink, or apply to Construction Security or Pre-In-Service Termination Costs.

Each Retail Security Certification must be substantially in the form of Exhibit A contained in Schedule 3 of this Agreement. Eligible Customer shall deliver a Retail Security Certification before first relying on Qualifying Retail Security Support to reduce the direct Operational Security requirement. The Retail Security Certification shall remain effective unless and until

PDF page 350

Schedule 3 - 2

superseded, withdrawn, or deemed ineffective under this Agreement. Eligible Customer shall deliver an updated Retail Security Certification within three (3) Business Days after any reduction, draw, expiration, nonrenewal, termination, amendment, loss of enforceable draw or application rights, or other event that could impair the certified support.

With each Reconciliation Statement, DesertLink may identify the amount of Qualifying Retail Security Support then reflected in calculating Required Operational Security. That identification does not require Eligible Customer to deliver a new Retail Security Certification unless an event requiring an update has occurred.

DesertLink may rely on the certification without reviewing the underlying retail security documents in the ordinary course, but may request supporting information after a payment default, Credit Review Event, Material Adverse Credit Event, or reasonable basis to question the certification.

4. Letter of Credit Requirements
If Eligible Customer provides a Letter of Credit as Security, the Letter of Credit must be irrevocable, unconditional, transferable, payable at sight, and permit partial and multiple draws. It must be issued by a major United States commercial bank or United States branch of a major foreign commercial bank rated at least A- by S&P, A3 by Moody’s, or A- by Fitch, in each case by at least two of those three agencies, and otherwise be in form and substance reasonably acceptable to DesertLink.

Each Letter of Credit must have an initial stated term of at least twelve (12) months and provide DesertLink at least ninety (90) Calendar Days’ prior written notice of nonrenewal. Eligible Customer shall provide a conforming extension, replacement Letter of Credit, cash collateral, or other Security accepted by DesertLink no later than sixty (60) Calendar Days before the applicable expiration date following a notice of nonrenewal, and within fifteen (15) Business Days after an issuer rating reduction.

If Eligible Customer fails to timely provide the required replacement or substitute Security, DesertLink may, before the applicable Letter of Credit expires, draw all or any portion of the then-available amount and retain the proceeds as cash collateral, apply the proceeds to secured obligations, or both.

5. Security Notices; Maintenance; and Replenishment
DesertLink may issue a Security Notice whenever it reasonably determines that the Required Security Amount exceeds available Security, including as a result of a draw, application of cash collateral, change in the Required Security Amount, loss of Qualifying Retail Security Support, or other event affecting Security availability.

Eligible Customer shall provide any required increase, restoration, replacement, or other cure within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the Security Notice, or by the applicable in- service date if earlier.

6. Draws; Application; and Release

PDF page 351

Schedule 3 - 3

DesertLink may draw against a Letter of Credit, apply cash collateral, or apply another accepted form of Security as permitted under Article 7. A draw, the holding of proceeds or cash collateral, or replenishment does not by itself satisfy an obligation or reduce Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. Proceeds of Operational Security become Applied Security Proceeds only when applied to an identified secured obligation as provided in Section 7.6; proceeds of Construction Security are treated as provided in Sections 3.3.2 and 3.3.3.

DesertLink shall release excess Security after the applicable Reconciliation Statement becomes final. DesertLink shall release all remaining Security within thirty (30) Calendar Days after final satisfaction of all secured obligations, subject to any specifically identified unresolved dispute.

7. Required Security Amount Not a Limitation
The Required Security Amount is based on then-current estimates and calculations and does not limit Eligible Customer’s total liability or responsibility for its obligations under this Agreement.

MTRC Calculation Template and Cumulative Revenue Ledger
This Schedule contains the project-specific calculation of each Estimated Annual MTRC and Final Annual MTRC and the Cumulative Revenue Ledger. DesertLink shall calculate each Annual MTRC solely under this Schedule. The Final Annual MTRC shall equal the applicable final incurred capital cost multiplied by the Project-Specific Levelized Fixed Charge Rate calculated in this Schedule. The calculation shall identify the applicable capital-cost input, present-worth tax-depreciation benefits, Formula Rate inputs, fixed expense allocator, applicable allocation percentage, Annual MTRC, Total Required Revenue Commitment, Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, and supporting inputs.

For purposes of calculating present-worth federal and state income-tax depreciation benefits, the Schedule applies a levelized-depreciation rate of five percent (5%) of the applicable capital cost input in each year of the twenty (20)-year MTRC Term. This levelized-depreciation schedule is not a separate annual charge. The Schedule is fixed on the Final MTRC Determination Date except to correct an error or fraud, to implement an effective prospective reassignment, to implement a final FERC order applicable to the calculation, to implement a Dispute Determination under Section 11.5, or to reflect, prospectively, a change in (i) DesertLink’s return on equity component of its Formula Rate, resulting from a final FERC order accepting or approving such change, or (ii) applicable federal or state tax rates or tax law enacted after the Final MTRC Determination Date; provided that, the five percent (5%) annual levelized- depreciation schedule shall remain fixed for the MTRC Term unless a final FERC order requires otherwise.

1

 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION PROCEDURES (LLIP)

Section 1.
Objectives and Applicability
1.1 Objectives

The objective of this LLIP is to implement requirements for Large Load interconnections to the Participating TO’s Transmission System pursuant to the TO Tariff.  For purposes of this LLIP, the “Participating TO” is DesertLink, LLC (“DesertLink”), and the “TO Tariff” is the DesertLink, LLC Transmission Owner Tariff.  Because DesertLink is a Non-Load-Serving Participating TO and has no End-Use Customers, a Large Load interconnecting under this LLIP will not be a retail transmission customer of the Participating TO.

1.2 Applicability

The LLIP is applicable to a Large Load Interconnection Customer that is either (1) proposing to interconnect a Large Load to the Participating TO’s Transmission System; (2) seeking to increase the capacity of an existing Large Load processed under the LLIP; or (3) with respect to an existing load interconnected to the Participating TO’s Transmission System that was not processed under the LLIP, seeking an increase of 50 MW or greater.  This LLIP only applies to completed Interconnection Requests submitted after the effective date of this Appendix VI to the TO Tariff.  Consistent with Section 10A of the TO Tariff, all requests for ECLL Interconnection shall be directed to the Participating TO.  An Interconnection Request submitted under this LLIP shall constitute the ECLL Interconnection Application, and the Interconnection Studies and the Large Load Interconnection Agreement under this LLIP shall constitute the study process and the ECLL Interconnection Agreement, respectively, for purposes of Section 10A of the TO Tariff.

Section 2.
Definitions

Terms used in this LLIP with initial capitalization shall have the meanings set forth below.  The singular of any definition shall include the plural and the plural shall include the singular.  If a term with initial capitalization used herein is not defined, such term shall have the meanings ascribed to such term in Section 3 of the TO Tariff.

Affected System shall mean an electric system other than the Participating TO’s Transmission System that may be affected by the proposed interconnection.

Affected System Operator shall mean the entity that owns or operates an Affected System, and includes an Affected System Owner as defined in any Cost Recovery Agreement.

Applicable Laws and Regulations shall mean all duly promulgated applicable federal, state and local laws, regulations, rules, ordinances, codes, decrees, judgments, directives, or judicial or administrative orders, permits and other duly authorized actions of any Governmental Authority.

PDF page 367

2

Base Case shall mean data including, but not limited to, base power flow, short circuit and stability data bases, underlying load, generation, and transmission facility assumptions, contingency lists, including relevant remedial action schemes, and transmission diagrams used to perform the Interconnection Studies.  The Base Case may include Critical Energy Infrastructure Information (as that term is defined by FERC).  The Base Case may include transmission facilities as approved by the Participating TO or ISO, as applicable, Reliability Network Upgrades that are included in a signed interconnection agreement, Large Load Network Upgrades, Large Loads and any co-located generation, and load forecast. The Base Case may also include generation facilities that (i) are directly interconnected to a Distribution System or the ISO Controlled Grid; (ii) are interconnected to Affected Systems and may have an impact on the Interconnection Request; (iii) have a pending request to interconnect to a Distribution System or an Affected System; or (iv) are not interconnected to a Distribution System or the ISO Controlled Grid, but are subject to the terms and conditions of a fully executed interconnection agreement (or its equivalent predecessor agreement) or for which an unexecuted interconnection agreement (or its equivalent predecessor agreement) has been requested to be filed with FERC.

Business Day shall mean Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Holidays.

Calendar Day shall mean any day including Saturday, Sunday or a Federal Holiday.

Commercial Readiness Deposit shall mean a deposit paid as set forth in LLIP Sections 4.2.1 and 4.6.1.4.

Confidential Information shall mean any confidential, proprietary or trade secret information of a plan, specification, pattern, procedure, design, device, list, concept, policy or compilation relating to the present or planned business of a Party, which is designated as confidential by the Party supplying the information, whether conveyed orally, electronically, in writing, through inspection, or otherwise.

Cost Recovery Agreement shall have the meaning set forth in Section 3 of the TO Tariff.

Dispute Resolution shall mean the applicable procedure for resolution of a dispute between the Parties as described in Section 14 of the TO Tariff, including, as applicable, the ISO ADR Procedures.

Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) Service shall have the meaning set forth in Section 3 of the TO Tariff.

FILI Study shall mean the study performed by the Participating TO pursuant to LLIP Section 4.6.2 to determine the availability of Interim Firm Interconnection Service and FILI Service.

Interconnection Financial Security shall mean any of the financial instruments listed in LLIP Section 4.7.1 provided by the Large Load Interconnection Customer to comply with its obligations under the LLIP or the Large Load Interconnection Agreement.

PDF page 368

3

Interconnection Request shall mean a request, in the form of Attachment 1 to Appendix VI to the TO Tariff, to interconnect a new Large Load, or to increase the capacity of, or make a Material Modification to the operating characteristics of, an existing Large Load that is interconnected with the Participating TO’s Transmission System.

Interconnection Study shall mean any of the following studies: the Large Load Interconnection Study, the FILI Study, restudies, and any additional studies performed pursuant to LLIP Section 4.6.3.

Interconnection Study Deposit shall mean the cash deposit provided to the Participating TO under LLIP Section 4.2.1 as a requirement of a valid Interconnection Request to be used to offset the cost of the Interconnection Studies.

Large Load Capacity shall mean the maximum capacity of the Large Load at the Point of Interconnection.

Large Load Customer shall mean the End-User that owns, operates, or proposes to develop the Large Load and receives, or will receive, retail transmission service from the Large Load Interconnection Customer, and shall be the Large Load Customer for purposes of the TO Tariff and any Cost Recovery Agreement.

Large Load Interconnection Agreement shall mean the interconnection agreement between the Participating TO and the Large Load Interconnection Customer, developed by the Participating TO consistent with the TO Tariff and the results of the Interconnection Studies and negotiated between the Parties pursuant to LLIP Section 5, which sets forth the terms and conditions governing the interconnection of the Large Load to the Participating TO’s Transmission System, including, without limitation, cost responsibility, payment provisions, cost recovery, and financial security for the Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large Load Network Upgrades, as it may be amended from time to time. The Large Load Interconnection Agreement shall constitute the ECLL Interconnection Agreement for purposes of the TO Tariff, as applicable, and shall be filed with FERC by the Participating TO to the extent required. For purposes of the TO Tariff, the Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large Load Network Upgrades identified in the Large Load Interconnection Agreement shall together constitute the ECLL Interconnection Facilities.

Large Load Interconnection Customer shall mean an Eligible Customer for Large Load (“ECLL”), as defined in Section 3 of the TO Tariff, that proposes to interconnect its facilities with the Participating TO’s Transmission System for the purpose of providing retail transmission service to a Large Load.

Large Load Interconnection Customer Interconnection Facilities shall mean all facilities and equipment owned, controlled, or operated by the Large Load Interconnection Customer or the Large Load Customer up to the Point of Change of Ownership as identified in the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, including any modifications, additions or upgrades to such facilities and equipment.

PDF page 369

4

Large Load Interconnection Procedures (LLIP) shall mean the interconnection procedures applicable to an Interconnection Request set forth in this Appendix VI to the TO Tariff.

Large Load Interconnection Study shall mean an engineering study conducted by the Participating TO for a Large Load Interconnection Customer under the LLIP that evaluates the impact of the proposed interconnection on the safety and reliability of Participating TO’s Transmission System and, if applicable, an Affected System. The Large Load Interconnection Study will also determine a list of facilities (including Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities and Large Load Network Upgrades), the cost of those facilities, and the time required to interconnect the Large Load with the Participating TO’s Transmission System. The scope of the study is defined in LLIP Section 4.6.1.1.

Large Load Network Upgrades shall mean the additions, modifications, and upgrades to the ISO Controlled Grid at or beyond the Point of Interconnection necessary to serve one or more Large Loads safely and reliably that are identified through the Large Load Interconnection Study and submitted to the ISO for concurrence pursuant to Section 25.7 of the ISO Tariff. Large Load Network Upgrades do not include Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities. To the extent a Large Load Network Upgrade is owned or to be constructed by the Participating TO and is identified in Schedule 1 to a Cost Recovery Agreement, such Large Load Network Upgrades shall constitute Large Load-Driven Upgrades, as defined in that Cost Recovery Agreement.

Large Load Study Process Agreement shall mean the agreement, developed and tendered by the Participating TO pursuant to LLIP Section 4.5, entered into by the Large Load Interconnection Customer and the Participating TO which sets forth the Parties’ agreement to perform Interconnection Studies under the LLIP.

Material Modification shall mean those modifications that have a material impact on the cost or timing of any Interconnection Request, or any other valid interconnection request to the Participating TO or the ISO, with an equal or later Queue Position date.

Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities shall mean all facilities and equipment owned, controlled, or operated by the Participating TO from the Point of Change of Ownership to the Point of Interconnection as identified in the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, including any modifications, additions or upgrades to such facilities and equipment. Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities are transmission facilities but are not controlled by the ISO.  Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities are sole use facilities and shall not include Large Load Network Upgrades.

Participating TO’s Transmission System shall mean the facilities owned and operated by the Participating TO and that have been placed under the ISO’s Operational Control, which facilities form part of the ISO Controlled Grid.

Point of Change of Ownership shall mean the point, as set forth in the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, where the Large Load Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities connect to the Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities.

PDF page 370

5

Point of Interconnection shall mean the point, as set forth in the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, where the Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities connect to the Participating TO’s Transmission System.  For purposes of the TO Tariff, the Point of Interconnection shall be the Point of Withdrawal for the Large Load.

Queue Position shall mean the order of a valid Interconnection Request, relative to all other pending valid Interconnection Requests, established pursuant to LLIP Section 3.8.

Reasonable Efforts shall mean, with respect to an action required to be attempted or taken by a Party under the LLIP or the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, efforts that are timely and consistent with Good Utility Practice and are otherwise substantially equivalent to those a Party would use to protect its own interests.

Report Meeting shall mean the meeting among the Participating TO, the Large Load Interconnection Customer, and if applicable, the ISO and other Affected System Operators to discuss the results of the Interconnection Studies as set forth in the LLIP.

Scoping Meeting shall mean the meeting between representatives of the Large Load Interconnection Customer and Participating TO, and if applicable, the ISO, conducted for the purpose of discussing alternative interconnection options, to exchange information including any transmission data and earlier study evaluations that would be reasonably expected to impact such interconnection options, to analyze such information, and to determine the potential feasible Points of Interconnection.

Service Commencement Date shall mean the date the Large Load is initially operated in parallel with the Participating TO’s Transmission System and transmission interconnection service is provided to the Large Load Interconnection Customer pursuant to the terms of an executed Large Load Interconnection Agreement. For purposes of any Cost Recovery Agreement, the Service Commencement Date shall be the Large Load Service Commencement Date specified in Schedule 1 to that agreement.

Site Control shall have the meaning set forth in Section 3 of the TO Tariff.

System Protection Facilities shall mean the equipment, including necessary protection signal communications equipment, that protects (1) the Participating TO’s Transmission System, Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities, ISO Controlled Grid, and Affected Systems from faults or other electrical disturbances occurring at the Large Load and (2) the Large Load from faults or other electrical system disturbances occurring on the ISO Controlled Grid, Participating TO’s Interconnection Facilities, and Affected Systems or on other delivery systems or other generating systems to which the ISO Controlled Grid is directly connected.

Transmission Interconnection Service shall mean the service provided by the Participating TO associated with interconnecting the Large Load to the Participating TO’s Transmission System and enabling the Large Load Interconnection Customer to receive electric energy at the Point of Interconnection, pursuant to the terms of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement and the TO Tariff.
