Q.
HOW DOES THE CRA ADDRESS STRANDED-ASSET RISK?
11
A. The CRA addresses stranded-asset risk through a twenty-year revenue commitment, 12

construction and operational security, and termination provisions that preserve the 13

Eligible Customer’s responsibility if the Large Load fails to materialize or departs the 14

system.
15
First, Section 6.7 establishes the Total Required Revenue Commitment for each Covered 16

Upgrade as the Final Annual MTRC multiplied by twenty, subject to the adjustments 17

specified in that section. Before final determination, the projected commitment uses the 18

Estimated Annual MTRC. The Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility equals 19

that commitment less cumulative QTR, Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security 20

Proceeds, effective prospective reassignment credits, and a Termination Fee received in 21

full, without double counting. DesertLink updates an upgrade-specific Cumulative 22

Revenue Ledger at least annually and includes it with each Reconciliation Statement. 23

When a final Reconciliation Statement determines that the remaining responsibility is 24

PDF page 418

Page 13

zero ("Break-Even"), operational payment and security obligations terminate. Once 1

finally satisfied, the responsibility does not revive because of later changes in Formula 2

Rate inputs, subject to final true-ups and correction of errors or fraud for periods before 3

satisfaction.
4
Second, Sections 3.3.4 and 3.5 provide that cancellation, downsizing, curtailment, or 5

cessation after an applicable in-service date does not itself eliminate payment or security 6

obligations. Upon effective termination of the CRA or permanent cessation of service 7

after that date, the Eligible Customer owes a lump-sum Termination Fee equal to the 8

Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility for the in-service Covered Upgrades, less 9

any Supplemental MTRC billed and unpaid as of the effective termination date, due thirty 10

Calendar Days after DesertLink’s invoice. The excluded unpaid Supplemental MTRC 11

remains separately payable and secured; its later payment, satisfaction through Applied 12

Security Proceeds, or direct recovery reduces the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. 13

Payment in full discharges only the remaining contractual responsibility included in the 14

fee, and no further Supplemental MTRC accrues for periods after the effective 15

termination or cessation date, subject to final reconciliation for earlier periods. 16

DesertLink holds each Termination Fee, together with any Operational Security proceeds 17

applied to it, in a separate interest-bearing Termination Fee Account. For each Covered 18

Upgrade, the Annual Termination Fee Credit for each remaining Rate Year equals the 19

applicable Annual MTRC, prorated for a partial Rate Year, but may not exceed the 20

available Termination Fee Balance. In the final Rate Year of the MTRC Term, the credit 21

includes the entire remaining balance, including earnings, so the account is reduced to 22

zero, subject to release and adjustment if a prospective reassignment occurs. The 23

PDF page 419

Page 14

uncredited balance is separately accounted for as a deferred liability, is not included in 1

rate base, and is not itself a TRBAA Credit. These credits do not reduce rate base. 2

Third, Article 7 requires Construction Security for incurred and irrevocably committed 3

costs and Pre-In-Service Termination Costs, including applicable cancellation, 4

demobilization, and restoration costs and properly accrued allowance for funds used 5

during construction ("AFUDC"). Construction Security continues separately for upgrades 6

not yet in service. Operational Security must be delivered no later than thirty Calendar 7

Days before the earliest expected applicable in-service date and be fully effective before 8

service. Under Section 7.3, it equals one hundred percent of the nominal Remaining 9

Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, reduced only by currently certified Qualifying 10

Retail Security Support.  Security is recalculated at the events specified in Section 7.4, 11

including annual projections and reconciliations, final MTRC determination, permitted 12

recalculations, reassignment, and credit review events. Security does not cap the Eligible 13

Customer’s underlying liability. For a DesertLink-owned CAISO-Assigned Regional 14

Project, the CRA does not independently impose pre-service Construction Security solely 15

because CAISO has assigned a project share; any such requirement must arise under the 16

applicable tariff, interconnection agreement, or other Commission-accepted arrangement. 17

Together, these provisions protect against stranded-asset exposure through an identified 18

revenue commitment and enforceable payment and security obligations. Sections 4.2 and 19

6.3.6 also require separate affected-system and third-party regional-project arrangements 20

and evidence of compliance. These provisions support the Show Cause Order’s objective 21

of mitigating the risk of stranded assets if large loads prove speculative. 22

HOW DOES THE CRA AVOID REDUNDANT FINANCIAL SECURITY
1
REQUIREMENTS?
2
A. Section 7.1 recognizes Construction Security provided under an interconnection or 3

engineering and procurement agreement for the same costs, avoiding duplication. Under 4

Article 7 and Schedule 3, a currently effective Retail Security Certification reduces direct 5

Operational Security dollar-for-dollar by certified Qualifying Retail Security Support. 6

This does not reduce the underlying wholesale obligation and does not apply to 7

Construction Security or Pre-In-Service Termination Costs. The certification remains 8

effective until superseded, withdrawn, or deemed ineffective; no annual recertification is 9

required unless an update-triggering event occurs. Direct Security may be cash, a 10

qualifying Letter of Credit, or another form accepted by DesertLink in its sole discretion. 11

There is no automatic unsecured allowance for an investment-grade utility. 12

Section 6.10 allows transfer to a Successor Eligible Customer through an assumption 13

agreement and required Security before the prior Eligible Customer is released. Section 14

6.9 permits prospective reassignment to a subsequent large load at another facility only 15

when an objective study demonstrates reliance on identifiable incremental upgrade 16

capability that avoids or reduces otherwise-needed upgrades. The reassignment is 17

bounded by the avoided upgrade cost, capability-supported amount, and remaining 18

allocated net plant. A reduction becomes effective only after the service, agreement, 19

transfer of the same Large Load Facility is governed by Section 6.10 rather than the 21

capital costs of those upgrades. Instead, the CRA establishes a minimum transmission 6

revenue commitment, with Supplemental MTRC payments credited to transmission 7

customers through the TRBAA mechanism.
8
Schedule 5, rather than a new Formula Rate calculation, controls the Estimated Annual 9

MTRC and Final Annual MTRC. The CRA controls Supplemental MTRC, the
10
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, Operational Security, and prospective reassignment. 11

With each Annual Projection, Section 6.5 requires upgrade-specific workpapers showing 12

the Annual MTRC, forecast QTR, projected Supplemental MTRC, prior-period true-up 13

adjustment, Forecast TRBAA Credit, Total Required Revenue Commitment, and 14

Required Operational Security. With each Annual Update, Sections 6.6 and 6.7 require 15

service of the Reconciliation Statement, updated Cumulative Revenue Ledger, 16

recalculated security, TRBA reconciliation, and supporting workpapers. 17

Section 6.8 governs credits through the TRBAA, and Article 11 governs disputes arising 18

under the CRA. The Annual MTRC and related contractual obligations are administered 19

under the CRA separately from the Formula Rate calculation.
20
Q.
HOW DOES THE CRA ADDRESS ANNUAL TRUE-UPS AND FINALITY?
21
A. Section 6.6 carries an under-billed or over-billed Supplemental MTRC amount into 22

billing following the next Annual Projection. If no further Supplemental MTRC will be 23

invoiced, DesertLink separately invoices an under-billed amount, payable within thirty 24

PDF page 427

Page 22

Calendar Days after receipt, or refunds an over-billed amount within thirty Calendar 1

Days after service of the Reconciliation Statement. These adjustments between the 2

Parties bear no interest. The Reconciliation Statement becomes final upon written 3

acceptance or ninety Calendar Days after service, whichever occurs first, unless a timely 4

Notice of Dispute identifies disputed items. Undisputed portions become final on the 5

otherwise applicable date; disputed items become final upon the applicable Dispute 6

Determination.
7
Under Section 11.5, DesertLink implements a final Dispute Determination by updating 8

the affected calculations, Schedules, ledger, reconciliation, and Security, as applicable, 9

and invoicing or refunding amounts between the Parties within thirty Calendar Days, 10

without interest. Any resulting adjustment affecting amounts credited to or recovered 11

from transmission customers is recorded in the TRBA and flows through the TRBAA, 12

with interest on amounts returned to transmission customers as provided in Section 5.5 of 13

the TO Tariff.
14
Q.
HOW DOES THE CRA SUPPORT COST AND BILLING TRANSPARENCY?
15
A. The Annual Projection workpapers and annual Reconciliation Statement make the 16

upgrade-specific minimum contribution, forecast and actual QTR, Supplemental MTRC, 17

cumulative commitment, security, and TRBAA credit calculations available to the 18

Eligible Customer. Schedule 5 records the MTRC calculation and Cumulative Revenue 19

Ledger. Section 6.8 also requires workpapers with each TRBAA filing sufficient for 20

transmission customers to verify the credits, with aggregation or privileged treatment 21

available to protect customer-specific information. LLIP Sections 4.6.1.2 and 4.6.1.3 22

separately provide for study reports, supporting documentation upon request, and a 23

PDF page 428

Page 23
Report Meeting addressing study results and assigned cost responsibility. LLIP Section 1

4.6.2.1 provides for ISO posting of FILI Service Agreements.
2
Section 6.12 provides the Eligible Customer access, upon reasonable request, to the 3

information needed to verify the identification of upgrades and the CRA’s calculations. 4

Article 11 provides informal resolution, alternative dispute resolution, and access to 5

FERC. Consistent with TO Tariff Sections 10.9, 10A.3, 10A.3.9, 10A.6, and 14, disputes 6

arising under a CRA are resolved under that agreement’s dispute resolution provisions. 7

The Large Load Customer and any Successor Eligible Customer may participate to the 8

extent a dispute affects its obligations under the CRA or Limited Acknowledgment. 9

Disputes over CAISO’s regional project designation or assignment are resolved under the 10

applicable CAISO Tariff procedures.
11
The CRA’s confidentiality provisions protect customer-specific information while 12

preserving verification and dispute rights. These contractual records and the TRBAA 13

filing workpapers provide a basis to trace payments and credits and test whether the same 14

obligation has been counted more than once.

II. PURPOSE AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY
5
Q.
WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?
6
A. The purpose of my testimony is to explain how DesertLink will recover the cost of 7

transmission facilities built to serve large loads and covered by a Large Load Cost 8

Recovery Agreement (“CRA”) (such facilities, “Covered Upgrades”), and how it will 9

credit the amounts Eligible Customers pay under their CRAs to transmission customers. 10

The proposal responds to the Commission’s June 18, 2026, order in Docket No. EL26- 11

71-000 (“Show Cause Order”). Specifically, my testimony (i) describes the large load 12

cost recovery framework; (ii) explains how the amounts DesertLink receives under its 13

CRAs will be credited to customers through DesertLink’s Transmission Revenue 14

Balancing Account Adjustment (“TRBAA”), and the related revisions to DesertLink’s 15

Transmission Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”); (iii) describes the changes to DesertLink’s 16

Formula Rate Template, including a new Attachment 1a; (iv) explains why no changes 17

are needed to DesertLink’s Formula Rate Implementation Protocols or Appendix I of the 18

TO Tariff; (v) describes the exhibits I sponsor, including two illustrative examples; and 19

(vi) explains why the proposal is just and reasonable. The pro forma CRA, including how 20

each Eligible Customer’s annual Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution is 21

established, is sponsored by DesertLink witness Mr. Hayes.
22

PDF page 444

3

Q.
PLEASE SUMMARIZE THE PROPOSAL.
1
A. DesertLink proposes to credit the amounts it receives under its CRAs to transmission 2

customers through its TRBAA, the existing mechanism DesertLink uses to pass revenue 3

that it does not receive through the California Independent System Operator Corporation 4

(“CAISO”) Transmission Access Charge (“TAC”) back to customers. To implement this 5

proposal, DesertLink proposes the following:
6
• Revise the definition of the TRBAA and Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff so that the 7

TRBAA also flows through to transmission customers the amounts a CRA 8

requires to be credited through it, including TRBAA Credits that DesertLink 9

receives directly from or on behalf of an Eligible Customer;
10
• Add Attachment 1a – Project Plant Detail to the Formula Rate Template, to report 11

plant and net investment separately for the Harry Allen to Eldorado 500 kV 12

Transmission Project (“Harry Allen to Eldorado Project”) and each Covered 13

Upgrade;
14
• Use the project detail on Attachment 1a to calculate the revenue requirement of 15

each project on Attachment 1 – Project Revenue Requirement Worksheet; and 16

• Add a new Line 17a to Attachment 12 – Revenue Credit Detail, so that TRBAA 17

Credits are not also credited in the Formula Rate.
18

19

III. DESERTLINK AND FORMULA RATE BACKGROUND
8
Q.
PLEASE PROVIDE AN OVERVIEW OF DESERTLINK AND ITS FORMULA
9
RATE.
10
A. DesertLink is a transmission-only Participating Transmission Owner in the CAISO that 11

owns the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project, which the CAISO selected DesertLink to 12

develop through its competitive solicitation process. DesertLink’s formula rate consists 13

of its Formula Rate Template (Appendix III of the TO Tariff) and its Formula Rate 14

Implementation Protocols (Appendix IV of the TO Tariff) (together, the “Formula 15

Rate”), which were originally accepted by the Commission in Docket No. ER17-135 and 16

most recently revised in Docket No. ER26-3479. DesertLink’s revenue requirement is 17

recovered through the CAISO TAC.
18
Q.
HOW DOES THE FORMULA RATE OPERATE EACH YEAR?
19
A. By October 1, DesertLink posts an Annual Projection of its net revenue requirement for 20

the upcoming Rate Year. By July 1 after each Rate Year, DesertLink posts an Annual 21

PDF page 446

5

Update using actual FERC Form No. 1 or other Company data. The difference between 1

the projected and actual net revenue requirement, with interest, is the True-Up 2

Adjustment, which is included in a later Annual Projection.
3
Q.
HOW IS DESERTLINK’S TRANSMISSION REVENUE REQUIREMENT
4
DETERMINED?
5
A. As provided in Appendix I of the TO Tariff, DesertLink’s Transmission Revenue 6

Requirement (“TRR”) is the sum of its Base Transmission Revenue Requirement (“Base 7

TRR”), determined under the Formula Rate, and its TRBAA. DesertLink files to update 8

its TRBAA each October, effective January 1. Under Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff, the 9

TRBAA equals the principal balance in DesertLink’s Transmission Revenue Balancing 10

Account (“TRBA”) as of September 30 (“Cr”), plus a forecast of Transmission Revenue 11

Credits for the following calendar year (“Cf”), plus the interest balance for the TRBA 12

(“I”). The TRBA compares DesertLink’s Base TRR to the amounts it actually receives, 13

so that DesertLink collects no more and no less than its Base TRR. DesertLink already 14

uses the TRBAA to credit customers with revenue it receives outside the TAC, such as 15

Generator Interconnection Process Forfeited Deposit Allocations.
16
Q.
WHY IS DESERTLINK MAKING THIS FILING?
17
A. In the Show Cause Order, the Commission directed the CAISO and its transmission 18

owners to show cause why their tariffs remain just and reasonable or to propose changes 19

for integrating large loads. Among other things, the Commission called for a mechanism 20

to ensure that large load payments are “credited toward transmission owners’ 21

transmission revenue requirements.” DesertLink’s current Formula Rate Template reports 22

plant values only in total and has no means of identifying the facilities built to serve large 23

loads, and its TO Tariff limits Transmission Revenue Credits to amounts received from 24

PDF page 447

6

the CAISO. The revisions I describe provide the mechanism the Commission called for. 1

IV. THE LARGE LOAD COST RECOVERY FRAMEWORK
2
Q.
WHAT IS A CRA?
3
A. A CRA is an agreement between DesertLink and an Eligible Customer taking 4

transmission service on behalf of a large load. Under its CRA, the Eligible Customer 5

commits to an annual Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“Annual MTRC”) 6

for each Covered Upgrade built to serve the large load, for a fixed twenty-year term 7

beginning on the applicable in-service date, with partial Rate Years prorated as provided 8

in the CRA. The pro forma CRA is set forth in Appendix V of the TO Tariff. The Annual 9

MTRC is calculated solely under the MTRC Calculation Template in Schedule 5 of the 10

CRA and is not an input to, or a calculation made under, the Formula Rate. The terms of 11

the pro forma CRA, including how the Annual MTRC is established, termination, and 12

credit support requirements, are described in the transmittal letter and the testimony of 13

Mr. Hayes.
14
Q.
HOW ARE THE COSTS OF COVERED UPGRADES RECOVERED?
15
A. Each Covered Upgrade placed under the CAISO’s Operational Control is included in 16

DesertLink’s rate base and Base TRR and recovered through the CAISO TAC together 17

with the cost of the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project. The Eligible Customer pays the 18

TAC for the service it takes, like any other transmission customer. The portion of those 19

TAC payments allocable to DesertLink, determined under Schedule 2 of the CRA, counts 20

toward the Eligible Customer’s Annual MTRC as “Qualifying Transmission Revenues.” 21

Under Section 6.2, Qualifying Transmission Revenues also include qualifying wheeling 22

and other wholesale transmission revenues attributable to service to the Large Load 23

Facility, to the extent they reduce transmission revenues otherwise collected from CAISO 24

PDF page 448

7

customers or directly credit DesertLink’s Net Revenue Requirement, without duplicate 1

recognition.
2
Q.
WHAT IS THE SUPPLEMENTAL MTRC?
3
A. The Supplemental MTRC is calculated separately for each Covered Upgrade as the 4

amount, if any, by which the applicable Annual MTRC, prorated for a partial Rate Year, 5

exceeds the Qualifying Transmission Revenues allocated to that upgrade under Section 6

6.4. It ensures that the Eligible Customer pays at least its committed Annual MTRC each 7

year, even if its load develops more slowly than expected. The Supplemental MTRC is 8

never less than zero.
9
Q.
HOW IS THE SUPPLEMENTAL MTRC BILLED AND RECONCILED?
10
A. The Supplemental MTRC follows the same calendar as the Formula Rate. With each 11

Annual Projection, DesertLink forecasts the Eligible Customer’s Qualifying 12

Transmission Revenues and resulting Supplemental MTRC for the Rate Year and 13

invoices that amount, increased or reduced by any prior-period true-up adjustment, to the 14

Eligible Customer in equal monthly installments. In connection with each Annual 15

Update, DesertLink determines the actual Supplemental MTRC using actual Qualifying 16

Transmission Revenues and serves the Eligible Customer a Reconciliation Statement. 17

The difference between the Supplemental MTRC billed for a Rate Year, excluding any 18

prior-period true-up adjustment included in that billing, and the actual Supplemental 19

MTRC for that Rate Year is a prior-period true-up adjustment, which increases or reduces 20

the Supplemental MTRC invoiced following the next Annual Projection. The adjustment 21

is invoiced or refunded separately only if no further Supplemental MTRC will be 22

invoiced. No interest accrues on the Supplemental MTRC or on any prior-period true-up 23

adjustment between DesertLink and the Eligible Customer.
24

PDF page 449

8

Q.
WHAT HAPPENS IF AN ELIGIBLE CUSTOMER DOES NOT PAY OR
1
TERMINATES ITS CRA?
2
A. If an Eligible Customer does not pay, DesertLink may draw on the Eligible Customer’s 3

Operational Security and apply the proceeds to the unpaid amount (“Applied Security 4

Proceeds”). Upon effective termination of the CRA or permanent cessation of service by 5

the Large Load Facility after the applicable in-service date, the Eligible Customer pays a 6

lump-sum Termination Fee equal to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility 7

for each in-service Covered Upgrade, less any Supplemental MTRC billed and unpaid as 8

of the effective termination or cessation date. The excluded unpaid amounts remain 9

separately payable and secured; their later payment, satisfaction through Applied Security 10

Proceeds, or direct recovery reduces the Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. Full 11

payment of the Termination Fee discharges only the responsibility included in that fee, as 12

provided in Section 3.3.4. DesertLink will hold the Termination Fee in a separately 13

identified, interest-bearing Termination Fee Account for each Covered Upgrade and 14

credit the balance, including earnings, to transmission customers through the TRBAA in 15

annual amounts equal to the Annual MTRC (“Annual Termination Fee Credits”), for the 16

Rate Years remaining in the applicable MTRC Term, prorated for partial Rate Years, 17

with each year’s credit limited to the available balance and the final year’s credit 18

including any remaining balance, including earnings, so that the account is reduced to 19

zero, subject to the prospective reassignment and release provisions of Section 3.3.4. The 20

uncredited Termination Fee Balance is separately accounted for as a deferred liability and 21

is not itself a TRBAA Credit or Formula Rate input. The Covered Upgrade remains in 22

rate base. The terms governing security and termination are described in the testimony of 23

Mr. Hayes.
24

PDF page 450

9

Q.
WHAT ARE TRBAA CREDITS?
1
A. The CRA uses the term “TRBAA Credits” for the Forecast TRBAA Credit and the 2

amounts DesertLink records in the TRBA and credits to transmission customers through 3

the TRBAA: payments of Supplemental MTRC received from or on behalf of the 4

Eligible Customer (“Supplemental MTRC Receipts”), Applied Security Proceeds, Annual 5

Termination Fee Credits, and any credit required to prevent DesertLink from recovering 6

the same cost twice. The projected Supplemental MTRC, increased or reduced by any 7

prior-period true-up adjustment, together with any Annual Termination Fee Credit 8

scheduled for the following year, included in the TRBAA is the “Forecast TRBAA 9

Credit.” Consistent with the CRA, TRBAA Credits are credited solely through the 10

TRBAA and are not inputs to the Formula Rate. Qualifying Transmission Revenues are 11

not TRBAA Credits because they are already reflected in calculating the Supplemental 12

MTRC.
13
Q.
HOW ARE COVERED UPGRADES TREATED FOR PURPOSES OF RETURN
14
ON EQUITY AND COST CONTAINMENT?
15
A. Covered Upgrades will be subject to DesertLink’s Commission-accepted Formula Rate 16

and the return on equity (“ROE”) reflected in the effective Formula Rate. DesertLink’s 17

commitment to limit its ROE to 9.8%, inclusive of incentive ROE adders, was made in 18

connection with the competitive solicitation for the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project. 19

DesertLink is not proposing in this proceeding to extend that project-specific competitive 20

commitment to Covered Upgrades.
21
Covered Upgrade costs will be separately identified on Attachment 1a and reported as 22

“other costs” in the commitment work paper provided under Attachment A to the 23

Formula Rate Implementation Protocols. Those costs will not be subject to the Binding 24

PDF page 451

10

Cost Cap applicable to the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project.
1
DesertLink is not requesting a different ROE or any new incentive ROE adder in this 2

proceeding. DesertLink retains the right, subject to applicable Commission requirements, 3

to seek a different ROE or incentive treatment for Covered Upgrades in a future filing 4

under Section 205 of the Federal Power Act. Unless and until the Commission authorizes 5

different treatment, the ROE and any applicable incentive treatment reflected in the 6

effective Formula Rate will govern.
7
V. CREDITING CRA AMOUNTS TO CUSTOMERS THROUGH THE TRBAA
8
Q.
HOW WILL DESERTLINK CREDIT TRBAA CREDITS TO CUSTOMERS?
9
A. Through the TRBAA. Each October, DesertLink will include the Forecast TRBAA 10

Credit for the following calendar year in Cf. Under the CRA, the Forecast TRBAA Credit 11

equals the projected Supplemental MTRC, increased or reduced by any prior-period true- 12

up adjustment, which is the same amount DesertLink will invoice the Eligible Customer, 13

plus any Annual Termination Fee Credit scheduled for that year under Section 3.3.4. The 14

Forecast TRBAA Credit lowers the TRR effective January 1 and, through the TAC, the 15

transmission charges paid by all customers. During the year, the CAISO pays DesertLink 16

the lower TRR, and the Eligible Customer pays the Supplemental MTRC directly to 17

DesertLink. The TRBA records both. For these CRA amounts, a TRBA difference arises 18

when the amounts DesertLink records in the TRBA differ from the corresponding credits 19

reflected in CAISO payments, for example because of late payment or non-payment, the 20

application of security, a termination, or the timing of monthly installments. Any such 21

difference is included in the September 30 TRBA balance and returned to, or recovered 22

from, customers through Cr in the following TRBAA. Amounts later refunded or 23

reversed, and adjustments resulting from the resolution of a dispute under the CRA, are 24

PDF page 452

11

also recorded in the TRBA.
1
Q.
WHY IS THE TRBAA THE APPROPRIATE MECHANISM?
2
A. There are several reasons. First, the TRBAA already exists to credit customers with 3

revenue DesertLink receives outside the TAC, and the Commission and stakeholders 4

review it each year. Second, because the Supplemental MTRC is invoiced on a forecast 5

basis, including the Forecast TRBAA Credit in Cf gives customers the credit in the TRR 6

effective January 1, rather than a year later. Third, the TRBA ensures DesertLink collects 7

no more and no less than its Base TRR, so DesertLink retains none of the TRBAA 8

Credits. Fourth, crediting the revenue through the TRBAA keeps the full cost of each 9

Covered Upgrade in the Base TRR, consistent with the CAISO’s requirement that 10

facilities under its Operational Control be included in the TRR, while the TRBAA shows 11

the credit transparently and separately.
12
Q.
DOES USING THE TRBAA LIMIT THE ABILITY OF CUSTOMERS AND
13
OTHER INTERESTED PARTIES TO REVIEW OR CHALLENGE THESE
14
CREDITS?
15
A. No. DesertLink’s annual TRBAA filing is made under Section 205 of the Federal Power 16

Act. Each filing is noticed by the Commission, is open to intervention, comment, and 17

protest, and is subject to Commission review and acceptance. DesertLink will include in 18

each filing the calculations, work papers, and testimony supporting the TRBAA Credits, 19

so interested parties can review and challenge those amounts in that proceeding. In 20

addition, the inputs to the Formula Rate Template, including the Covered Upgrade plant 21

reported on Attachment 1a and the amounts removed on Attachment 12, Line 17a, are 22

subject to the existing information exchange, review, and challenge procedures of the 23

Formula Rate Implementation Protocols. As a result, every amount affected by the 24

proposal remains subject to review and challenge in one or both of these processes. 25

PDF page 453

12

Q.
WHAT CHANGES TO THE TO TARIFF ARE NEEDED TO IMPLEMENT THIS
1
APPROACH?
2
A. Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff currently provides for the TRBAA to flow Transmission 3

Revenue Credits through to transmission customers. The TO Tariff defines Transmission 4

Revenue Credits as proceeds received from, and charges imposed by, the CAISO, other 5

than proceeds that recover DesertLink’s TRR through the TAC. Because CRA-related 6

credits include amounts received directly from or on behalf of the Eligible Customer and 7

Annual Termination Fee Credits scheduled under Section 3.3.4, DesertLink proposes to 8

revise the definition of the TRBAA and Section 5.5 so that the TRBAA also flows 9

through to transmission customers all amounts a CRA requires to be credited through it. 10

The revisions add amounts recorded in the TRBA under a CRA to Cr, add any forecast 11

credit a CRA requires to Cf, and include amounts recorded in the TRBA under a CRA in 12

the TRBA principal balance used to calculate interest. The revisions also clarify that 13

Section 5.5 does not require the payment of interest between DesertLink and an Eligible 14

Customer, which is governed solely by the CRA. The definition of Transmission 15

Revenue Credits is unchanged.
16
Q.
HOW WILL TRBAA CREDITS BE REFLECTED IN THE ANNUAL TRBAA
17
FILING?
18
A. DesertLink will add the following lines to the TRBA and TRBAA calculation it files each 19

year, as shown in Exhibit No. DLK-205:
20
• Lines 7a through 7d record Supplemental MTRC Receipts, Applied Security 21

Proceeds, Annual Termination Fee Credits, and duplicate-recovery credits and 22

other adjustments, including reversals of amounts later refunded and adjustments 23

resulting from the resolution of disputes under the CRA. Applied Security 24

Proceeds used to pay a Termination Fee are held in the Termination Fee Account 25

PDF page 454

13

and credited through the Annual Termination Fee Credits on Line 7c, rather than 1

on Line 7b. These amounts are included in Net Payment on Line 8; and 2

• Cf on Line 18 is separated into other Transmission Revenue Credits (Line 18a) 3

and the Forecast TRBAA Credit (Line 18b), which equals the projected 4

Supplemental MTRC for the following calendar year, increased or reduced by any 5

prior-period true-up adjustment, plus any Annual Termination Fee Credit 6

scheduled for that year.
7
Because TRBAA Credits are included in Net Payment, any difference between the credit 8

reflected in CAISO payments and the TRBAA Credits recorded becomes part of the 9

TRBA balance and accrues interest in the same manner as other TRBA balances. Absent 10

TRBAA Credits, these lines are zero and the calculation is unchanged. 11

Q.
WHY DO TRBA BALANCES RELATED TO TRBAA CREDITS ACCRUE
12
INTEREST WHILE PRIOR-PERIOD TRUE-UP ADJUSTMENTS DO NOT?
13
A. Interest applies when DesertLink holds funds that belong to transmission customers, or 14

when transmission customers hold funds owed to DesertLink. A TRBA balance created 15

by a late payment, a non-payment before security is applied, or the timing of monthly 16

installments reflects an actual over- or under-recovery by DesertLink, so it accrues 17

interest like any other TRBA balance. A prior-period true-up adjustment is different. 18

When further Supplemental MTRC will be invoiced, the adjustment is added to the 19

Supplemental MTRC invoiced for a later Rate Year and to the Forecast TRBAA Credit 20

for that same Rate Year, so the matched adjustment does not itself create an over- or 21

under-recovery by DesertLink. Differences between the credit reflected in CAISO 22

payments and actual receipts or applied amounts remain subject to TRBA interest. When 23

no further Supplemental MTRC will be invoiced, Section 6.6 instead requires a separate 24

PDF page 455

14

invoice or refund, with the receipt or refund recorded in the TRBA when received or 1

paid. Consistent with Section 6.6 of the CRA and Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff, no interest 2

accrues on a prior-period true-up adjustment between DesertLink and the Eligible 3

Customer; interest on any resulting TRBA balance is calculated separately. 4

Q.
WILL DESERTLINK SUPPORT THESE AMOUNTS IN EACH ANNUAL
5
TRBAA FILING?
6
A. Yes. In each annual TRBAA filing, DesertLink will provide the TRBA and TRBAA 7

calculation substantially in the form of Exhibit No. DLK-205, together with work papers 8

supporting the Forecast TRBAA Credit and the TRBAA Credits recorded during the 9

TRBA year, and its witness will testify to those amounts. As provided in Section 6.8 of 10

the CRA, those work papers may present customer-specific information on an aggregated 11

basis or be submitted with a request for privileged treatment under 18 C.F.R. § 388.112. 12

Q.
ARE ANY CHANGES NEEDED TO APPENDIX I OF THE TO TARIFF?
13
A. No. Appendix I states that DesertLink’s TRR equals its Base TRR plus its TRBAA, and 14

that the TRBAA is computed in accordance with Section 5.5 of the TO Tariff and the 15

CAISO Tariff. TRBAA Credits are included in the TRBAA amount stated in Appendix I 16

each year, so no change to its terms is required.
17
VI. DESERTLINK’S PROPOSED FORMULA RATE TEMPLATE CHANGES
18
Q.
WHY IS ATTACHMENT 1A NEEDED?
19
A. The existing Formula Rate Template calculates the revenue requirement of the Harry 20

Allen to Eldorado Project using total transmission plant. To show the revenue 21

requirement of each Covered Upgrade, the Formula Rate Template must report plant for 22

each project separately. Attachment 1a provides that detail.
23

PDF page 456

15

Q.
PLEASE DESCRIBE ATTACHMENT 1A.
1
A. Attachment 1a has five sections, each with a line for each project. Additional project lines 2

may be added as Covered Upgrades are placed in service.
3
• Section 1 reports monthly transmission gross plant in service and its 13-month 4

average. The total ties to Attachment 4, Line 14, Column (b);
5
• Section 2 reports monthly transmission accumulated depreciation and its 13- 6

month average. The total ties to Attachment 4, Line 14, Column (h);
7
• Sections 3 and 4 report Construction Work in Progress (“CWIP”) and 8

unamortized abandoned plant by project, which tie to Attachment 4; and 9

• Section 5 calculates each project’s net plant (Line 1 – Line 2 + Line 3 + Line 4). 10

The total ties to Appendix III, page 2, Line 14 plus Lines 25 and 27. 11

Because the Attachment 1a totals tie to Attachment 4 and Appendix III, total plant and 12

the total revenue requirement are unchanged.
13
Q.
PLEASE DESCRIBE THE REVISIONS TO ATTACHMENT 1.
14
A. Each project line on Attachment 1 now draws its project name, gross plant including 15

CWIP (Column 3), net plant (Column 6), and depreciation and amortization expense 16

(Column 9) from Attachment 1a. Notes D, E, and F are revised to reference Attachment 17

1a. The allocation factors applied to each project are unchanged, so each project’s 18

revenue requirement reflects its share of total plant, and the project revenue requirements 19

sum to the total revenue requirement on Appendix III.
20
Q.
PLEASE DESCRIBE THE REVISIONS TO ATTACHMENT 12.
21
A. DesertLink proposes a new Line 17a, “Less: Revenue Credits included in the TRBAA,” 22

and revises Line 18 to subtract it. Consistent with Section 6.8 of the CRA, TRBAA 23

Credits are credited solely through the TRBAA and are not Formula Rate revenue credits. 24

PDF page 457

16

Line 17a is a safeguard: to the extent any TRBAA Credits are recorded in the revenue 1

accounts included on Line 15, Line 17a removes them, so they are credited to customers 2

once, through the TRBAA, and not also through the Formula Rate.
3
Q.
ARE THERE OTHER CHANGES TO THE FORMULA RATE TEMPLATE?
4
A. Yes. Attachment 1a has been added to the Table of Contents. There are no other changes. 5

Q.
ARE ANY CHANGES NEEDED TO THE FORMULA RATE
6
IMPLEMENTATION PROTOCOLS?
7
A. No. The Formula Rate Implementation Protocols already require DesertLink to support 8

each input to the Formula Rate Template that is not taken directly from the FERC Form 9

No. 1 and to explain material changes in revenue credits, which will include the amounts 10

on Attachment 12, Line 17a. The existing posting, review, challenge, and true-up 11

procedures apply to Attachment 1a without change. TRBAA Credits are reviewed in 12

DesertLink’s annual TRBAA filing under Section 205 of the Federal Power Act, as I 13

described above.
14
VII. NATIVE AND ILLUSTRATIVE EXHIBITS
15
Q.
PLEASE DESCRIBE EXHIBIT NO. DLK-203.
16
A. Exhibit No. DLK-203 is the revised Formula Rate Template in native Excel format with 17

all formulas and links intact, including new Attachment 1a. It is not populated with 18

DesertLink or customer data. Reviewers can enter values in the input cells and observe 19

the formula mechanics.
20
Q.
PLEASE DESCRIBE EXHIBIT NO. DLK-204.
21
A. Exhibit No. DLK-204 is the revised Formula Rate Template populated with hypothetical 22

data for the 2030 Rate Year to illustrate the treatment of a Covered Upgrade. The 23

example includes the Harry Allen to Eldorado Project and one $60 million Covered 24

PDF page 458

17

Upgrade placed in service January 1, 2030, consistent with the illustrative CRA 1

worksheet sponsored by Mr. Hayes (Exhibit No. DLK-101). In that worksheet, the 2

Covered Upgrade has an Annual MTRC of $7,292,700 and projected Qualifying 3

Transmission Revenues of $3,363,840, for a Supplemental MTRC of $3,928,860. In 4

Exhibit No. DLK-204:
5
• Because the Covered Upgrade is placed in service January 1, 2030, it is not 6

included in the December 2029 plant balance, and its 13-month average gross 7

plant is $55.38 million. The Covered Upgrade’s revenue requirement on 8

Attachment 1 is $7.08 million and the total Base TRR is $23.85 million; 9

• TRBAA Credits of $3,928,860 are assumed to be recorded in a revenue account 10

reported on Attachment 12, Line 14, and are removed on Line 17a, so they do not 11

reduce the Base TRR; without Line 17a, the Base TRR would be $19.92 million 12

and the amounts would be credited twice; and
13
• The Covered Upgrade’s first-year Formula Rate revenue requirement of $7.08 14

million differs from its Annual MTRC of $7.29 million because the two are 15

calculated separately and on different bases. The Annual MTRC is calculated 16

under Schedule 5 of the CRA and, once finalized, is fixed subject to the 17

adjustments expressly permitted by Section 6.3.1. Its levelized calculation uses a 18

twenty-year MTRC Term to recover the allocated capital cost and the return, 19

taxes, and fixed expenses reflected in Schedule 5. The Formula Rate revenue 20

requirement is recalculated each year using 13-month average balances and book 21

depreciation rates, so this January 1 in-service example includes a zero December 22

2029 plant balance in the 13-month average even though the upgrade is in service 23

PDF page 459

18

for all of 2030. All else equal, the capital-related revenue requirement declines as 1

the plant depreciates. The difference does not affect DesertLink’s revenue: the 2

Covered Upgrade is recovered through the Base TRR, and all TRBAA Credits are 3

returned to customers through the TRBAA.

The illustrative data are hypothetical and are not DesertLink or customer data. 5

Q.
PLEASE DESCRIBE EXHIBIT NO. DLK-205.
6
A. Exhibit No. DLK-205 illustrates the TRBA and TRBAA calculation for two consecutive 7

TRBA years ending September 30, 2030 and 2031, using the Supplemental MTRC from 8

Exhibit No. DLK-101 and the Base TRR from Exhibit No. DLK-204. For trade months 9

before January 2030, the example uses a Base TRR that excludes the Covered Upgrade; 10

the 2030 Base TRR is then held constant so the TRBA balances shown result only from 11

the TRBAA Credits. Two years are shown because the TRBAA operates on a lag: a 12

credit included in Cf in one filing is compared to actual receipts in the following TRBA 13

year, and any difference is returned in the filing after that.
14
• In the TRBA year ending September 30, 2030, the annual $3,928,860 credit takes 15

effect January 1, 2030, and Supplemental MTRC Receipts replace the reduction 16

in CAISO payments.  Only a small timing difference remains, because the 17

Supplemental MTRC is invoiced in equal monthly installments while CAISO 18

payments reflect the days in each month.  The resulting TRBA balance of $3,883 19

and interest of $202 are returned to customers, and the TRBAA effective January 20

1, 2031 is a credit of $3,932,944.
21
• In the TRBA year ending September 30, 2031, the example assumes two 22

hypothetical events.  First, the 2030 Reconciliation Statement shows that the 23

19

Eligible Customer was under-billed by $100,000.  Under the CRA, that prior- 1

period true-up adjustment is added to the Supplemental MTRC invoiced for 2032 2

and to the 2032 Forecast TRBAA Credit on Line 18b of $4,028,860, so it does not 3

create a TRBA balance and carries no interest.  Second, the Eligible Customer 4

VIII. CONCLUSION
11
Q.
WHY ARE THE PROPOSED REVISIONS JUST AND REASONABLE?
12
A. The revisions implement the Commission’s direction that large load payments be credited 13

toward transmission owners’ revenue requirements, using DesertLink’s existing TRBAA 14

mechanism. Each Eligible Customer pays at least its committed Annual MTRC for each 15

Covered Upgrade, and TRBAA Credits reduce the TRR paid by all customers through the 16

TAC. DesertLink retains none of the TRBAA Credits, and Attachment 12, Line 17a 17

ensures they are credited only once. The cost of service inputs and methods are 18

unchanged, and Attachment 1a ties to the existing plant totals. The existing Formula Rate 19

review procedures and DesertLink’s annual TRBAA filing provide full transparency for 20

the new calculations.
21
Q.
DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR TESTIMONY?
22
A. Yes.

DA = Direct Assignment; GP = Gross Plant Allocator (page 2, line 5); N/A = Not Applicable; NP = Net Plant Allocator (page 2, line 17); TP = Transmission Plant Allocator (page 4, line 5); WS = Wage and Salary Allocator (page 4, line 11). X

The revenues credited on page 1, lines 2-6, shall include only the amounts received by DesertLink for service rendered using facilities for which recovery is provided under this tariff. They do not include revenues associated with FERC annual charges, gross receipts taxes, or facilities not included in this template (e.g., direct assignment facilities and GSUs) which are not recovered under this Rate Formula Template.

Accumulated deferred income tax amounts associated with asset or liability accounts excluded from rate base (such as ADIT related to asset retirement obligations and certain tax-related regulatory assets or liabilities) do not affect rate base.  Balance of Account 255 will be reduced by prior flow throughs and excluded if the utility chooses to utilize amortization of tax credits against taxable income. Account 281 is not allocated to Transmission.

Recovery of Regulatory Asset permitted only for pre-commercial and formation expenses as authorized by the Commission. Recovery of any other regulatory assets requires authorization from the Commission. A carrying charge equal to the AFUDC rate will be applied to the Regulatory Asset prior to the rate year when costs are first recovered.

Cash Working Capital assigned to transmission is one-eighth of O&M allocated to transmission at page 3, line 17, column 5 minus amortization of Regulatory Asset at page 3, line 14, column 5.  Prepayments are the electric related prepayments booked to Account No. 165 and reported on page 111, line 57 in the Form 1.

The FERC's annual charges for the year assessed the Transmission Owner for service under this tariff.  To the extent the charges are separately identified on the FERC Form 1, page 350, column 1, the line number will be added to the source in Column 2 for reference.  Line item references can change from year to year.  Items not specifically identified in the FERC Form 1, page 350 will be obtained from Company books and records.

Includes only FICA, unemployment, highway, property, gross receipts, and other assessments charged in the current year.  Taxes related to income are excluded.  Enter the line number on page 262-63 upon which each item is identified.  To the extent individual types of taxes are separately identified on the FERC Form 1, page 262, column a, the line number will be added to the source in Column 2 for reference.  Line item references can change from year to year.  Items not specifically identified in the FERC Form 1, page 262-63 will be obtained from Company books and records.

FIT is the weighted average Federal income tax rate and SIT is the weighted average State income tax rate, both from Attachment 7, and p is the "the percentage of federal income tax deductible for state income taxes". A utility that elected to utilize amortization of tax credits against taxable income, rather than book tax credits to Account No. 255 and reduce rate base, must reduce its income tax expense by the amount of the Amortized Investment Tax Credit (Form 1, 266.8.f) multiplied by (1/1-T) (page 3, line 26). Excess Deferred Income Taxes reduce income tax expense by the amount of the expense multiplied by (1/(1-T)).

The Tax Effect of Permanent Differences captures the differences in the income taxes due under the Federal and State calculations and the income taxes calculated in Appendix III that are not the result of a timing difference. Tax Effect equals Permanent Differences multiplied by T.

The cost of debt will be determined based on the financing in place during each stage of project development. Before debt is obtained, a proxy interest rate which will be supported in the original Section 205 filing will be used. This rate is provided on Attachment 8 line 36. If construction debt (wherein principal is drawn down over time) is issued, the rate plus an amortization of fees projected to be incurred on the construction debt during the rate year will be the cost of debt. This construction debt rate (inclusive of fees) will be reset and trued-up every year using the method on Attachment 9 for multi-year construction projects. Once non-construction debt is obtained, the actual interest rate and fees on the debt in place at the end of the year such non- construction debt is obtained will become the cost of debt. In the first full year after non-construction debt is obtained, the cost of debt will be the actual cost of debt determined using the method on Attachment 5. A h

Calculate rate base using 13 month average balance, except ADIT.  The calculation of ADIT in the annual true-up calculation will use the beginning-of-year and end-of-year balances, and will be performed in accordance with IRS regulation Section 1.167(l)- 1(h)(6).  The calculation of ADIT in the annual projection will be performed in accordance with IRS Regulation Section 1.167(l)-1(h)(6).

Removes dollar amount of transmission plant to be included in the development of OATT ancillary services rates and generation step-up facilities, which are deemed to be included in OATT ancillary services. For these purposes, generation step-up facilities are those facilities at a generator substation on which there is no through-flow when the generator is shut down.

Upon enactment of changes in tax law, ADIT balances are re-measured and adjusted in the Company’s books of account, resulting in excess or deficient accumulated deferred income tax assets and liabilities.  Excess or deficient ADIT attributable to timing differences between the amounts of expenses or revenues recognized for income tax purposes and amounts of expenses or revenues recognized for ratemaking purposes as well as subsequent recoverable or refundable amortization of such amounts will be based upon Company records and be calculated and recorded in accordance with ASC 740 and any applicable normalization requirements of the taxing jurisdiction.  The Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Tax Adjustment (page 3, line 44) is computed by multiplying each component of Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Taxes (page 3, line 40) by the applicable tax gross-up factor.  For each re-measurement of ADIT, the amounts entered as the Deficient or (Excess) Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes component of ADJUSTMENTS TO RATE BASE (page 2, line 22a) or as the Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Tax Adjustment component of INCOME TAXES (page 3, line 44) will be supported by Attachment 13 (Deficient or Excess Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) providing the balance for each taxing jurisdiction at the beginning and end of the year, amortization for the year, calculation of the gross-up to the revenue requirement level and any other information required to support compliance with any applicable normalization requirements.

General and Intangible Depreciation and Amortization Expense includes all expenses (except depreciation and armortization of G&I Asset Retirement Obligations) not directly associated with a project, which is entered on page 3 , column 9.

Project Gross Plant is the total capital investment including CWIP for the project calculated from Company books and records in the same method as the gross plant value in line 1.  This value includes subsequent capital investments required to maintain the facilities to their original capabilities.  Refer to Attachment 1a for detail.

Project Depreciation Expense is the actual value booked for the project (excluding General and Intangible depreciation) at Appendix III, page 3, line 19, plus amortization of Abandoned Plant at Appendix III, page 3, line 21.  For each project on Attachment 1a, Depreciation Expense is Attachment 1a, Line 2, Column (15) minus Column (3), and Amortization of Abandoned Plant is the difference between Columns (3) and (15) on Attachment 1a, Line 4. The Competitive Concession is the reduction in revenue, if any, that the company agreed to, for instance, to be selected to build facilities as the result of a competitive process and equals the amount by which the  annual revenue requirement is reduced from the ceiling rate.

This Attachment 3 is used to calculate the annual formula rate true-up. Any projects for which the RTO requires a true-up on an individual project basis, as shown on Attachment 1, will be computed separately. The remainder of the revenue requirement will also be trued up. The utility will individually enter the projected true-up year revenue requirements in Column C. A percentage of total will be calculated in Column D. Actual revenue received during the true-up year is entered into Column E, line 2 and allocated using the Column D percentage. The utility will prepare this formula rate template with the actual inputs for the true-up year, with the resulting revenue requirement for each line being separately entered in Column F.  In Col. G, Col. F is subtracted from Col. E to calculate the true-up adjustment. Interest on the true-up is computed in Column H. Any adjustments to prior period true-ups are entered in Col.

I.  Col. J computes the total true-up as the sum of Col. G, H and I.

Recovery of CWIP in rate base must be approved by FERC.  Lines 29-41 of page 2 provide a reconciliation of the Company's total CWIP to the CWIP allowed in rate base. The annual report filed pursuant to the Protocols will include for each project under construction (i) the CWIP balance eligible for inclusion in rate base; (ii) the CWIP balance ineligible for inclusion in rate base; and (iii) a demonstration that AFUDC is only applied to the CWIP balance that is not included in rate base The annual report will also describe the reconciliation prepared on this Attachment

Recovery of a Regulatory Asset is permitted only for pre-commercial and formation expenses, and is subject to FERC approval before the amortization of the Regulatory Asset can be included in rates. Recovery of any other regulatory assets requires authorization from the Commission.

The Formula Rate shall include a credit to rate base for all unfunded reserves (funds collected from customers that (1) have not been set aside in a trust, escrow or restricted account; (2) whose balance are collected from customers through cost accruals to accounts that are recovered under the Formula Rate; and (3) exclude the portion of any balance offset by a balance sheet ac count (see Note H)).  Each unfunded reserve will be included on lines 42 above. The allocator in Col. (g) will be the same allocator used in the formula for the cost accruals to the account that is recovered under the Formula Rate.  Since reserves can be created by creating an offsetting balance sheet account, rather than through cost accruals, the amount to be deducted from rate base should exclude the portion offset by another balance sheet account. Not all unfunded reserves are created only from contributions from customers. Many are created by creating an offsetting liability in whole or in part.  Column (f) ensures only the portion of the unfunded reserve contributed by the customer (and not created by an offsetting liability) is a reduction to rate base.

The inputs in Column (f) are the percentage of the unfunded reserve that was created by an offsetting liability. The percentage shown in Column (f) is then equal to the percentage that customers have contributed to the unfunded reserve.

In the case of tax law changes with an effective date(s) after the beginning of the test period, the impact of a timing difference on current tax expense or benefit differs from the impact on ADIT.  For example, in the case of a deductible timing difference originating in a tax year with a higher enacted tax rate than will apply when the difference will reverse, the current tax benefit will exceed the deferred tax expense.  In this situation, the adjustment computed below to recoverable income tax expense is made in order to avoid over-recovering income tax expense in the current test period due to the excess of current tax benefit over deferred tax expense (computed based on the estimated amount of the future tax liability) with respect to a given timing difference.  The adjustment to recoverable tax expense during the test period in which a timing difference originates mitigates the need for refund of a regulatory liability for excess deferred taxes in a future period (or, as applicable, the need for recovery of a regulatory asset for deficient deferred taxes in a future period).  Amounts in column (i) are reported in the Income Tax Allowance Adjustment Mechanism - Summary on this worksheet.

Note 2 - Explanation of how ADIT accounts are re-measured upon a change in income tax law
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted (re-measured) for the effect of the changes in tax law (including tax rates) in the period that the change is enacted.  Adjustments are recorded in the appropriate deferred tax balance sheet accounts (Accounts 190, 281, 282 and 283) based on the nature of the temporary difference and the related classification requirements of the accounts.   If as a result of action or expected action by a regulator, it is probable that the future increase or decrease in taxes payable due to the change in tax law or rates will be recovered from or returned to customers through future rates, a regulatory asset or liability is recognized in Account 182.3 (Other Regulatory Assets), or Account 254 (Other Regulatory Liabilities), as appropriate, for that probable future revenue or reduction in future revenue.  Re-measurements of deferred tax balance sheet accounts may also result in re-measurements of tax-related regulatory assets or liabilities that had been recorded prior to the change in tax law.  If it is not probable that the future increase or decrease in taxes payable due to the change in tax law or rates will be recovered from or returned to customers through future rates, tax expense is recognized in Account 410.2 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes, Other Income or Deductions) or tax benefit is recognized in Account 411.2 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes-Credit, Other Income or Deductions), as appropriate.

Note 3 - [Complete to support information above.]
Note 4 - The amortization of the deficient or excess ADIT reducing Account 254 (Other Regulatory Liabilities) is recorded with credits to Account 411.1 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes – Credit, Utility Operating Income) and to Account 190 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) or Account 283 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes—Other), as appropriate, in accordance with the Commission’s Accounting for Income Taxes Guidance.  The amortization of the deficient or excess ADIT reducing Account 182.3 (Other Regulatory Assets) is recorded with debits to Account 410.1 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes, Utility Operating Income) and to Account 190 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) or Account 283 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes—Other), as appropriate, in accordance with the Commission’s Accounting for Income Taxes Guidance. This activity is summarized in the table "Income Tax Allowance Mechanism - Projected" or the table "Income Tax Allowance Mechanism - Actual," as appropriate.  The annual amortization in the tables above reflects tax gross-up and is stated at the revenue requirement level.

Note 5 - [Complete to support information above.]
Note 6 -  The worksheet indicates whether each excess or deficient ADIT amounts are protected (i.e., subject to normalization rules of a taxing jurisdiction) or unprotected (i.e., not subject to normalization rules of a taxing jurisdiction).  To the extent that normalization requirements apply to ADIT remeasurements, additional computations (e.g., proration of excess deferred tax activity related to future test periods) may be necessary.

Note 3 -
Note 4  -  Column J is the difference between actual monthly and projected monthly activity (Column I minus Column C).  Specifically, if projected and actual activity are both positive, a negative in Column J represents over-projection (i.e., the amount of projected activity that did not occur) and a positive in Column J represents under-projection (i.e., the excess of actual activity over projected activity). If projected and actual activity are both negative, a negative in Column J represents under-projection (i.e., the excess of actual activity over projected activity) and a positive in Column J represents over-projection (i.e., the amount of projected activity that did not occur).

Note 5  -  Column K preserves the effects of excess ADIT proration from the projected revenue requirement when actual monthly excess ADIT activity and projected monthly excess ADIT activity are either both increases or decreases.  Specifically, if Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was over-projected, enter Column G x [Column I / Column C].  If Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was under-projected, enter the amount from Column G and complete Column L).  In other situations, enter zero.

Note 6  -  Column L applies when (1) Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was under-projected AND (2) actual monthly and projected monthly activity are either both increases or both decreases.  Enter 50 percent of the amount from Column J.  In other situations, enter zero.  The excess ADIT activity in column L is multiplied by 50 percent to reflect averaging of rate base to the extent that the proration requirement has not been applied to a portion of the monthly excess ADIT activity.

Note 7  -  Column M applies when (1) projected monthly activity was an increase while actual monthly activity was a decrease OR (2) projected monthly activity was a decrease while actual monthly activity was an increase.  Enter 50 percent of the amount of actual monthly activity (Column I).  In other situations, enter zero.  The excess ADIT activity in column M is multiplied by 50 percent to reflect averaging of rate base to the extent that the proration requirement has not been applied to a portion of the monthly excess ADIT activity.

Note 8  -  Column N is computed by adding the balance at the end of the prior month to EITHER (1) the sum of prorated monthly excess ADIT activity, if any, from Column K and the portion of monthly excess ADIT activity, if any, from Column L OR (2) the portion of monthly excess ADIT activity in Column M.

The ratemaking treatment of each item in terms of whether it is subject to the normalization requirements (i.e., P or "protected") or not subject to the normalization requirements (i.e., U or "unprotected") and included in rate base or not (i.e., RB or non-RB) is indicated in column (b).  The balances are measured at the composite tax rate in effect immediately before effective date of the change in tax law and remeasured immediately after the change in tax law.  Each set of balances includes the appropriate income tax rates and tax gross-up factors (as computed in the specific note for this tax law change in Att. 13).  The journal entry to record the remeasurements (Line 16) is based on the differences in balances of accounts recorded prior to the change in law (columns (d)-(h)) and activity in other accounts resulting from the remeasurement (columns (i)-(n)).  The remeasurement entry is also included in Att. 13.  The accounting is further described in Att. 13, Note 2. This worksheet will be included in support of the revenue requirement computation until the excess or deficient ADIT is fully amortized.  A similar worksheet will be used for subsequent changes in tax law resulting in re-measurement of ADIT.

DA = Direct Assignment; GP = Gross Plant Allocator (page 2, line 5); N/A = Not Applicable; NP = Net Plant Allocator (page 2, line 17); TP = Transmission Plant Allocator (page 4, line 5); WS = Wage and Salary Allocator (page 4, line 11). X

The revenues credited on page 1, lines 2-6, shall include only the amounts received by DesertLink for service rendered using facilities for which recovery is provided under this tariff. They do not include revenues associated with FERC annual charges, gross receipts taxes, or facilities not included in this template (e.g., direct assignment facilities and GSUs) which are not recovered under this Rate Formula Template.

Accumulated deferred income tax amounts associated with asset or liability accounts excluded from rate base (such as ADIT related to asset retirement obligations and certain tax-related regulatory assets or liabilities) do not affect rate base.  Balance of Account 255 will be reduced by prior flow throughs and excluded if the utility chooses to utilize amortization of tax credits against taxable income. Account 281 is not allocated to Transmission.

Recovery of Regulatory Asset permitted only for pre-commercial and formation expenses as authorized by the Commission. Recovery of any other regulatory assets requires authorization from the Commission. A carrying charge equal to the AFUDC rate will be applied to the Regulatory Asset prior to the rate year when costs are first recovered.

Cash Working Capital assigned to transmission is one-eighth of O&M allocated to transmission at page 3, line 17, column 5 minus amortization of Regulatory Asset at page 3, line 14, column 5.  Prepayments are the electric related prepayments booked to Account No. 165 and reported on page 111, line 57 in the Form 1.

The FERC's annual charges for the year assessed the Transmission Owner for service under this tariff.  To the extent the charges are separately identified on the FERC Form 1, page 350, column 1, the line number will be added to the source in Column 2 for reference.  Line item references can change from year to year.  Items not specifically identified in the FERC Form 1, page 350 will be obtained from Company books and records.

Includes only FICA, unemployment, highway, property, gross receipts, and other assessments charged in the current year.  Taxes related to income are excluded.  Enter the line number on page 262-63 upon which each item is identified.  To the extent individual types of taxes are separately identified on the FERC Form 1, page 262, column a, the line number will be added to the source in Column 2 for reference.  Line item references can change from year to year.  Items not specifically identified in the FERC Form 1, page 262-63 will be obtained from Company books and records.

FIT is the weighted average Federal income tax rate and SIT is the weighted average State income tax rate, both from Attachment 7, and p is the "the percentage of federal income tax deductible for state income taxes". A utility that elected to utilize amortization of tax credits against taxable income, rather than book tax credits to Account No. 255 and reduce rate base, must reduce its income tax expense by the amount of the Amortized Investment Tax Credit (Form 1, 266.8.f) multiplied by (1/1-T) (page 3, line 26). Excess Deferred Income Taxes reduce income tax expense by the amount of the expense multiplied by (1/(1-T)).

The Tax Effect of Permanent Differences captures the differences in the income taxes due under the Federal and State calculations and the income taxes calculated in Appendix III that are not the result of a timing difference. Tax Effect equals Permanent Differences multiplied by T.

The cost of debt will be determined based on the financing in place during each stage of project development. Before debt is obtained, a proxy interest rate which will be supported in the original Section 205 filing will be used. This rate is provided on Attachment 8 line 36. If construction debt (wherein principal is drawn down over time) is issued, the rate plus an amortization of fees projected to be incurred on the construction debt during the rate year will be the cost of debt. This construction debt rate (inclusive of fees) will be reset and trued-up every year using the method on Attachment 9 for multi-year construction projects. Once non-construction debt is obtained, the actual interest rate and fees on the debt in place at the end of the year such non- construction debt is obtained will become the cost of debt. In the first full year after non-construction debt is obtained, the cost of debt will be the actual cost of debt determined using the method on Attachment 5. A h

Calculate rate base using 13 month average balance, except ADIT.  The calculation of ADIT in the annual true-up calculation will use the beginning-of-year and end-of-year balances, and will be performed in accordance with IRS regulation Section 1.167(l)- 1(h)(6).  The calculation of ADIT in the annual projection will be performed in accordance with IRS Regulation Section 1.167(l)-1(h)(6).

Removes dollar amount of transmission plant to be included in the development of OATT ancillary services rates and generation step-up facilities, which are deemed to be included in OATT ancillary services. For these purposes, generation step-up facilities are those facilities at a generator substation on which there is no through-flow when the generator is shut down.

Upon enactment of changes in tax law, ADIT balances are re-measured and adjusted in the Company’s books of account, resulting in excess or deficient accumulated deferred income tax assets and liabilities.  Excess or deficient ADIT attributable to timing differences between the amounts of expenses or revenues recognized for income tax purposes and amounts of expenses or revenues recognized for ratemaking purposes as well as subsequent recoverable or refundable amortization of such amounts will be based upon Company records and be calculated and recorded in accordance with ASC 740 and any applicable normalization requirements of the taxing jurisdiction.  The Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Tax Adjustment (page 3, line 44) is computed by multiplying each component of Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Taxes (page 3, line 40) by the applicable tax gross-up factor.  For each re-measurement of ADIT, the amounts entered as the Deficient or (Excess) Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes component of ADJUSTMENTS TO RATE BASE (page 2, line 22a) or as the Deficient or (Excess) Deferred Income Tax Adjustment component of INCOME TAXES (page 3, line 44) will be supported by Attachment 13 (Deficient or Excess Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) providing the balance for each taxing jurisdiction at the beginning and end of the year, amortization for the year, calculation of the gross-up to the revenue requirement level and any other information required to support compliance with any applicable normalization requirements.

General and Intangible Depreciation and Amortization Expense includes all expenses (except depreciation and armortization of G&I Asset Retirement Obligations) not directly associated with a project, which is entered on page 3 , column 9.

Project Gross Plant is the total capital investment including CWIP for the project calculated from Company books and records in the same method as the gross plant value in line 1.  This value includes subsequent capital investments required to maintain the facilities to their original capabilities.  Refer to Attachment 1a for detail.

Project Net Plant is the Project Gross Plant Identified in Column 3 less the associated Accumulated Depreciation plus CWIP in rate base if applicable and Unamortized Abandoned Plant.  Refer to Attachment 1a for detail. Project Depreciation Expense is the actual value booked for the project (excluding General and Intangible depreciation) at Appendix III, page 3, line 19, plus amortization of Abandoned Plant at Appendix III, page 3, line 21.  For each project on Attachment 1a, Depreciation Expense is Attachment 1a, Line 2, Column (15) minus Column (3), and Amortization of Abandoned Plant is the difference between Columns (3) and (15) on Attachment 1a, Line 4. The Competitive Concession is the reduction in revenue, if any, that the company agreed to, for instance, to be selected to build facilities as the result of a competitive process and equals the amount by which the  annual revenue requirement is reduced from the ceiling rate.

This Attachment 3 is used to calculate the annual formula rate true-up. Any projects for which the RTO requires a true-up on an individual project basis, as shown on Attachment 1, will be computed separately. The remainder of the revenue requirement will also be trued up. The utility will individually enter the projected true-up year revenue requirements in Column C. The utility will prepare this formula rate template with the actual inputs for the true-up year, with the resulting revenue requirement for each line being separately entered in Column F.  In Col. G, Col. F is subtracted from Col. E to calculate the true-up adjustment. Interest on the true-up is computed in Column H. Any adjustments to prior period true-ups are entered in Col.

I.  Col. J computes the total true-up as the sum of Col. G, H and I.

Recovery of CWIP in rate base must be approved by FERC.  Lines 29-41 of page 2 provide a reconciliation of the Company's total CWIP to the CWIP allowed in rate base. The annual report filed pursuant to the Protocols will include for each project under construction (i) the CWIP balance eligible for inclusion in rate base; (ii) the CWIP balance ineligible for inclusion in rate base; and (iii) a demonstration that AFUDC is only applied to the CWIP balance that is not included in rate base The annual report will also describe the reconciliation prepared on this Attachment

Recovery of a Regulatory Asset is permitted only for pre-commercial and formation expenses, and is subject to FERC approval before the amortization of the Regulatory Asset can be included in rates. Recovery of any other regulatory assets requires authorization from the Commission.

The Formula Rate shall include a credit to rate base for all unfunded reserves (funds collected from customers that (1) have not been set aside in a trust, escrow or restricted account; (2) whose balance are collected from customers through cost accruals to accounts that are recovered under the Formula Rate; and (3) exclude the portion of any balance offset by a balance sheet ac count (see Note H)).  Each unfunded reserve will be included on lines 42 above. The allocator in Col. (g) will be the same allocator used in the formula for the cost accruals to the account that is recovered under the Formula Rate.  Since reserves can be created by creating an offsetting balance sheet account, rather than through cost accruals, the amount to be deducted from rate base should exclude the portion offset by another balance sheet account. Not all unfunded reserves are created only from contributions from customers. Many are created by creating an offsetting liability in whole or in part.  Column (f) ensures only the portion of the unfunded reserve contributed by the customer (and not created by an offsetting liability) is a reduction to rate base.

The inputs in Column (f) are the percentage of the unfunded reserve that was created by an offsetting liability. The percentage shown in Column (f) is then equal to the percentage that customers have contributed to the unfunded reserve.

In the case of tax law changes with an effective date(s) after the beginning of the test period, the impact of a timing difference on current tax expense or benefit differs from the impact on ADIT.  For example, in the case of a deductible timing difference originating in a tax year with a higher enacted tax rate than will apply when the difference will reverse, the current tax benefit will exceed the deferred tax expense.  In this situation, the adjustment computed below to recoverable income tax expense is made in order to avoid over-recovering income tax expense in the current test period due to the excess of current tax benefit over deferred tax expense (computed based on the estimated amount of the future tax liability) with respect to a given timing difference.  The adjustment to recoverable tax expense during the test period in which a timing difference originates mitigates the need for refund of a regulatory liability for excess deferred taxes in a future period (or, as applicable, the need for recovery of a regulatory asset for deficient deferred taxes in a future period).  Amounts in column (i) are reported in the Income Tax Allowance Adjustment Mechanism - Summary on this worksheet.

Note 2 - Explanation of how ADIT accounts are re-measured upon a change in income tax law
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted (re-measured) for the effect of the changes in tax law (including tax rates) in the period that the change is enacted.  Adjustments are recorded in the appropriate deferred tax balance sheet accounts (Accounts 190, 281, 282 and 283) based on the nature of the temporary difference and the related classification requirements of the accounts.   If as a result of action or expected action by a regulator, it is probable that the future increase or decrease in taxes payable due to the change in tax law or rates will be recovered from or returned to customers through future rates, a regulatory asset or liability is recognized in Account 182.3 (Other Regulatory Assets), or Account 254 (Other Regulatory Liabilities), as appropriate, for that probable future revenue or reduction in future revenue.  Re-measurements of deferred tax balance sheet accounts may also result in re-measurements of tax-related regulatory assets or liabilities that had been recorded prior to the change in tax law.  If it is not probable that the future increase or decrease in taxes payable due to the change in tax law or rates will be recovered from or returned to customers through future rates, tax expense is recognized in Account 410.2 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes, Other Income or Deductions) or tax benefit is recognized in Account 411.2 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes-Credit, Other Income or Deductions), as appropriate.

Note 3 - [Complete to support information above.]
Note 4 - The amortization of the deficient or excess ADIT reducing Account 254 (Other Regulatory Liabilities) is recorded with credits to Account 411.1 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes – Credit, Utility Operating Income) and to Account 190 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) or Account 283 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes—Other), as appropriate, in accordance with the Commission’s Accounting for Income Taxes Guidance.  The amortization of the deficient or excess ADIT reducing Account 182.3 (Other Regulatory Assets) is recorded with debits to Account 410.1 (Provision for Deferred Income Taxes, Utility Operating Income) and to Account 190 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes) or Account 283 (Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes—Other), as appropriate, in accordance with the Commission’s Accounting for Income Taxes Guidance. This activity is summarized in the table "Income Tax Allowance Mechanism - Projected" or the table "Income Tax Allowance Mechanism - Actual," as appropriate.  The annual amortization in the tables above reflects tax gross-up and is stated at the revenue requirement level.

Note 5 - [Complete to support information above.]
Note 6 -  The worksheet indicates whether each excess or deficient ADIT amounts are protected (i.e., subject to normalization rules of a taxing jurisdiction) or unprotected (i.e., not subject to normalization rules of a taxing jurisdiction).  To the extent that normalization requirements apply to ADIT remeasurements, additional computations (e.g., proration of excess deferred tax activity related to future test periods) may be necessary.

Note 3 -
Note 4  -  Column J is the difference between actual monthly and projected monthly activity (Column I minus Column C).  Specifically, if projected and actual activity are both positive, a negative in Column J represents over-projection (i.e., the amount of projected activity that did not occur) and a positive in Column J represents under-projection (i.e., the excess of actual activity over projected activity). If projected and actual activity are both negative, a negative in Column J represents under-projection (i.e., the excess of actual activity over projected activity) and a positive in Column J represents over-projection (i.e., the amount of projected activity that did not occur).

Note 5  -  Column K preserves the effects of excess ADIT proration from the projected revenue requirement when actual monthly excess ADIT activity and projected monthly excess ADIT activity are either both increases or decreases.  Specifically, if Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was over-projected, enter Column G x [Column I / Column C].  If Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was under-projected, enter the amount from Column G and complete Column L).  In other situations, enter zero.

Note 6  -  Column L applies when (1) Column J indicates that excess ADIT activity was under-projected AND (2) actual monthly and projected monthly activity are either both increases or both decreases.  Enter 50 percent of the amount from Column J.  In other situations, enter zero.  The excess ADIT activity in column L is multiplied by 50 percent to reflect averaging of rate base to the extent that the proration requirement has not been applied to a portion of the monthly excess ADIT activity.

Note 7  -  Column M applies when (1) projected monthly activity was an increase while actual monthly activity was a decrease OR (2) projected monthly activity was a decrease while actual monthly activity was an increase.  Enter 50 percent of the amount of actual monthly activity (Column I).  In other situations, enter zero.  The excess ADIT activity in column M is multiplied by 50 percent to reflect averaging of rate base to the extent that the proration requirement has not been applied to a portion of the monthly excess ADIT activity.

Note 8  -  Column N is computed by adding the balance at the end of the prior month to EITHER (1) the sum of prorated monthly excess ADIT activity, if any, from Column K and the portion of monthly excess ADIT activity, if any, from Column L OR (2) the portion of monthly excess ADIT activity in Column M.

The ratemaking treatment of each item in terms of whether it is subject to the normalization requirements (i.e., P or "protected") or not subject to the normalization requirements (i.e., U or "unprotected") and included in rate base or not (i.e., RB or non-RB) is indicated in column (b).  The balances are measured at the composite tax rate in effect immediately before effective date of the change in tax law and remeasured immediately after the change in tax law.  Each set of balances includes the appropriate income tax rates and tax gross-up factors (as computed in the specific note for this tax law change in Att. 13).  The journal entry to record the remeasurements (Line 16) is based on the differences in balances of accounts recorded prior to the change in law (columns (d)-(h)) and activity in other accounts resulting from the remeasurement (columns (i)-(n)).  The remeasurement entry is also included in Att. 13.  The accounting is further described in Att. 13, Note 2. This worksheet will be included in support of the revenue requirement computation until the excess or deficient ADIT is fully amortized.  A similar worksheet will be used for subsequent changes in tax law resulting in re-measurement of ADIT.
